entries.title: Degree-at-most-four Meng--Yang graph obstruction
entries.scope: Let y3=R(x1,x2,y1,y2) be an arbitrary polynomial graph of total degree at most four over a characteristic-zero field, and pull back Psi_(L,M,N), with L*N nonzero. On the full pencil (0,t,c*t,d*t), the t^8 coefficient is 256*N^4*(partial_y2 R4(0,1,c,d))^2, so all ten x1-free quartic jets containing y2 vanish, including [x2^3*y2]R. The next square kills three x1-free cubic y2^2/y2^3 jets and expresses the remaining x1-free quartic slice triangularly. Four coefficients of t^5 force sigma=tau=[x2^4]R4=0 and Q(rho)=160*rho^2+1968*rho+6021=0 for rho=[x2^2*y2]R3. At t^4, the c^4 and d^2 coefficients force [y1^3]R3=[y2^2]R2=0, and the d coefficient then forces P(rho)=8*rho^2+99*rho+279=0. But Q-20*P=-3*(4*rho-147) and P(147/4)=58887/4, equivalently resultant(Q,P)=16959456, so the two equations have no common root in characteristic zero. Hence every degree-at-most-four graph has nonconstant Hessian determinant. The collision equations are not used.
supersedes_notes: the quartic x2^3*y2 graph jet as a viable first cancellation parameter
quartic Meng--Yang graphs as an untested descent class

entries.title: Meng--Yang plane normal-jet theorem
entries.scope: For an arbitrary polynomial graph y3=R(x1,x2,y1,y2), put T=R(0,x2,y1,y2) and S=partial_x1 R(0,x2,y1,y2). On x1=0, the graph Hessian has a universal lower 3-by-3 minor -2*L*N^2 and determinant F(T,partial T)-8*L*N^3*S. Thus, for L*N nonzero, every trace and target constant determine at most one first normal jet, while every x1^2-divisible correction is invisible on the plane. Consequently no graph R=R_le4+x1^2*U, with R_le4 of degree at most four and U of arbitrary degree, has constant Hessian determinant. More precisely, adding x1^2*U changes the first transverse determinant coefficient by -24*L*N^3*U(0,x2,y1,y2); for a degree-at-most-five graph, all components of that coefficient above degree three are immutable.
supersedes_notes: x1-squared higher-degree tails as a possible repair of the quartic plane obstruction

entries.title: Meng--Yang all-normal triangularity and formal graph theorem
entries.scope: Let D_R be the Hessian determinant of the scaled Meng--Yang potential pulled back to an arbitrary polynomial or x1-adic formal graph y3=R(x1,x2,y1,y2). For every k>=1 and U in K[x2,y1,y2], D_(R+x1^k*U)-D_R is congruent modulo x1^k to -4*L*N^3*k*(k+1)*x1^(k-1)*U. The multiplier is a unit in characteristic zero when L*N is nonzero. Hence every plane trace T and target constant determine a unique formal graph R in K[x2,y1,y2][[x1]] with D_R equal to that constant. This is formal local existence and uniqueness; it does not prove polynomial termination, global convergence, or preservation of the marked collision.
supersedes_notes: higher Meng--Yang graph normal orders as an undifferentiated nonlinear coefficient search

entries.title: Meng--Yang polynomial terminal-coefficient cone gate
entries.scope: Let R in K[x,y,p,q] be a polynomial graph of positive x-degree n with last coefficient R_n=U nonzero, and suppose the scaled Meng--Yang graph determinant is constant over a characteristic-zero field with L*N nonzero. Put d=2*n+6. The top x-coefficient of the determinant is 8*L^4*d*U^4 times ((d-1)*U*det(Hess(U))-(d+1)*grad(U)^T*adj(Hess(U))*grad(U)), so the displayed terminal equation must vanish. If U_m is the highest homogeneous tangential part of U, Euler's identity reduces its top part to the nonzero scalar -(d+2*m-1)/(m-1) times U_m*det(Hess(U_m)); hence det(Hess(U_m))=0, with degrees zero and one automatic. The ternary Hesse theorem therefore makes every terminal top form a cone after scalar extension. This is a necessary backward terminal gate, not a polynomial nontermination theorem; cone and lower-rank terminal coefficients remain.
supersedes_notes: the last normal coefficient as an unrestricted generic polynomial ansatz

entries.title: Meng--Yang pure weight-five polynomial-balance obstruction
entries.scope: For the scaled Meng--Yang family over a characteristic-zero field with L*N nonzero, no polynomial graph R=(N/L)*y^5*f(x*y), f in K[z], has constant Hessian determinant. After differentiating the full graph potential, restricting to p=q=0, and extracting the weight-six determinant face, one obtains a semilinear equation E(z,f,f',f''). For f asymptotic to a*z^m, its quartic sector has strictly largest z-degree 4*m+22 for every integer m>=0 and leading coefficient -144*a^4*(m^2-m-21). The resonance discriminant is 85, so no polynomial degree occurs; f=0 also fails because the degree-six constant-sector coefficient is 2916. This closes only the displayed one-function ansatz. The formal branch above the collision-containing plane-flat near miss couples its weight-five face to at least four lower graph channels and is not excluded; its higher corrections are not asserted to retain the marks.
supersedes_notes: pure weight-five polynomial balances as possible Meng--Yang graph terminations

entries.title: Meng--Yang coupled five-channel terminal split
entries.scope: Consider an exact five-function Meng--Yang graph R=y^5*f(x*y)+y^3*p*g(x*y)+y^3*h(x*y)+y^2*q*j(x*y)+y*p^2*ell(x*y) over a characteristic-zero field with L*N nonzero. Let n>0 be the maximum degree of the five univariate polynomials and let A,B,C,D,E be their respective z^n coefficients. The universal last-coefficient equation, restricted injectively by p=P*y and q=Q*y, factors as D^2*y^(4*n+6) times ((8*A*E*n^2+14*A*E*n-40*A*E+2*B^2*n+7*B^2)*y^2+2*B*E*P*(4*n^2+15*n+8)*y+2*E*(n+2)*(4*n+11)*(C+D*Q+E*P^2)). It vanishes identically if and only if D=0 or B=E=0. Thus, if the j-channel has maximal degree, the g- and ell-channels have smaller degree. This classifies the terminal face of the exact five-function packet; it does not exclude either surviving branch, unequal-degree balances, or repairs using lower graph-weight channels.
supersedes_notes: the coupled five-function terminal face as an unclassified common-degree balance

entries.title: Meng--Yang coupled upper-Newton chamber gate
entries.scope: For the exact five-function graph R=y^5*f(x*y)+y^3*p*g(x*y)+y^3*h(x*y)+y^2*q*j(x*y)+y*p^2*ell(x*y), assume f,g,j,ell are nonzero over a characteristic-zero field with L*N nonzero, and write their degrees as a,b,d,e. After differentiating before the substitutions x=z/y, p=P*y, q=Q*y, the complete weight-six determinant coefficient has 2348 terms, is independent of M,P,Q,h, and groups into 396 Newton sectors. Its upper degree is max(5*a+e+2*d+22,4*a+2*b+2*d+22). For d>0, the strict chamber 2*b>a+e is empty because its leading resonance P_G is a downward quadratic in d with negative discriminant after t=2*b-a>0. The other strict chamber requires P_F=2*a^3-4*a^2*d+15*a^2-2*a*d^2-34*a*d+29*a-30*d+60=0; for a>0 its discriminant is 4*(a+3)*(a+5)*(2*a+1)*(4*a+15), leaving an explicit genus-one integral-point condition, while a=0 forces d=2. The wall a+e=2*b retains one amplitude equation. If d=0, either strict chamber first forces j=3; substituting j=3 leaves 512 terms and 121 Newton sectors, whose next upper coefficients have fixed nonzero signs, so both strict chambers are empty. Thus the only unresolved Newton strata are the positive-degree P_F resonance and the wall; this does not exclude either stratum or graph channels below the five-function packet.
supersedes_notes: the complete coupled five-function polynomial-balance system as an undifferentiated Newton search

entries.title: Meng--Yang strict-resonance arithmetic closure
entries.scope: In the strict f^5*ell chamber of HC4MYPT4 with nonnegative integer degrees a,b,d,e and nonzero leading coefficients A,B,D,E, the resonance P_F(a,d)=0 has no solution with a>0. Indeed d=0,1 are positive cases; for d>=2, reduction modulo a gives a|30*(d-2), and k=30*(d-2)/a reduces P_F=0 to a quadratic Q_k(a). For k>=13 all coefficients of Q_k are positive. For 0<=k<=12 its discriminant is 900*(51-k)*(25-k)*(75-2*k), and none of the thirteen residual factors is a square. The only a=0 resonance is d=2. Its next f^5*j*ell face and the competing g^2*j^2 face exclude every degree gap except e=2*b+2, where 360*A*E+B^2*D*(b+5)^2=0 is necessary; HC4MYPT3 further forces b>=1. Thus the positive-degree genus-one resonance is empty, but this exceptional ridge, the balanced wall, and graph channels below the five-function packet remain open.
supersedes_notes: the positive-degree P_F resonance as an unresolved genus-one integral-point problem

entries.title: Meng--Yang algebraic fifth-channel elimination
entries.scope: For the complete 2348-term weight-six equation E_5 of the exact five-function Meng--Yang graph, E_5 contains neither ell' nor ell'' and is affine in ell: E_5=C_ell*ell+R, where C_ell=2*z*(2*L*z^5*f-3*N*z+2*N)*Q. The expanded nonzero factor Q has 311 terms and is independent of g,h,ell; R=E_5|_(ell=0) has 1895 terms. The explicit z-factor gives the necessary axis equation 80*L*f(0)*j(0)+492*L*f(0)-8*L*f'(0)+4*N*g(0)^2-64*N*g(0)*j(0)-356*N*g(0)+256*N*j(0)^2+2848*N*j(0)+7921*N=0. On an admissible wall a+e=2*b, the multiplier for every successive lower ell coefficient is -32*L^4*A^5*D^2*P_F(a,d), which cannot vanish by HC4MYPT5 and the wall leading equation. Hence the wall is unit-triangular in ell, and polynomiality is equivalent to the exact four-function divisibility C_ell|R plus its terminal remainder equations. The divisibility is not excluded here, either on the wall or on the exceptional HC4MYPT5 ridge; lower graph-weight channels also remain outside the theorem.
supersedes_notes: the balanced five-function wall as a free simultaneous coefficient ansatz

entries.title: All-degree diagonal ternary-Schur rigidity
entries.scope: Let m>=2 over a characteristic-zero field and normalize Hess(f)=diag(x^m,y^m,z^m). For homogeneous a of degree m and q of degree m-2, the reverse-Schur equation q*x^m*y^m*z^m=a_x^2*y^m*z^m+a_y^2*x^m*z^m+a_z^2*x^m*y^m holds if and only if a=alpha*x^m+beta*y^m+gamma*z^m and q=m^2*(alpha^2*x^(m-2)+beta^2*y^(m-2)+gamma^2*z^(m-2)). Indeed reduction modulo each coordinate power gives x^ceil(m/2)|a_x and its two analogues; any mixed monomial would then have two exponents at least ceil(m/2)+1 and total degree greater than m. Over an algebraic closure, the radical of the coefficient divisibility ideal is therefore the linear ideal of every mixed coefficient in every potential degree D=m+2>=4. This closes only the completely split diagonal Hessian stratum, not a general ternary Hessian or the remaining nonsquarefree factor strata.
supersedes_notes: the all-degree diagonal ternary-Schur pure-power classification as bounded evidence through degree eight

entries.title: All-degree minimal diagonal rank-two direction obstruction
entries.scope: For m>=3 and a nonzero normalized channel vector epsilon in {0,1}^3, let psi_min be the degree-D=m+2 three-layer diagonal Schur tower sum_v v^(m+2)/((m+2)(m+1))+(t/m)*sum_v epsilon_v*v^m+(t^2/2)*sum_v epsilon_v^2*v^(m-2). No constant symmetric rank-two 4-by-4 matrix Q satisfies det(Hess(psi_min)+s*Q)=det Hess(psi_min). The top Hessian coefficients first force the t row and column of Q to vanish. On t=0, two or three active channels force the ternary block to have rank at most one. With one active channel, rank two forces a nondegenerate inactive 2-by-2 block, while its complementary Hessian minor is (3-m)*t*x^(2m-4)-((m-1)*(m-2)/2)*t^2*x^(2m-6), nonzero for every m>=3. The theorem concerns only this minimal tower: arbitrary lower homogeneous layers can change later faces, and the tower itself is not asserted to be an HC4 potential.
supersedes_notes: the absence of constant rank-two directions on minimal diagonal Schur towers as a bounded degree-five-through-eight experiment

entries.title: All-lower-layer diagonal constant-direction obstruction
entries.scope: Let D=m+2>=5 over a characteristic-zero field. Consider an arbitrary completed diagonal Schur packet whose degree-D part has Hessian diag(x^m,y^m,z^m,0), whose degree-(D-1) part is (t/m)*sum_v alpha_v*v^m+b(x,y,z), and whose degree-(D-2) part has forced t^2 coefficient (1/2)*sum_v alpha_v^2*v^(m-2), with an arbitrary nonzero channel vector alpha in K^3; retain arbitrary compatible t-linear, ternary, and lower homogeneous terms. No constant symmetric 4-by-4 matrix Q of rank at least two satisfies det(Hess(psi)+s*Q)=det Hess(psi). The highest faces kill the t row and column of Q; rank four is impossible from det(Q), and rank three from det(Q_xyz)*H_tt. For rank two, two or three active channels force rank at most one. One active channel forces a nondegenerate inactive 2-by-2 block B, and the exact s^2 coefficient is det(B)*(H_xx*H_tt-H_xt^2). Its vanishing would make P=partial_x psi(x,0,0,t) and R=partial_t psi(x,0,0,t) algebraically dependent of consecutive degrees D-1 and D-2. Their common polynomial generator must therefore be linear; the pure x^(D-1) leading form forces it to depend only on x, contradicting P_t=R_x with R nonconstant. Thus arbitrary lower layers can move the minimal obstruction but never remove it. In degree five, HC4MR4 also excludes rank one, so the complete nonaligned diagonal quintic Schur packet admits no nonzero constant symmetric determinant-preserving direction of any rank. This closes constant quadratic pencil admission on that packet, not the packet itself, nonlinear or polynomially moving directions, or collision-preserving recharts.
dependencies: external: polynomial common-generator theorem for algebraically dependent polynomials
supersedes_notes: arbitrary lower homogeneous layers as an unresolved escape from the minimal diagonal rank-two obstruction
constant rank-two pencil admission as open on a completed diagonal quintic Schur packet

entries.title: Degree-five Meng--Yang leading-jet rigidity
entries.scope: Let y3=R(x1,x2,y1,y2) have total degree at most five and suppose its pulled-back scaled Meng--Yang potential has constant Hessian determinant over a characteristic-zero field. If T_j is the degree-j homogeneous part of the trace R(0,x2,y1,y2), the t^10, t^8, and t^7 faces on the full two-slope pencil force T_5=kappa*x2^5 and partial_y2(T_4)=0. The next faces kill [y2^3]T_3, [y1*y2^2]T_3, [x2*y2^2]T_3, and [y1^4]T_4, express [x2*y1^3]T_4=8*[y1^2*y2]T_3/3, then force tau=U=sigma=0 and V^2+(4*L*kappa/N)*(20*rho+123)=0 in the notation of the canonical note. Thus only one of the 21 x1-free quintic coefficients survives the leading faces; the first possible plane repair is the 15-dimensional x1-linear quartic normal jet.
supersedes_notes: the full 21-parameter x1-free quintic trace as an undifferentiated frontier

entries.title: Rational quintic Meng--Yang graph top-cone normal form
entries.scope: For a degree-at-most-five rational graph with constant pulled-back Hessian determinant, the complete two-slope jet forces R_5(0,x2,y1,y2)=zeta*x2^5 with zeta nonzero. The leading potential is L*(x1^3*R_5)^2; its zero top Hessian face and the low-dimensional Gordan--Noether theorem give a constant kernel direction in the (x2,y1,y2)-space, and the nonzero trace forces that direction into the (y1,y2)-plane. Hence the full quintic graph top lies on exactly two projective charts: R_5=zeta*x2^5+x1*T_4(x1,x2,y1-kappa*y2), or R_5=zeta*x2^5+x1*U_4(x1,x2,y2). This is a necessary top normal form, not a completed determinant identity. Over a larger characteristic-zero field the zero-zeta axis branch over Q(sqrt(34)) is not excluded by this theorem.
dependencies: external: low-dimensional Gordan--Noether zero-Hessian cone theorem
supersedes_notes: the rational quintic graph top as an unrestricted 56-parameter form

entries.title: Complete degree-two lower-trace obstruction on the first quintic kernel chart
entries.scope: For the v2 Meng--Yang potential, consider a degree-at-most-five graph on the partial_y2 top-kernel chart whose x1=0 trace is kappa*x2^5+d*x2^3*y1+rho*x2^2*y2+h*x2^3+e*x2*y1^2+T_le2(x2,y1,y2), with every coefficient of the complete degree-at-most-two polynomial T_le2 arbitrary. The degree-six and degree-five plane faces and y2-independence of the forced quartic normal jet parameterize the generic branch by (rho,a), where a=[y1*y2]T. At a=0, [x1*x2^7] and [x1*x2^4*y2] reduce to coprime cubics of resultant -108117004020524928. For arbitrary a, three repair-invariant transverse coefficients of bidegrees (1,3),(3,7),(1,3) generate the unit ideal in Q[a,rho]. Their two projection resultants have monic gcd 32*rho^2+384*rho+1557, but the third equation removes it. The exceptional chart 2*a+3=0 forces P=8*rho^2+99*rho+279=0 and is excluded by resultant(P,25*rho+141)=-15552. The coefficient [y2]T cancels from all witnesses. Writing b=[x2*y2]T and c=[y2^2]T, the forced quartic normal jet contains 256*c^2*x2^2*y2^2, hence c=0. If b is nonzero, the raw degree-five face forces 4*V+5*kappa=0. The V=0 branch would require P=Q=0; the other branch has V=8*(20*rho+123)/5 and ends in coprime polynomials 160*rho^2+1968*rho+5841 and 3968000*rho^4+98457600*rho^3+896972480*rho^2+3553345920*rho+5132433339, whose resultant is 986335129354383654912000. Every remaining lower-trace and target-constant coefficient cancels, while any x1^2*U changes the first transverse determinant only through degree three. Exact enumeration gives no admissible point modulo 101 or 103 on either branch; bad-prime collapses are recorded separately. Hence the complete displayed slice is empty over every characteristic-zero field. Collision equations are not used. This retained theorem treats the displayed slice. PF155 subsequently proves complete18-parameter witness cancellation, excludes every nonzero-quintic-trace degree-five v2 graph across all kernel directions, and reduces the complex remainder to two zero-quintic-trace conjugate classes overQ(sqrt34); no rational degree-at-most-five graph remains. PF156 subsequently closes both complex classes and the full v2 degree<=5 graph branch over every characteristic-zero field; global HC4 remains open.

entries.title: Sparse degree-five Meng--Yang graph-trace obstruction
entries.scope: For the v2 Meng--Yang potential, no graph of total degree at most five whose complete x1=0 trace is kappa*x2^5+d*x2^3*y1+rho*x2^2*y2 has constant Hessian determinant over a characteristic-zero field. All x1-linear normal coefficients and every remaining x1^2-divisible term allowed by the degree bound are included. The plane equations reduce to an explicit curve G(rho,V)=0 and uniquely fix the normal jet. Two immutable first-transverse axis coefficients have resultants whose common factor is Q(rho)=160*rho^2+1968*rho+6021; the residual Groebner basis forces V=kappa=0 and Q=0, while the full coefficient [x1*x2^4*y2]=216*(5*rho+12) is then incompatible with Q. The collision equations are not used. Nevertheless, the rational trace (kappa,d,rho)=(51/100,-47/10,-123/20) and target constant 17165601/25 give an exact graph containing both marked collision points and flattening the determinant on x1=0; its coefficient [x1*x2^7]=22032/125 proves transverse failure.

entries.title: Degree-89 relative-linear Meng--Yang collision obstruction
entries.scope: Complete the polynomial unit pivot t=A in the Meng--Yang potential and allow an arbitrary base-dependent residual-dual change C(x1,x2) in SL2(Q[x1,x2]) whose entries have total degree at most 89. The reduced potential has the form f(x1,x2)+2*G_1*r+2*G_2*s and Hessian determinant 16*Jac(G)^2, where G=gamma*C, gamma has degree profile (11,5), and Jac(G)(0)=-2. Constant nonzero Hessian therefore makes G a plane Keller map of degree at most 100; Moh's plane theorem makes G a polynomial automorphism. The last two gradient coordinates recover the base and the first two then recover the residual dual variables, so the descended gradient is a polynomial automorphism and has no collision. Corrections of degree at least 90 and changes nonlinear in the residual dual variables remain open.

entries.title: Nonlinear toric Schur descent from the Meng--Yang potential
entries.scope: The Meng--Yang HC(5) potential admits an explicit determinant-one nonlinear dual-coordinate change with t=A and unit quadratic pivot. Its natural four-variable Schur descent has determinant 16*J(x1*x2)^2 and loses the known collision. An explicit relative toric SL(2) correction makes the determinant 64 but makes the descended gradient polynomially invertible. In the full toric radial class, constant nonzero determinant forces both radial factors to be units, so no collision survives. Non-toric changes, non-coordinate coisotropic embeddings, and mixed coefficient-dependent critical equations are not excluded. Pure univariate higher-degree repairs are excluded separately by SDX1.

entries.title: Degree-four non-toric relative-SL(2) obstruction
entries.scope: After the polynomial unit-pivot reduction of the foundational Meng doubling, let beta=(-y*P(xy),x*Q(xy)) be the natural complementary coefficient row and let C(x,y) be a general polynomial 2x2 matrix of determinant one whose four entries have total degree at most four. For G=beta*C, the descended four-variable Hessian determinant is 16*det(DG)^2. The full 60-parameter characteristic-zero coefficient ideal has 45 determinant-one equations and 218 nonconstant-Jacobian equations; exact Singular elimination gives the unit ideal, before collision equality is imposed. Starting instead from the known degree-ten toric correction beta*C0=(y,2x), an arbitrary affine determinant-one perturbation also gives the unit ideal after imposing constant Jacobian and equality at the known antipodal collision bases. Raw corrections of degree at least five, quadratic-or-higher perturbations of C0, mixed base-dual changes, and non-coordinate coisotropic embeddings are not excluded.
dependencies: external: Singular exact Groebner bases over Q

entries.title: Double-Schur obstruction for root-engineered gauge families
entries.scope: For every admissible root-engineered quadratic-gauge Keller map, eliminating two constant linear dual directions from the six-variable Meng doubling cannot produce a four-variable constant-Hessian potential: the s^2 coefficient is the bordered invariant K(L), which is nonzero for every nonzero constant target linear form L. In the full cubic parameter family this follows from three triangular coefficients; in every exact degree N>=4 it follows from the top z-layer. A source-first Meng descent followed by a constant dual pivot also fails: higher-degree maps have no nonzero constant affine source direction, while in degree three the unique z-direction has no constant nonzero target-linear pivot. Nonlinear symplectic changes, nonlinear retained dual coefficients, non-coordinate coisotropic embeddings, and nonconstant pivots with exceptional divisibility are not excluded.

entries.title: Cubic triangular-target obstruction for double Schur descent
entries.scope: After the canonical linear normalization of the full cubic quadratic-gauge family, let (U,V,W) be any permutation of its three target coordinates and L=W+H(U,V), where H is arbitrary of total degree at most three. Exact sparse coefficients of the bordered invariant K(L) force the cubic shear coefficients to vanish and then give a quadratic contradiction in the P- and B-retained orientations; in the C-retained orientation [x^8]K(L)=9 independently of every shear coefficient. Hence no such triangular target coordinate can be the retained dual coefficient of a four-variable constant-Hessian double-dual descent. Compositions of nonlinear triangular shears, degree at least four, preliminary nonlinear changes of U and V, general nonlinear target automorphisms, and nonlinear source-dual symplectic changes are not excluded.

entries.title: Length-two quadratic triangular-target obstruction
entries.scope: For the foundational normalized cubic gauge F=(P,B,C), choose distinct target indices i,j and let k be the remaining index. Let A=F_i+Q(F_j,F_k) and L=F_j+R(A,F_k), where Q and R are arbitrary positive-degree real polynomials of total degree at most two. Exact axis and transverse-line coefficients of the bordered invariant K(L) exclude all six ordered words. The proof separately eliminates the A^2 coupling r20!=0 and the bilinear coupling r20=0, r11!=0; when r20=r11=0 the word is one quadratic triangular shear after rescaling and is covered by HC4TTS1. Degree-four single shears, words with a cubic-or-higher factor, length at least three, general tame or wild target automorphisms, and nonlinear source-dual symplectic changes are not excluded.

entries.title: Quartic triangular-target obstruction for double Schur descent
entries.scope: After canonical normalization to the foundational cubic gauge F=(P,B,C), let (U,V,W) be any target permutation and L=W+H(U,V), where H is arbitrary of positive total degree at most four over a characteristic-zero coefficient field. In the P- and B-retained orientations, five exact extreme spatial coefficients of the bordered invariant K(L), computed with all lower-degree parameters present, successively force every homogeneous quartic coefficient to vanish; HC4TTS1 then excludes the remaining cubic-or-lower shear. In the C-retained orientation [x^8]K(L)=9 independently of every coefficient through degree four. Degree at least five, words containing cubic-or-higher factors, length at least three, general target automorphisms, and nonlinear source-dual symplectic changes are not excluded.

entries.title: Sparse-quartic Meng--Yang collision and principal-part reduction
entries.scope: After the unit-pivot t=A descent and polynomial base gauge, the transported Meng--Yang points are an antipodal pair for psi_0=2yr+4xs. Collision-first linear algebra exhausts every homogeneous quartic correction supported on at most four monomials: 42953 isolated choices and 515 one-parameter families. Exact modular determinant evaluations reject every quartic-only isolated choice, and rational gcds reject every quartic-only family. The degree-eight principal-part screen leaves exactly 232 isolated quartics and two exact family members, hence 234 inputs for the full cubic-kernel theorem HC4MCK. The same checker also excludes corrections supported on one or two cubic monomials; those bounded-support terminal calculations are retained as regressions but are logically subsumed by HC4MCK. HC4MS6 and HC4JQS4 treat the pure sextic and joint quartic--sextic total-support-four boundaries. Dense quartics, quadratic renormalizations, larger mixed supports, and non-coordinate coisotropic embeddings are not excluded.

entries.title: Dense mixed-quartic Meng descent obstruction
entries.scope: In the collision-normalized Meng chart psi_0=2yr+4xs, take all 25 homogeneous quartic monomials of base-dual bidegrees (1,3), (2,2), and (3,1). Also treat separately the two 30-dimensional enlargements obtained by adjoining either every pure-base quartic or every pure-dual quartic. Collision plus the spatial-degree-two determinant identity has exact rank 14, leaving 11, 16, and 16 parameters. Sparse exact determinant expansion gives coefficient ideals with 262, 273, and 273 generators; Singular proves all three ideals are the unit ideal over Q. This dense coefficient theorem does not itself allow the pure-base and pure-dual sectors simultaneously, but HC4HQ1 subsumes it and closes the complete homogeneous quartic chart.

entries.title: Complete homogeneous-quartic obstruction in four Hessian variables
entries.scope: Let q be any nondegenerate quadratic form in four variables over a characteristic-zero field and h_4 any homogeneous quartic. After scalar extension and an explicit congruence, grad(q+h_4) becomes z+grad(H_4), with homogeneous cubic nonlinear part and symmetric Jacobian. If det Hess(q+h_4) is a nonzero constant, the de Bondt--van den Essen dimension-at-most-four theorem makes this gradient a polynomial automorphism. Hence it has no collision. In the normalized Meng chart the checker verifies the explicit congruence from 2yr+4xs to one half the sum of four squares, the chain rule on all 35 quartic monomials, and transport of the antipodal collision. HC4CQ1 subsequently closes cubic plus quartic, and HC4E46 closes quartic plus sextic. Simultaneous cubic and sextic corrections and non-coordinate coisotropic embeddings are not covered.

entries.title: Complete dense cubic--quartic Meng obstruction
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4 be a four-variable potential in the collision-normalized Meng chart, with q2 nondegenerate quadratic and h3,h4 arbitrary homogeneous cubic and quartic forms. Homogeneous determinant layers and the Gordan--Noether theorem give a constant direction v with D_v h4=0 and D_v^2 h3=0 in every possible generic rank of Hess(h4); the rank-one quartic case is closed by a secondary ternary linear-pencil rank analysis. A nonisotropic v gives polynomial Schur descent to HC(3). In the isotropic bordered case, exact t^2 and t coefficients reduce either to a cotangent lift of a plane Keller map of degrees at most two and three, or to a two-variable HC(2) block after a binary quadratic bordered invariant forces s=constant+x. Moh's plane bound, HC(3), and HC(2) exclude a nonzero antipodal collision. There is no support restriction. HC4E46 separately closes quartic--sextic corrections. Simultaneous cubic and sextic corrections and non-coordinate coisotropic embeddings are not covered.

entries.title: Three-cubic Meng descent characteristic-zero obstruction
entries.scope: For each of the 234 collision-compatible quartic principal parts from HC4MQ1, all 1140 supports of exactly three cubic monomials are reconstructed and screened over Q. The combined determinant-degree-seven and degree-one rank census on the 266760 quartic/triple pairs is 5480, 53364, 130508, and 77408 in ranks zero through three, exactly matching the finite-field discovery calculation. After support-at-most-two boundary loci are delegated to HC4MQ1, exact rational full-determinant gcds or Groebner ideals are units for all 920 genuine rank-two lines, 2952 genuine rank-one planes, and 5480 rank-zero three-parameter coefficient spaces. entries.title: Full cubic-kernel Meng descent obstruction
entries.scope: For every one of the 234 collision-compatible quartic principal parts supported on at most four monomials, the complete odd determinant signature is reconstructed over Q on the 20-dimensional cubic coefficient space. Its rank is 8 for 229 quartics, 7 for one quartic, and 4 for four exceptional quartics, giving full kernel dimensions 12, 13, and 16. The exceptional quartics factor as u^3 times a linear form and are treated in triangular harmonic-cubic charts. Exact symbolic spatial-coefficient ideals, added in descending determinant degree, are unit ideals over Q for every full kernel: 62 first become units at degree six, 16 at degree five, and 156 at degree four. Thus no arbitrary homogeneous cubic correction preserves the Meng collision with constant nonzero Hessian determinant in this sparse-quartic chart.

entries.title: Sparse sextic-only Meng collision obstruction
entries.scope: In the collision-normalized Meng four-variable chart, every homogeneous sextic correction supported on at most four of the 84 sextic monomials is excluded. Collision-first exponent linear algebra exhausts 2028355 supports and leaves 1725838 isolated points, 7566 lines, and one plane. A rank-preserving reduction modulo 1000003 and leading-Hessian evaluations leave 748 isolated candidates, all rejected by two full-determinant evaluations. Every positive-dimensional family is reconstructed over Q: exact principal gcds leave two lines, with parameters -81/8 and 9/2, and determinant degree twelve rejects both; the unique binary-cubic plane in yr and xs has unit principal coefficient ideal over Q. This sparse theorem is retained as an exact regression and is subsumed by the support-free even quartic--sextic theorem HC4E46.

entries.title: Mixed sparse quartic--sextic Meng obstruction
entries.scope: For every one of the 234 quartic principal parts from HC4MQ1, no added homogeneous sextic supported on at most four monomials, with zero gradient at the normalized collision point and with no cubic correction, gives constant nonzero Hessian determinant. Exactly four quartics pass the immutable determinant-degree-two gate. Their sextic exponent kernel has 976 three-support lines, 205494 four-support lines, and 519 planes; principal Hessian cancellation leaves 121146 lines. For each quartic, 52686 lines have projectively complete modular certificates and the remaining 68460 have unit exact rational gcds. All 2076 plane/quartic three-evaluation ideals are unit ideals over Q. This sparse mixed theorem is retained as an exact regression and is subsumed by HC4E46.

entries.title: Joint total-support-four quartic--sextic Meng obstruction
entries.scope: In the collision-normalized Meng four-variable chart, no correction h4+h6 of combined monomial support at most four, with no cubic term, retains the collision and has constant nonzero Hessian determinant. The pure quartic and pure sextic boundaries are HC4MQ1 and HC4MS6. For the genuinely mixed part, collision-first linear algebra exhausts 6133820 supports and leaves 5225684 isolated points, 44300 lines, and 34 planes. A rank-preserving reduction modulo 1000003 and descending determinant-layer evaluations reject every isolated point. Every line is reconstructed over Q and has unit exact evaluation gcd; every plane has unit exact three-evaluation ideal over Q. This bounded-support theorem is retained as an exact regression and is subsumed by HC4E46.

entries.title: Dense common-kernel quartic--sextic Meng obstruction
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h4+h6 be an even four-variable potential in the collision-normalized Meng chart, with nonsingular quadratic Hessian, homogeneous quartic and sextic corrections, and no cubic term. If a nonzero constant direction v satisfies D_v h6=0 and D_v^2 h4=0, then constant nonzero Hessian determinant is incompatible with an antipodal gradient collision, without any support bound. Gordan--Noether and the determinant-degree-fourteen layer make this common-kernel condition automatic when Hess(h6) has generic rank three. A non-isotropic quadratic pivot reduces to HC_3. In the isotropic bordered case, exact t^2 and t coefficient factorizations reduce to either an odd plane Keller map of degree at most five or a two-variable constant-Hessian potential; Moh's degree bound and HC_2 exclude the collision. HC4E46 uses this theorem together with cone-degree rigidity to close the rank-at-most-two boundary; simultaneous cubic and sextic corrections are not covered.

entries.title: HC4 source/dual bigrading and successive-cone synchronization
entries.scope: In the even collision-normalized four-variable Meng chart, the 2+2 source/dual decomposition has quartic bidegree dimensions 5,8,9,8,5 and sextic dimensions 7,12,15,16,15,12,7. The locus whose nonlinear corrections have dual degree at most one has the exact cotangent form psi=tF+mG+H and det Hess(psi)=Jac(F,G)^2, so its collision obstruction is precisely an odd plane JC(2) problem of degree at most five and is excluded by Moh's bound. For every integral weight, diagonal conjugation removes Hessian derivative shifts and makes the determinant a one-exponent face pencil. After a nondegenerate quotient is eliminated, any two-dimensional residual symmetric Hessian form with vanishing determinant has, on each pivot chart, the unique Schur factorization a[[1,r],[r,r^2]]; its successive weighted faces recursively determine one rational projective kernel line. This synchronization does not itself make the line constant: (xt+ym)^2 has the moving kernel (-y,x). HC4E46 subsequently excludes the moving cone by bihomogeneous degree rigidity and the next full determinant face.

entries.title: Complete even quartic--sextic obstruction in four Hessian variables
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h4+h6 be an even four-variable potential over a characteristic-zero field, with q2 nondegenerate quadratic and h4,h6 homogeneous of degrees four and six. If det Hess(psi) is a nonzero constant, then grad(psi) has no nonzero antipodal collision. Rank three of Hess(h6) is HC4DCK. In rank two, low-dimensional Gordan--Noether makes the sextic kernel a constant source/dual plane and the degree-twelve face forces the binary Hessian of h4 on that plane to vanish. Two-variable singular-Hessian classification, successive-cone synchronization, a primitive UFD argument, and total degree four leave only c*(X^T*M*U)^2 as a nonconstant cone. Rank-one M is a constant direction covered by HC4DCK; for invertible M, the dual-degree-four part of the spatial z^4 face is the uncancellable polynomial 48*c^4*det(M)^2*(X^T*M*U)^4. In sextic rank one, the three-variable singular-Hessian normal form over the one-variable quotient field supplies a D_v^2 h4=0 direction and homogeneity makes its direction scheme constant, reducing again to HC4DCK. Rank zero is HC4HQ1. Thus all support restrictions in the quartic--sextic chart are removed; simultaneous cubic and sextic corrections and non-coordinate coisotropic embeddings are not covered.

entries.title: Rank-three sextic reduction with simultaneous cubic and quartic layers
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h6 be a four-variable collision-normalized Meng potential, with q2 nondegenerate quadratic, h3,h4,h6 arbitrary homogeneous forms of degrees three, four, and six, and Hess(h6) of generic rank three. The constant sextic kernel and determinant degrees fourteen and thirteen force D_t^2 h4=D_t^2 h3=0. A nonisotropic t-direction descends to HC(3). In the isotropic chart, the t^2 coefficient is the bordered invariant of a ternary polynomial s of degree at most three. Gordan--Noether and the three binary-cubic root-multiplicity orbits reduce its coefficient equations to exact constant-direction branches: the rank-two orbits have ideal (qxm,qym,lm)^2, the rank-one orbit has two explicitly certified radical branches, and the quadratic boundary follows from adjugate linear algebra. The next coefficient is either a cotangent lift of a plane Keller map of degrees at most three and five or a terminal HC(2) block. Thus a constant nonzero Hessian determinant is incompatible with a nonzero antipodal collision, with no support restriction within the displayed homogeneous support. HC4T21 and HC4T11 subsequently close sextic Hessian ranks two and one, and HC4TC1 exhausts the coordinate q2+h3+h4+h6 chart; quintic and higher layers and non-coordinate coisotropic embeddings are not covered.

entries.title: Rank-one sextic reduction with simultaneous cubic and quartic layers
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h6 be a four-variable collision-normalized Meng potential with q2 nondegenerate quadratic, h3,h4,h6 arbitrary homogeneous forms of degrees three, four, and six, and Hess(h6) of generic rank one. The three-variable singular-Hessian classification and one-base homogeneity make all residual projective cones constant. Every branch reaches the common-direction descent HC4T31, so a constant nonzero Hessian determinant is incompatible with a nonzero antipodal collision, with no support restriction.

entries.scope: For every ternary polynomial s of degree at most four over a characteristic-zero field, the identity grad(s)^T adj(Hess(s)) grad(s)=0 forces s to omit a nonzero constant direction. entries.title: Quintic bordered constant-direction lemma
entries.scope: Extending the quartic constant-direction lemma HC4BL4, for every ternary polynomial s of degree at most five over a characteristic-zero field, the identity grad(s)^T*adj(Hess(s))*grad(s)=0 forces s to omit a nonzero constant direction. HC4RSD23 closes every non-pure binary quintic top. For a fifth-power top x^5/20, the degree-twelve face is x^8*det(Hess_(y,z)(s_4))/16. The passive singular-Hessian normal form is s_4=Q_4(x,y)+k*x^3*z. If k*Q_yy is nonzero, the next two faces leave exactly two normalized branches and both complete lower-tail coefficient ideals are the unit ideal. If the quartic passive part is affine, the finite-ratio and zero-ratio radicals force a fixed missing direction, the ratio-infinity chart is inconsistent, and its conic boundary returns to ratio zero. If the first transverse cubic is nonzero, the complete radical aligns every lower passive term with z+d*y. If it is zero, writing s=h(x,y)+z*(M*x+N*y+R)+F*z^2/2 gives z^2 and z coefficients F*K and 2*(M*x+N*y+R)*K for the same unbordered Schur factor K; binary singular-Hessian reduction ends in -(x*g'-g)^2 and again a fixed direction. Thus every degree-at-most-five bordered coefficient is a cylinder.

entries.title: Fermat-sextic quintic Schur obstruction
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h5+h6 be a four-variable collision-normalized potential with h6=(x^6+y^6+z^6)/30 and arbitrary h5. Write h5=t*s4+r5 in the constant sextic-kernel direction. Polynomial Schur divisibility forces the quartic s4 to be diagonal: the 66 bad coefficients have radical equal to the ideal of all twelve mixed quartic coefficients. Retain arbitrary r5 and every compatible lower quartic, cubic, and quadratic coefficient. The lambda^13*t*x^4*y^4*z^4 coefficient fixes the t^3 coefficient delta of h3 as 32*(a^3+b^3+c^3)/3. Three lambda^11*t^3 coefficients then become 1024*a^5, 1024*b^5, and 1024*c^5, so characteristic zero forces s4=0. HC4CD5 closes the resulting common-direction branch. The radical and determinant extractions are exact symbolic certificates; Lean independently checks the scalar Schur identity and the characteristic-zero fifth-power implication, but not those extractions.

entries.title: Symmetric-sextic quintic Schur obstruction
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h5+h6 be a four-variable collision-normalized potential with h6=(x^6+y^6+z^6)/30+mu*x^2*y^2*z^2. Write h5=t*s4+r5 in the constant sextic-kernel direction. For mu nonzero, comparison of the generic quartic Schur numerator with det(Hess(h6)) times a generic quadratic quotient gives 111 equations. Saturation by mu has an exact 261-element rational Groebner basis contained in the 21-variable coefficient origin, while the fourth power of every origin generator lies in the saturated ideal. Hence s4=0 and HC4CD5 closes the branch. At mu=0, HC4QF1 applies. Thus every member of this non-diagonal symmetric sextic pencil is excluded, with arbitrary base quintic and all lower homogeneous pieces. Lean checks the reduced-ring fourth-power endpoint, but not the Groebner saturation.

entries.title: Generic two-parameter symmetric-sextic Schur rigidity
entries.scope: For h6=(x^6+y^6+z^6)/30+mu*x^2*y^2*z^2+nu*sum_(i!=j)x_i^4*x_j^2, consider the generic quartic Schur-divisibility problem over Q(mu,nu). On nu nonzero, six boundary coefficients solve the quadratic quotient with determinant 4096*nu^12. Clearing the resulting 2*nu^2 denominator leaves 114 intrinsic equations in fifteen quartic coefficients. Their exact function-field Groebner basis has 117 elements and contains the cube of every quartic coefficient, so the generic point admits only s4=0 and reaches HC4CD5. This proves rigidity on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the two-parameter surface. The calculation alone does not exclude exceptional algebraic curves inside nu nonzero; HC4QSE4 later gives the full reduced classification. HC4QSE1 gives the exceptional radial point, HC4QSE2 proves that point cannot prolong to a collision, and the boundary nu=0 is separately closed by HC4QS1.

entries.title: Exceptional radial quartic Schur pair
entries.scope: Write R=x^2+y^2+z^2, P2=x^2*y^2+x^2*z^2+y^2*z^2, and P3=x^2*y^2*z^2. The two-parameter surface is h6=R^3/30+(nu-1/10)*R*P2+(mu-3*nu+1/10)*P3. At (mu,nu)=(1/5,1/10), both deformation coefficients vanish and h6=R^3/30. Its Hessian determinant is R^6/25, and the nonzero quartic s4=R^2 satisfies grad(s4)^T*adj(Hess(h6))*grad(s4)=det(Hess(h6))*16*R. For the fixed quartic R^2 and its symmetry-forced quotient q*R, the eight coefficient equations over the deformation coordinates A,B have reduced Groebner basis (q-16,A,B), so this radial quartic occurs nowhere else on the surface. This certifies the exceptional degree-fourteen Schur face; HC4QSE2 separately excludes its lower-face prolongation.

entries.title: Radial Schur-pair lower-face obstruction
entries.scope: For the exceptional radial Schur pair h6=R^3/30 and h5=t*R^2 from HC4QSE1, retain an arbitrary ternary base quintic r5 and the complete lower ansatz h4=8*t^2*R+t*r3+phi4, h3=delta*t^3+t^2*L1+t*g2+phi3, and an arbitrary quadratic q2. In the four-variable Hessian determinant pencil, the coefficient of lambda^13*t*x^12 is 2*(3*delta-32)/25, while the coefficient of lambda^11*t^3*x^8 is 64*(99*delta-1040)/25. Every coefficient of r5,r3,phi4,L1,g2,phi3,q2 cancels. The first face forces delta=32/3, after which the second coefficient is 1024/25. Hence the exceptional radial Schur pair cannot extend to a constant-Hessian collision, even with fully non-invariant lower homogeneous data.

entries.title: Even symmetric Schur-locus classification
entries.scope: Write R=x^2+y^2+z^2, P2=x^2*y^2+x^2*z^2+y^2*z^2, P3=x^2*y^2*z^2, and h6=R^3/30+A*R*P2+B*P3, where A=nu-1/10 and B=mu-3*nu+1/10. For the projective line of even permutation-invariant quartics s4=a*R^2+b*P2, symmetry forces the quadratic Schur quotient to be q*R. On the chart a=1, the radical of the eight coefficient equations is the intersection (q-16,b,A,B) intersect (q-16,b+2,10*A+1,10*B-1). These are respectively the radial pair at (mu,nu)=(1/5,1/10) and the Fermat pair at (mu,nu)=(0,0), s4=x^4+y^4+z^4. The complementary chart a=0 is the unit ideal. Hence this complete symmetric-even quartic slice has no exceptional parameter curve. The two isolated pairs are excluded at lower faces by HC4QSE2 and HC4QF1.

entries.title: Full exceptional Schur atlas on the two-parameter sextic surface
entries.scope: For h6=(x^6+y^6+z^6)/30+mu*x^2*y^2*z^2+nu*sum_(i!=j)x_i^4*x_j^2 and an arbitrary fifteen-coefficient nonzero quartic s4, the reduced projective Schur incidence scheme is the disjoint union of the Fermat component {(mu,nu)=(0,0)} times P<span(x^4,y^4,z^4)> and the radial point {(mu,nu)=(1/5,1/10), [s4]=[(x^2+y^2+z^2)^2]}. The proof writes the Hessian determinant in the seven symmetric invariants and uses the fact that a squarefree degree-twelve Hessian determinant cannot divide the rank-one Schur norm of a degree-four gradient: it would divide the degree-eleven vector adj(Hess(h6))*grad(s4), forcing s4=0. Exact elimination of the P3-discriminant leaves Fermat, radial, and (5/7,-1/14); the third Hessian is a product of two distinct coprime factors, the two degree-drop lines add no repeated factor, and invariant-quotient ramification adds no component. HC4QF1 excludes the full Fermat projective plane at the next determinant faces, while HC4QSE2 excludes the radial point. Both calculations retain arbitrary lower homogeneous data in a collision-normalized potential, so adjoining antipodal collision equations cannot restore a solution. Thus no nonzero Schur pair on this surface defines a new HC(4) candidate. The theorem classifies the reduction; nilpotent and embedded thickness at the two support points is not asserted.

entries.title: Cube-torsion nilpotence jump and bounded fourth-power support audit
entries.scope: For the HC4QSG2 two-parameter sextic surface, the committed cube-torsion calculation uses the canonical multiplication presentation A^1710 -> A^680 and fifteen coefficient-cube targets, rather than a noncanonical A^114 -> A^15 compression. Complete scans of four coefficient-monomial orbits over F_11, F_13, F_17, and F_19 reconstruct the radial point and the additional rational point (mu,nu)=(-5/3,-1/6) on D(nu). Exact rational specialization at the additional point leaves precisely the three x_i^2*x_j^2 coefficient cubes nonzero, while every coefficient fourth power vanishes and the reduced Schur fiber is the origin. Thus this point is a nilpotence-order jump, not a reduced exceptional Schur component, and cube-torsion support is not the reduced exceptional locus. Separate complete F_p-rational parameter scans at p=7,11,13 show that on D(nu) every tested nonradial fiber has empty reduced projective Schur fiber; they do not cover proper finite-field extensions or prove a characteristic-zero support theorem. The primitive 114-equation extension across nu=0 is chart-dependent and cannot be used for Fermat. The integral even-block annihilator, function-field lift, and symbolic fourth-power annihilator each timed out before a certificate; the exact zeroth Fitting ideal, primary thickness, and associated primes remain open. HC4QSE4 independently gives the full reduced characteristic-zero classification, but does not determine this nilpotent thickness.

entries.title: Backward rank-compressed cubic restriction and companion cancellation
entries.scope: For F=x+Q+B*c and V(x,y,t)=(x+t*Q+t^2*B*y,y-c,t), every collision-compatible fixed linear covector gives a Keller restriction on its common affine level. Relatively over the full t-line, V factors as A_(t^2 B) o (E_t x I) o S_c with E_t=x+tQ+t^2Bc. For t!=0, homogeneity gives E_t(x)=t^-1 F(tx), so all nonzero fibers are stably equivalent scaled copies of F; the t=0 fiber (x,y-c(x)) is triangular and injective. Hence every parent collision normalizes to t=1 without loss, and the off-diagonal collision scheme over G_m is stably Coll_off(F) x G_m x A^r. Collision arcs have exact pole ledger wt(t,x,y)=(1,-1,-3), so ordinary specialization erases them while the weighted Rees coordinates X=tx, Y=t^3y recover the base collision. Exact symbolic fixtures check a non-coordinate fixed covector, the generic companion determinant identity, the injective special fiber, a transported MacFarlane collision at t=2, and the collision-arc weights. The implementation calibrates G20 -> M19 ~ F13 x I6, retains collision pairs individually, records distinct direct degree-three and cubic-homogeneous objective keys, and applies them to the active restricted-minima, boundary-obstruction, and 16 -> 24 rank-compressed BCW pipelines. At this stage the pinned external G20 determinant certificate improved the frontiers to n_cub<=20 and n_HN,4<=40. BCR2 later resolves BCR-OPEN1 with an exact twelve-variable map and improves those endpoints to 19 and 38. The thirteen retained restricted-minima representatives have best direct key (18,26,7), but their old archive objective makes this no lower bound.

entries.title: Twelve-variable degree-three coordinate-pair reduction
entries.scope: Let F13 be MacFarlane's degree-three Keller collision. The triangular source coordinate s=F13_13=x13+x2^2 and triangular target square completion y4->y4-y8^2 put it in the exact relative form (K1,K2,K3,K4+s*(2*z12-z1^2),K5,...,K12,s). The determinant is recomputed directly as an exact sparse polynomial, independently of the relative bridge, and a separate standard-library implementation replays the explicit map, collision, and determinant without SymPy or shared algebra code. The cubic-output rank of K is exactly six, so rank-compressed homogenization gives an explicit nineteen-variable cubic-homogeneous Keller collision G19. The scaling and companion identities prove det DG19=1. Its homogeneous cotangent lift gives a quartic HN counterexample in 38 variables. Thus the certified upper bounds are n_degree<=3<=12, n_cub<=19, and n_HN,4<=38. These are upper bounds only; minimality, literature priority, Lean formalization, and external review are not claimed.

entries.title: Dimension-38 cross-construction and coordinated-shear frontier
entries.scope: The public Traboulsi route at commit 73635c96034bb8364c036fbec2e366224e601b40 starts from an eleven-variable degree-three Keller collision of cubic-output rank seven, while the independent BCR2 route starts from twelve variables and rank six. Both have compressed score n+r=18, homogeneous cubic dimension nineteen, and quartic HN dimension 38. Thus ordinary cotangent doubling next targets dimension 36 and requires n+r<=17; it cannot produce 37. For the public eleven-variable lift, every linear/quadratic completed-pivot system on each of the seven source-affine graph coordinates a,b,c,q,s,h,k is exactly inconsistent, with augmented rank one above full column rank; the non-affine d pivot is outside this linear audit. For the nonlinear local pivot K8=z8+z1*z2, restriction after a completion P in the eight z8-independent outputs gives K4=z4+(z1*z2)^2-P(K)^2. Degree at most three forces the pullback of P to have degree at most two and quadratic part plus or minus z1*z2. For target degree at most two, the degree-at-least-three cancellation system has shape 206 by 44, rank 39, and a five-dimensional kernel whose quadratic-part span has rank five but augmented rank six after adjoining z1*z2; hence no such completion succeeds. Finally, coordinated quadratic shears of the jointly affine source block (z4,z7,z9,z10,z11) by quadratics in (z1,z2,z3,z5,z6,z8,z12) have a fourteen-dimensional exact degree-preserving kernel, which separate-coordinate tests miss. A fixed cubic coefficient minor has determinant six, and the Schur conditions for cubic-output rank at most five contain six affine equations with coefficient and augmented ranks (5,6). Therefore this entire coordinated-shear family cannot lower the rank from six to five. These are bounded exact obstructions only, not a lower bound below dimension 38.

entries.title: Twelve-to-eleven coordinate-pair bounded frontier
entries.scope: For the BCR2 twelve-variable map K, every linear target coordinate g whose pullback g(K) is a polynomial graph coordinate is classified by exact linear equations. Source pivots z1,z2,z3 are impossible; pivots z4,...,z12 give nine normalized parameter families of dimensions seven through ten. In every family, the equations forcing all eleven raw retained outputs to have degree at most three generate the unit ideal over Q, so no linear graph coordinate gives a raw cubic restriction. At the nine literal coordinates g=y_j, j=4,...,12, every graph restriction has degree four or five. For each deletion, at least one high-degree defect lies outside the complete span generated by all target monomials of degrees one through three in the other raw retained outputs. Good-prime augmented-rank increases certify inconsistency over Q. The two closest literal deletions, j=11,12, remain obstructed through target degree four: 990 nonzero columns have rank 990 modulo 1000003 and the required defect raises rank to 991. This is an exact bounded obstruction only; it does not exclude parameter-dependent completion over nonliteral linear families, nonlinear source coordinates, or ordered multi-stage target automorphisms, and it is not a dimension-eleven lower bound.

entries.title: Parameterized quadratic-graph target-completion frontier
entries.scope: For the BCR2 twelve-variable map K, the linear target coordinates whose pullbacks have quadratic graph correction form exactly six normalized families with source pivots z7,...,z12, of parameter dimensions four or five. On the common collision slice their bad original output sets are respectively {3}, {2,3,4}, {2}, {3}, {1}, {1}. For every family, the full high-degree coefficient matrix for all linear and quadratic target monomials in the other ten raw retained outputs has full-column minors Delta_nu(a), while corresponding augmented minors are nonzero constant multiples of Delta_nu(a). The determinant opens generate the unit ideal in every parameter ring; for z8 four opens close all exceptional hypersurfaces. Hence no family admits a one-stage quadratic target completion restoring degree at most three. For the five single-defect families z7,z9,z10,z11,z12, adjoining all cubic target monomials gives 275 nonzero columns, and constant 275-by-275 and augmented 276-by-276 minors prove that no cubic target completion exists anywhere in those parameter families. This is a bounded exact theorem, not a dimension-eleven lower bound; the multi-defect z8 cubic system, target degree at least four, cubic graph corrections, nonlinear target coordinates, and ordered multi-stage automorphisms are outside its scope.

entries.title: Nonlinear-pivot and coordinated left-right closure at dimension 38
entries.scope: At the public eleven-variable pivot G7=d-xy, a completed target coordinate gives G4=a+(xy)^2-R^2 on its slice; at the local twelve-variable pivot K8=z8+z1*z2, it gives K4=z4+(z1*z2)^2-R^2. Degree at most three forces R to have degree at most two and quadratic part plus or minus xy or z1*z2. For every target degree from one through eight, good-prime coefficient ranks have constant nullities three and five respectively, matching the explicit characteristic-zero spans (G8,G10,G11) and (K7,K9,K10,K11,K12). Their quadratic spans have ranks 3 and 5, rising to 4 and 6 after adjoining the required monomial. Hence both nonlinear pivots are obstructed through target degree eight. For the local map, combine 140 quadratic shears of the jointly affine source block (z4,z7,z9,z10,z11) with all 792 elementary quadratic target directions. The degree-at-least-four matrix has good-prime rank 896 and a 36-dimensional kernel; all sparse relations have support at most five, rationally reconstruct, and cancel exactly. A fixed cubic minor has determinant 12 and a Schur entry is constantly -2, so the linearized kernel cannot reach cubic-output rank five. Of 22 target-bearing relations, 17 integrate to exact triangular degree-three one-parameter families and five have only the trivial parameter because their common high-degree factor is lambda^2. Combining the 17 integrable directions gives a genuine triangular source-target family whose degree-three locus has 48 quadratic/cubic equations. Adjoining a selected six-by-six cubic minor gives Groebner basis (1) over Q, so every member of that degree-three locus has cubic-output rank at least six. These are bounded family theorems, not a lower bound below dimension 38.

entries.title: Parameterized z8 cubic-completion obstruction
entries.scope: For the BCR2 twelve-variable map, consider the five-parameter quadratic graph coordinate g=a0*y7+y8+a1*y9+a2*y10+a3*y11+a4*y12 with source pivot z8. Its collision-slice restriction has bad original components 2,3,4. Completing component 2 by all linear, quadratic, and cubic target monomials in the other ten raw retained outputs gives 285 formal columns, 277 nonzero high-degree columns, and 54977 source-monomial rows. A sparse two-exponent-block implementation uses modular elimination only to select three fixed row sets, then reconstructs the 277-by-277 column and 278-by-278 augmented determinants exactly over Q[a0,...,a4]. The augmented determinant is 9/7 times the column determinant on all three row sets. Up to nonzero constants, the column determinants are (a2*a4+1)*(2*a2*a4+1)^2*(4*a2*a4+1)*(18*a0*a3*a4^2+7*a2*a4+1), a2^22*a4^159, and a0^2*a3^29*a4^160; they generate the unit ideal. It does not cover target degree at least four, cubic graph corrections, nonlinear target coordinates, or ordered multi-stage automorphisms, and is not a dimension-eleven lower bound.

entries.title: K12/G19 tensor-module obstruction and cubic-graph modular frontier
entries.scope: For a homogeneous polynomial tensor T in W tensor Sym^d(V*), the output flattening has kernel equal to the common left kernel of the coefficient matrices of JT, while the input-directional flattening v -> D_v T has kernel equal to their common right kernel. Thus all three displayed tensors have zero common right kernel; G19 has only the fixed tau output in its common left kernel. Consequently no constant linear source direction quotients either the K12 cubic tensor or G19, and their partially symmetric pure-cube ranks are at least 12 and 19. The checker replays the K12 and G19 collisions and the companion scaling identity; the direct K12 determinant remains in BCR2. Separately, a bounded discovery experiment tests 7844 signed integer parameter points at each of GF(101) and GF(103), for 15688 modular evaluations across all nine normalized graph-coordinate families. It finds no survivor at either prime, including 13646 genuinely cubic-graph evaluations. This census is not a characteristic-zero obstruction. Neither part proves dimension-twelve minimality or excludes nonlinear graphs, nonconstant modules, ordered target stages, exact Schur elimination, or a different collision tensor.

entries.title: External collision-ideal and off-diagonal-sheet audit
entries.scope: The manuscript Collision Ideals and Off-Diagonal Sheets names Chloe van der Vlugt as author; its public Lean source is published by the GitHub account what-social-construct, with no identity link between those attributions inferred here. The manuscript discloses OpenAI Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol) assistance and assigns final responsibility to its author. At external commit a409db9922279907493d96f691b5ea9eb71baaf9, the project correctly identifies S/I_R with A tensor_B A, the obstruction I_Delta/I_R with the diagonal kernel, and planar Keller collision rings with a clopen diagonal/off-diagonal splitting cut out by a secant idempotent. For a separable nonnormal cubic L/K, the paper proof gives L tensor_K L isomorphic to L times its S_3 normal closure N. The pinned Lean 4.24.0 project builds with no sorry or admit. Its planar endpoint keeps no-hidden-inertia explicit and uses three named literature axioms; no-hidden-inertia is not proved and, on the supplied planar diagram, is equivalent to absence of divisorial ramification, so this is a conditional reformulation rather than a new JC2 result. The Lean cubic endpoint takes the residual-field equivalence and nontrivial fixing subgroup as inputs; their derivation from nonnormality is proved on paper but not formalized. The repository adopts the algebraic interface while retaining saturation for arbitrary non-clopen off-diagonal closures and refusing to promote the generic N factor to a global component without separate descent and normality arguments. The separately announced explicit three-dimensional counterexample and its independent AFP verification are background provenance, not results of this paper.

entries.title: Rank-three collision-framed target-local descent
entries.scope: For every rank-three finite-etale cover E/S, the ordered off-diagonal self-collision cover Off_2(E/S) is canonically the S_3 frame torsor: an ordered distinct pair has a functorial rank-one complement. On this torsor, signed maximal minors give the unique PGL_2 transformation between any two ordered primitive-root triples; its determinant is the product of their Vandermondes, simultaneous S_3 relabeling changes only its scalar, and uniqueness gives the exact three-presentation cocycle. Every quadratic Tschirnhaus change u=q0+q1*r+q2*r^2 has explicit symmetric target formulas; its precise transition open is the product of the primitive basis determinant Theta and the normalized-linear-coefficient factor f2, and its coefficient composition law closes. For the normalized linear-quadratic factorization model of the fixed foundational cubic Keller map, the PGL_2 transition lifts canonically after inverting D_g(C)=ell(g dot C), with exact resultant-preserving source factors and cocycle. Thus arbitrary primitive-coordinate changes preserve the target-localized marked Keller incidence. Saturating the constant-denominator equations by det(g) gives exactly the diagonal torus, which is the known global source-target scaling. This isolates, but does not solve, the remaining global polynomial extension across D_g=0 and does not classify nonlinear polynomial self-equivalences outside the canonical factorization transport.

entries.title: Rank-four collision frames and projective cross-ratio defect
entries.scope: For every rank-four finite-etale cover E/S, the ordered-pair collision cover has rank twelve and pointwise stabilizer S_2, while Conf_3(E/S) is canonically the rank-24 S_4 frame torsor because three disjoint sections have a functorial rank-one complement. On that frame, for a primitive change u=q0+q1*r+q2*r^2+q3*r^3, signed-minor interpolation through the first three roots misses the fourth by -V_4(r)*Psi, where Psi=q2^2-q1*q3+q2*q3*e1+q3^2*e2. The numerator of labeled cross-ratio equality has the same factor, so one PGL_2 transformation matches all four roots exactly on Psi=0. The primitive boundary is independently Theta_4=product_(i<j)(q1+q2*(r_i+r_j)+q3*(r_i^2+r_i*r_j+r_j^2)); a primitive nonprojective quadratic witness and a primitive non-affine projective cubic witness are explicit. On the universal quartic inverse chart E=u4*pi^4*S^4+pi*S^3+b*S^2+S-c/2, the cleared projective equation is u4*pi^4*(q2^2-q1*q3)-pi*q2*q3+b*q3^2=0. Thus collision framing completely resolves finite S_4 labeling, but canonical projective root transport covers only this hypersurface. R4NP1 constructs the exact first-order and all-finite-order formal lift for an arithmetic-neutral nonprojective witness, excludes its straight target translation globally by a four-to-two fiber-orbit drop, and proves that every target self-equivalence through degree twelve is residual mu_5. Endpoint transport from degree thirteen onward and a full descent cocycle remain open.

entries.title: All-rank collision frames and projective Tschirnhaus descent
entries.scope: For every N>=3 and every rank-N finite-etale cover E/S, Conf_(N-1)(E/S) is canonically the full S_N frame torsor: the N-1 disjoint marked sections have a functorial rank-one complement. Over a characteristic-zero field, if A is rank-N finite etale and r,u are primitive coordinates, put W_r=span(1,r). Then u=(a*r+b)/(c*r+d) for a unique element of PGL_2 exactly when W_r intersects u*W_r nontrivially, equivalently when the four columns 1,r,u,r*u have rank at most three. On the primitive framed open, signed-minor interpolation through the first three roots reduces the determinantal ideal to N-3 residuals with independent differentials, so the projective locus is smooth of codimension N-3. For a normalized relation E=a0+S+a2*S^2+...+aN*S^N and u=q0+...+q_(N-1)*S^(N-1), the locus is cut out polynomially by the 4-by-4 minors of the explicit coefficient matrix for 1,S,q,aN*S*q. Rank three is automatic; in rank four its determinant is a4*(q2^2-q1*q3)-a3*q2*q3+a2*q3^2 and specializes exactly to the cleared universal-Keller cross-ratio defect. The split witness q=r+r^2 is primitive and nonprojective for every N>=4. This classifies canonical PGL_2 root transport, not arbitrary nonlinear Keller-incidence equivalences.

entries.title: Rank-four nonprojective Keller Kummer reduction, formal lift, and target-symmetry obstructions
entries.scope: For quartic quadratic-gauge maps over any characteristic-zero field K, the exact stable ground-field orbit criterion is ((b4/b3^4)/(a4/a3^4)) in K^(times 5), the Kummer form of the geometric mu_5 stabilizer. The primitive nonprojective change r -> r+r^2 on roots 1,2,3,4 has a separate nontrivial rational Kummer twist, while the split witness r=(-6,-3,0,3), u=r+r^2-18 is primitive, nonprojective, and arithmetic-neutral: its compressed seeds are -243/2 and -124416 with ratio 4^5. The explicit rational source-target scaling reduces it to the two regular fibers (-1/144,1/24,0) and (-1/144,1/96,-9) of the single determinant-one map F_(-124416). Their straight target line has inverse polynomial -(S-12)(S+12)(S^2+24S+108*lambda)/3456 and discriminant -(lambda+4)^2(3*lambda-4)^3/1358954496, so it is finite etale at both endpoints, but its constant two-sheet factor does not realize the required quadratic collision-frame labels. A label-preserving rational path has an exact divergence-free polynomial first-order source lift with coordinate degrees (55,53,55), term counts (512,510,612), and induced root velocity r^2-18 at all four reconstructed source points. Formal orbit triviality gives a unique lift to every finite order, with every finite jet represented by a polynomial SAut(A3) curve. The fixed-map target translation separately has a divergence-free first-order lift of degrees (31,29,31), but it cannot lift to a polynomial source automorphism: its -4 iterate sends the four-point start fiber to the exact two-point affine fiber with simple roots -36 and -12. This is an instance of the general fiber-orbit obstruction that every source-target intertwining preserves all scheme-theoretic fiber invariants along integer target orbits. The prime decorated discriminant has ordinary degree thirteen; after its residual mu_5 action is removed, every coordinate difference of a target self-equivalence is divisible by that prime equation. Thus every target self-equivalence through degree twelve is exactly in mu_5. The two endpoint targets are not in one mu_5 orbit, so any remaining endpoint target symmetry has degree at least thirteen. No degree-at-least-thirteen endpoint self-equivalence, prescribed-frame global transport, or full nonprojective descent cocycle is claimed.

entries.title: Rank-four nonprojective endpoint target-degree-eighteen obstruction
entries.scope: For the arithmetic-neutral fixed-map endpoint problem of R4NP1, every Q-defined target self-equivalence outside residual mu_5 has the form T=id+H*V, where H is the prime degree-thirteen ramified-discriminant equation. If deg(T)<=18, preservation of H modulo H^2 forces V(H)-QH-kappa=0 with deg(V)<=5. The exact logarithmic-system nullities for degree bounds zero through five are (0,0,0,0,1,7), and every solution has kappa=0. Since H(y_lin)=-1/16, the endpoint equation H(y_lin)V(y_lin)=delta has evaluation rank three and leaves four parameters. For T=id+HV, ten exact rational target evaluations of det(DT)-1 give cubic equations in those four parameters; their characteristic-zero Singular standard basis is [1]. Hence no polynomial target automorphism of degree at most eighteen can carry y_lin to y_1 in a left-right self-equivalence of F_(-124416), with or without the prescribed frame. Target degree nineteen and above, and the full nonprojective descent cocycle, remain open.

entries.title: Cyclic absolute no-go and uniform dihedral inverse-cover ledger
entries.scope: Every faithful transitive action of a nontrivial cyclic group is regular, so the Galois case of the characteristic-zero Jacobian theorem excludes cyclic generic inverse monodromy for every absolute polynomial Keller map. For the natural degree-n action of D_n, the Dickson incidence (a,u) -> (u,P_n(a,u)) has polynomial source and target invariant rings, Jacobian -J_n with J_n=partial_a P_n, reduced branch v^2-4u^n, and pullback P_n^2-4u^n=(a^2-4u)(J_n/n)^2. Over a fully split reflection field the etale source boundary-unit rank is 1+floor(n/2), while the target rank is one for odd n and two for even n; both open class groups vanish. The geometric orientation normalization is split for n=1 mod 4, is the A_(n-1) surface XY=u^n with class group Z/n for n=3 mod 4, and is A2 for even n. The suspension (a,u,z)->(u,P_n,z/J_n) has determinant -1 and preserves the degree-n dihedral cover. Any one-coordinate triangular polynomial suspension retaining the two cover outputs has determinant -J_n*A and cannot be Keller; odd-degree coupled affine modifications remain open, while the later KMFI2 theorem excludes every even-degree natural action absolutely in all dimensions. The exact checker replays the uniform polynomial identities through n=12, which is a regression certificate rather than the all-degree proof.

entries.title: Split D5 Cox-fill and affine-linear modification obstruction
entries.scope: Over a characteristic-zero field containing sqrt(5), J_5/5 factors as R_+ R_- and the reduced target branch pulls back with source boundary vector (1,2,2), while J_5 has vector (0,1,1). The two smooth ramification colors meet with multiplicity two. The product fill xy=R_+R_- is a normal singular threefold with class group Z and only constant units. Each one-color fill is A3, but leaves the other Jacobian color. The separated simultaneous fill is a factorial four-dimensional nondegenerate quadric cone with class group zero, constant units, and a unique singular vertex, so neither standard fill is affine space; free stabilization preserves the defects. More generally, for every r>=1, a map F(a,z)=h(a)+M(a)z over K[a] with r auxiliary variables and nonzero constant Jacobian has generic degree one. Applied over K=k(u), every polynomial D5 modification that retains u and is affine-linear in any number of auxiliary coordinates loses the degree-five function-field extension. Independently, any polynomial thickening that restricts to the original incidence on a source and target zero section has restricted determinant -J_5 det(M), even with arbitrary nonlinear auxiliary terms, and cannot be Keller. Thus a surviving construction must modify u, use nonlinear auxiliary dependence, and preserve the D5 field through nontrivial birational elimination rather than an unchanged polynomial section. This result does not construct an absolute Keller map.

entries.title: Nonlinear D5 affine-modification obstruction classification
entries.scope: For stable polynomial realizations of the split degree-five Dickson D5 extension with two or three auxiliary coordinates, eight necessary gates are separated: arithmetic monodromy, exact field degree, relocation of finite branch valuations, boundary log discrepancy, affine-space invariants, incidence-graph normal modules, inverse-adjugate divisibility, and complete regular fibers. Etaleness forces the target branch valuation and both index-two source ramification valuations not to retain corresponding finite divisorial centers. In the single-branch-supported factorization class, if the target exceptional determinant pulls back with order m times (1,2,2), constant Jacobian uniquely forces source orders (m,2m-1,2m-1), with m>=1 and primitive source ledger C*R_+*R_- against one target branch factor. The diagonal realization of that primitive ledger still has pole 1/(R_+*R_-). Every polynomial source/target graph carrying the old incidence is excluded by the restricted block determinant. Every polynomial incidence into the target branch factors geometrically through (U,V)=(s^2,+/-2s^5), with base differential rank one off the cusp and zero at it. These are necessary obstructions and a search classification, not a construction or a no-go theorem for the remaining nonlinear nonautomorphic branch-incidence stratum.

entries.title: Canonical D5 two-mask blowdown obstructions
entries.scope: The polynomial two-mask blowdown beta(U,V,A,B)=(U,V,V*A+2*U*B,2*U^4*A+V*B) is generically birational with determinant Delta=V^2-4*U^5 and inverse adjugate numerators V*S-2*U*T and -2*U^4*S+V*T. Any polynomial map whose first two outputs are (u_0,P_5(a_0,u_0)) for polynomial a_0,u_0 has determinant divisible by J_5, independently of nonlinear source dependence, so the fixed-base factorization cannot be Keller. For a constant linear rechart, the identity q^2-4*p^5=lambda*(V^2-4*U^5) forces p=c*U and q=d*V with d^2=c^5; inverse divisibility then forces the two mask rows into the span of the base rows. More generally, at every polynomial degree, p and q satisfying that identity cannot depend on any mask variable: specializing all other variables gives a polynomial A1-map to a smooth projective genus-two completion, which is constant by Riemann--Hurwitz. Exact division also rejects all 72 coordinate assignments from the unchanged primitive source chart and the two normalized ramification-incidence charts. The first nonautomorphic normalized-cusp chart p=V^2+Delta*S, q=2*V^5+Delta*T also fails in every degree: every fourth-coordinate contraction determinant is divisible by Delta, while the required log-crepant quotient is nonzero modulo Delta. Every tangential chart affine in one normal coordinate is degenerate by its top T coefficients. DNACO1 subsequently closes arbitrary nonlinear dependence on that one normal coordinate as well. Thus only two genuinely coupled normal directions or a different determinant-Delta blowdown remain in the canonical search. Neither remaining stratum is excluded here, and no Keller map is constructed.

entries.title: All-degree dihedral affine-completion obstructions
entries.scope: For every n>=3, the Dickson branch identity Delta_n(u,P_n)=(a^2-4u)(J_n/n)^2 gives a complete branch-supported log-Jacobian ledger. In odd degree, target order ell forces source orders (ell,2ell-1,...,2ell-1). In even degree n=2m, J_n/n=A_m B_m and the two target components pull back as P_n-2u^m=(a^2-4u)A_m^2 and P_n+2u^m=B_m^2, so independent target orders (ell_-,ell_+) force source orders (ell_-,2ell_--1,2ell_+-1) in the composite (C,A_m,B_m) basis. The canonical two-mask blowdown beta_n(U,V,A,B)=(U,V,V*A+2*U*B,2*U^(n-1)*A+V*B) has determinant Delta_n and explicit adjugate inverse. Fixed polynomial Dickson bases cannot be Keller by the chain rule. Any polynomial automorphic base rechart satisfying q^2-4p^n=lambda*(V^2-4U^n) is mask-independent, since each mask specialization maps A1 to a positive-genus curve. The normalized-cusp chart p=V^2+Delta_n*S, q=2V^n+Delta_n*T has an unavoidable contraction-divisor mismatch, and every tangential cusp chart affine in one normal coordinate is degenerate by its T^n and T^2 coefficients. More generally, any one-normal-coordinate log-crepant chart retaining the other two base coordinates must either be normal-independent or satisfy 2*deg_T(q)=n*deg_T(p) with cusp-shaped leading coefficients. If n is even, factorization at the resonant degree forces q=+/-2*p^(n/2), so the chart Jacobian is zero. If n is odd, adjoining w^2=p and comparing the infinity orders in w^(n-1)(y^2-1)=c*((partial w)*y'-w'*(partial y)), where y=q/(2w^n), forces y=+/-1 and again zero bracket. Thus the canonical one-normal-coordinate programme is excluded for every n>=3. The exact search compiler routes every one-normal degree pair to inactivity, a degree contradiction, even factorization, or odd infinity valuation; explicit resonant-looking false positives guard against treating 2*deg_T(q)=n*deg_T(p) as sufficient. These results do not exclude two coupled nonlinear directions or alternative determinant-Delta_n blowdowns, and do not construct a Keller map. The later KMFI2 theorem separately excludes every even-degree natural dihedral action without architectural restrictions; the unrestricted continuation therefore concerns odd degrees.
