entries.title: Full-box coefficient tangents and first raw obstructions for F4 through F6
entries.scope: For the explicit integer-root maps F_N with N=4,5,6 and the minimal full coefficient bounds d=12,17,22, the determinant-one coefficient schemes have respectively 1365,3420,6900 variables and exact rational tangent dimensions 58,88,123. The normalized seed tangents have ranks 1,2,3 and unique source trivializers of maximum degrees (25), (30,35), and (35,40,45). In each degree an explicit bounded-box tangent has a nonzero quadratic class in coker(L_F), so the first nonzero raw bounded-box Kuranishi order is two. These claims concern the raw coefficient schemes; they do not identify radicals, local components, or stable-moduli tangent spaces.

entries.title: Complete quartic raw quadratic Kuranishi map
entries.scope: At the integer-root quartic map in X(3,12), exact rational relation tracking gives tangent dimension 58 and quadratic Kuranishi rank 53 from 1711 polarized pairs; 727 pair classes are nonzero and use 338 canonical cokernel monomials. The determinant-preserving affine left-right orbit has rank 22, four target shears raise the displayed reduced-family rank to 26, and the normalized seed raises it to 27. This proves an explicit reduced subfamily, not that its closure is an irreducible component or that the ambient local ring is nonreduced.

entries.title: Generic reduced coefficient-family tangent profiles
entries.scope: For N=4,5,6, adjoining the allowable target shears C^k in the first two outputs to the normalized seed family and the affine left-right orbit gives explicit reduced-family tangent ranks 27,30,33. At selected rational points, exact rational elimination gives full coefficient-scheme tangent dimensions 49,80,109, leaving transverse tangent excesses 22,50,76. Tangent excess alone does not decide whether it is nilpotent, reduced, or a mixture, and does not prove that the displayed families are components.

entries.title: Good-prime source-degree contact profiles for F4 through F6
entries.scope: Modulo 32003, the unique source-only trivializers adj(DF_N)G exhaust the full bounded-box tangent spaces at source-degree cutoffs 33,48,63 for N=4,5,6. The visible seed quotients disappear at cutoffs (25), (30,35), and (35,40,45); these individual seed degrees already have exact rational certificates in CSK1. Those latter obligations remain with OP-CCDM even after a rational profile certificate.

entries.title: All-degree formal-versus-algebraic location of stable moduli
entries.scope: For every N>=4, the fixed-Jacobian deformation functor of F_N modulo unrestricted polynomial source jets is the one-point functor on local Artin algebras, so no finite unfiltered Kuranishi order detects stable parameters. On a nonempty reduced boundary-clean seed open, decorated normalization is stable-left-right invariant and has image dimension N-3. Thus the N-3 stable parameters first occur at the exact reduced global-boundary level. The optimal two-sided filtered complexity growth and uniform no-algebraization theorem remain open.

entries.title: HC4 projective-gradient Segre formula and low-degree numerical atlas
entries.scope: For a four-variable potential of degree d with gradient degree m=d-1, the projective compactification whose top degree equals the affine gradient's generic degree is Gamma=[X0^m:(partial_1 Psi)^h:...:(partial_4 Psi)^h], not in general the full polar map of the homogenized potential. Its infinity base scheme has no divisorial component, and if i_*s(B,P4)=sum sigma_k H^k then g_i=m^i-sum_(k<=i) binom(i,k)m^(i-k)sigma_k, in particular deg_aff(grad Psi)=m^4-6m^2 sigma_2-4m sigma_3-sigma_4. Positivity, degree bounds, and log-concavity leave respectively 9, 7, 72, 67, 319, and 307 necessary integral Segre signatures for m=2,3,4 and affine degree 2,3; zero-dimensional bases have forced lengths 14,13,79,78,254,253. A smooth-curve-only quadratic-gradient base is numerically possible only for affine degree two with degree/genus (4,0), and is impossible for affine degree three. Cotangent lifts preserve the plane map's generic degree, so a hypothetical geometric-degree-four packet has aggregate correction m^4-4. The Meng--Yang HC6/HC5 controls have generic degree three and aggregate corrections 7^6-3=117646 and 13^5-3=371290; Schur descent preserves the generic fiber count by an exact Keller-linear solve. The equation R(P)=0 alone does not determine a Segre class, as an all-degree constant-Hessian automorphism family shows. The atlas gives necessary numerical configurations only: it does not prove their existence, classify schemes by Hilbert polynomial, compute every individual Meng--Yang Segre degree, or settle HC4.

entries.title: Quadratic-gradient HC4 infinity-base exclusion
entries.scope: Let Psi be a characteristic-zero four-variable potential whose gradient has polynomial degree at most two and whose Hessian determinant is a nonzero constant. Then grad(Psi) is a quadratic Keller map, so Wang's degree-two theorem makes it a polynomial automorphism. Its affine generic degree is therefore one, and the infinity Segre degrees satisfy 24*sigma_2+8*sigma_3+sigma_4=15. Consequently all nine quadratic-gradient affine-degree-two signatures and all seven affine-degree-three signatures in HC4PPG1 are empty. In particular, neither the length-14 nor the length-13 zero-dimensional infinity base scheme can occur, and no quadratic-gradient HC4 counterexample exists. This is an intersection-theoretic consequence of Wang's theorem, not a new proof of that theorem or a classification of quadratic gradient automorphism base schemes.

entries.title: Cubic-gradient HC4 infinity-base exclusion and degree lower bound
entries.scope: Let Psi be a characteristic-zero four-variable potential of degree at most four with constant nonzero Hessian determinant. Any gradient collision can be translated at its midpoint and have its common gradient subtracted, giving Psi=q2+h3+h4 with q2 nondegenerate and a nonzero antipodal critical pair. HC4CQ1 excludes that pair, so grad(Psi) is injective over the algebraic closure; Ax--Grothendieck makes it a polynomial automorphism. For cubic gradients the infinity Segre degrees therefore satisfy 54*sigma_2+12*sigma_3+sigma_4=80. Consequently all 72 cubic-gradient affine-degree-two signatures and all 67 affine-degree-three signatures in HC4PPG1 are empty, including the length-79 and length-78 zero-dimensional rows. Together with HC4PPG2, any HC4 counterexample potential has degree at least five, equivalently gradient degree at least four. This is a projective restatement of HC4CQ1 plus Ax--Grothendieck, not a new proof of either theorem or a classification of cubic gradient automorphism base schemes.

entries.title: Quintic leading-Hessian coverage and cubic Schur gap
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h5 be a collision-normalized four-variable potential with constant nonzero Hessian determinant, and let r be the generic rank of Hess(h5). Gordan--Noether gives a constant kernel K of dimension 4-r. For r=1,2,3, the highest remaining determinant face is det(C_r)*det(Hess(h4)|K)=0 in lambda-degree 8+r. Rank zero has h5=0 and is closed by HC4CQ1. In rank three, with kernel direction t, the first face gives D_t^2 h4=0; writing s3=D_t h4, the next face is det(C_3)*D_t^2 h3-grad(s3)^T*adj(C_3)*grad(s3)=0. The aligned branch s3=0 reaches HC4CD5 and is closed. The nonaligned branch is exactly a ternary quintic--cubic Schur divisibility problem with degree-nine denominator, degree-ten numerator, and linear quotient. Ranks one and two remain constant-kernel synchronization problems. Independently, positivity and log-concavity leave 319 affine-degree-two and 307 affine-degree-three projective signatures for gradient degree four, split by leading base codimension as (260,58,1) and (249,57,1) in codimensions two, three, and four; the isolated codimension-four lengths are 254 and 253. Under the additional assumption that the whole base is one smooth integral curve, the Segre genus formula and Castelnuovo bound leave 18 rows for each affine degree. No general signature-level exclusion is claimed because the projective degrees do not currently determine the leading Hessian rank or kernel alignment.

entries.title: Squarefree rank-three quintic Hessian obstruction
entries.scope: In the rank-three nonaligned branch of HC4PPG4, put C=Hess_u(h5) for the ternary quintic h5 and d=grad(s3) for the ternary cubic s3=D_t h4. If Delta=det(C) is squarefree, the Schur divisibility Delta | d^T adj(C)d forces adj(C)d to vanish modulo every irreducible component of Delta: at its generic point C has corank one and its nonzero symmetric rank-one adjugate turns the scalar equation into the square of one pairing. Hence Delta divides adj(C)d. But Delta has degree nine while adj(C)d has degree eight, so adj(C)d=0; the identity C*adj(C)=Delta*I then gives d=0 and s3=0. HC4CD5 closes the branch. Thus every nonaligned rank-three quintic candidate has nonsquarefree ternary Hessian determinant. The explicit quintic x^5+y^5+z^5+x^4*y+y^4*z+z^4*x has a degree-nine Hessian determinant coprime to its three partial derivatives, proving the squarefree locus is nonempty and the remaining nonsquarefree condition is proper. No classification of that exceptional locus or signature-level exclusion is claimed.

entries.title: Universal quintic top-gradient/Rees support sieve
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h5 be a collision-normalized degree-five HC4 candidate. The universal four-variable h5 has 56 coefficients; its four quartic derivatives satisfy six curl relations, Euler sum x_i partial_i h5=5h5, Hess(h5)x=4 grad(h5), and the usual Koszul relations. The top constant-determinant face det Hess(h5)=0 removes generic rank four. After the low-dimensional Gordan--Noether constant-kernel reduction, the essential rank-r top forms for r=1,2,3 have 1,6,21 coefficients. On the open locus where the essential hypersurface is smooth, the active gradient ideal is a regular sequence of linear type; its Rees ideal has only Koszul equations, padded zero coordinates give linear target equations, and adding X0^4 gives an equal-degree complete intersection of codimension r+1. The pure-top calibration vectors are g=(1,4,0,0,0),(1,4,16,0,0),(1,4,16,64,0) and sigma=(0,16,-128,768),(0,0,64,-768),(0,0,0,256). These are degeneration calibrations, not completed constant-Hessian Segre vectors. For the actual completed base, the reduced support is the join of the kernel vertex P^(3-r) with Sing(h5=0). This support statement is the n=4,m=4 specialization of PGS3; on a singular component, PGS3 shows that the missing multiplicity is governed by the transverse Jacobian length and the finite k[[X0]]-module rank/torsion profile of the lower active gradients. Hence rank one has leading base codimension two; a squarefree essential binary rank-two top has codimension three and a repeated root has codimension two; a ternary rank-three top has codimension four when smooth, codimension three for isolated singularities, and codimension two for a positive-dimensional singular locus. Intersecting with the HC4 atlas leaves respectively (260,249), (58,57), and (1,1) rows in codimensions two, three, and four for affine degrees two and three. In codimension four the only signatures are (0,0,0,254) and (0,0,0,253). Midpoint collision parity additionally gives grad(h2+h4)(a)=0 and grad(h3+h5)(a)=0. This top-support theorem alone does not exclude a row; HC4PPG7 subsequently uses the lower vertex filtration to exclude both codimension-four rows.

entries.title: Smooth rank-three quintic vertex-colength obstruction
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h5 be a collision-normalized degree-five HC4 candidate whose leading Hessian has essential rank three, with constant kernel coordinate t, and suppose the essential ternary quintic h5(u)=0 is smooth. This is the (n,m,r)=(4,4,3) specialization of PGS2. Its three quartic partial derivatives define an Artinian complete intersection B of length 64, Hilbert series (1+z+z^2+z^3)^3, and socle degree nine. The first determinant face gives h4=t*s3(u)+r4(u). On the vertex chart t=1, the three active homogenized gradient components define a one-dimensional Cohen--Macaulay algebra finite flat of rank 64 over k[[epsilon]], so after quotienting by epsilon^4 its algebra A has associated graded B tensor k[epsilon]/(epsilon^4) and length 256. In the nonaligned branch s3 is a nonzero cubic, hence not a socle element and dim(B*s3)>=2. The missing gradient component has initial form epsilon*s3, so length(A*G_t)>=3*dim(B*s3)>=6. Since the full vertex base has length sigma4=256-delta, the exact sequence gives affine gradient degree delta=length(A*G_t)>=6. The aligned branch s3=0 is already excluded by HC4CD5. Therefore every such candidate has affine degree at least six; in particular, no affine-degree-two or affine-degree-three HC4 candidate has a smooth essential rank-three quintic top, and the two codimension-four signatures g=(1,4,16,64,2),(1,4,16,64,3), equivalently sigma=(0,0,0,254),(0,0,0,253), are empty. Exact Fermat and deformed Macaulay2 calculations calibrate the length mechanism but are not substituted for the universal flatness/socle proof.

entries.title: Codimension-three quintic gradient-stratum sieve
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h5 be a collision-normalized degree-five HC4 candidate in a codimension-three top-gradient packet. In essential Hessian rank two, let K be the constant kernel plane and assume the squarefree essential binary quintic h5 has h4|K nonzero. The rank-two determinant face det Hess_K(h4)=0 makes h4|K a fourth power. After normalizing it to t^4 and working over the active quotient field, the exact Hessian coefficient ideal contains powers a02^2,a11^3,a03,a12,a21^3, so a constant kernel direction w satisfies D_w^2 h4=D_t D_w h4=0. The lambda-degree-nine face is det(C) D_w^2 h3-grad_U(s3)^T adj(C) grad_U(s3)=0, with C=Hess_U(h5) and s3=D_w h4. If the degree-six binary Hessian determinant det(C) is squarefree, rank-one adjugate divisibility makes det(C) divide the degree-five vector adj(C)grad_U(s3), forcing that vector, grad_U(s3), and D_w^2 h3 to vanish; HC4CD5 closes the branch. The squarefree locus is nonempty. On the nonsquarefree remainder, the generic transverse active algebra has length 64 and a kernel-gradient component is epsilon times a unit, so the full generic transverse length and leading Segre multiplicity are sigma3=16. This is the (n,m,r)=(4,4,2) unit-penultimate specialization of PGS2. Thus only g=(1,4,16,48,2),(1,4,16,48,3), equivalently sigma=(0,0,16,-2),(0,0,16,-3), can occur in that subpacket. The branch h4|K=0 remains open. In essential rank three, at every isolated singular point p with rank Hess(h5)(p)=2, homogeneity and symmetry give adj(Hess(h5)(p))=c*p*p^T; evaluating the Schur face and using Euler for s3 forces s3(p)=0. Points with Hessian rank at most one are not constrained by this value-level argument. No codimension-three atlas row is excluded unconditionally because the exceptional rank-two and rank-three packets remain.

entries.title: All-dimensional projective-gradient Segre machinery and lift calibrations
entries.scope: For every degree-m polynomial self-map F of A^n, the actual affine-map compactification is Gamma_F=[X0^m:F_1^h:...:F_n^h]. If i_*s(B,P^n)=sum_(k=1)^n sigma_k H^k, then its projective degrees and signed Segre degrees are inverse triangular transforms g_i=m^i-sum_(k<=i) binom(i,k)m^(i-k)sigma_k and sigma_i=m^i-g_i-sum_(k<i) binom(i,k)m^(i-k)sigma_k. When F is dominant, g_n is its affine generic degree and the weighted total correction is m^n-g_n. For an actual gradient, the leading tuple is curl-free, reconstructs the top potential by Euler's identity, and cuts out the singular support of one homogeneous hypersurface at infinity; in characteristic zero there is no fixed divisor, so sigma_1=0. Executable constructors keep Gamma_Psi separate from the full polar map. Exact Macaulay2 calibrations show that the cotangent lifts of (x+y^r,y) for r=2,3 change (1,r,1) to (1,2,3,2,1) and (1,3,5,3,1), while one quadratic stabilization changes (1,r,r,r,1) to (1,r,r,r,r,1). Thus cotangent lift and stabilization preserve the top affine degree in these families but not the interior multidegrees. The registry attaches complete vectors, top-degree-only controls, or explicit open records to the triangular, cotangent, Meng--Yang/Schur, and HN families without promoting boundary normalization, Hessian rank, or a collision count to an individual Segre class. Curl gives a realization condition on leading base-ideal generators, not by itself a forbidden numerical Segre vector. No new Keller-map exclusion or componentwise Schur/cotangent transport theorem is claimed.

entries.title: All-dimensional smooth-essential gradient normal slice
entries.scope: Let F=grad(Psi):A^n->A^n have degree m>=2, and suppose the top homogeneous potential h_(m+1) depends on exactly r<n essential variables and defines a smooth hypersurface in P^(r-1). The reduced infinity support along the kernel is the linear vertex V=P^(n-r-1), of base codimension r+1. At its generic point, the active Jacobian algebra B is the Artinian complete intersection of the r degree-m partial derivatives, with Hilbert series (1+z+...+z^(m-1))^r, length m^r, and socle degree r(m-1). The compactifier-truncated active algebra has associated graded B tensor k[epsilon]/(epsilon^m) and length m^(r+1). If a missing kernel-gradient component has initial form epsilon^q*s with 1<=q<m and nonzero s in B, its ideal removes at least (m-q)*dim(B*s), hence sigma_(r+1)<=m^(r+1)-(m-q)*dim(B*s). If the penultimate layer h_m restricts nontrivially to V, a missing component is epsilon times a unit and sigma_(r+1)=m^r exactly. If V is a point, then the affine gradient degree is at least (m-q)*dim(B*s), and at least 2(m-q) when s is not in the socle. The theorem controls the generic leading Segre multiplicity only: it does not determine later Segre components, singular essential tops, or componentwise behavior under cotangent and Schur lifts. HC4PPG7 and the normal-slice part of HC4PPG8 are respectively its (4,4,3) and (4,4,2) specializations.

entries.title: Radical finite-fiber theorem for slice-LND ideal images
entries.scope: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, B=k[x,s], D=partial_s, and I a radical zero-dimensional ideal. Then D(I) is a Mathieu--Zhao subspace. More strongly, if f^m lies in D(I) for every m>=1, then g*f^m lies in D(I) for every g and every m>=1. Zero-constant integration identifies membership with equality of primitive values on each vertical fiber; the one-variable polynomial moment lemma forces f to vanish identically on every fiber containing two points. LND-ZDF extends this to arbitrary zero-dimensional ideals, LND-MCF closes positive-s-degree monic carriers, and LND-NDD closes the normalized repeated degree-drop carrier. The checker verifies a six-point reduced complete intersection, the generic membership kernel in a fixed degree window, and powers through order twelve; those bounded computations are regressions, not the all-order proof.

entries.title: Monic-carrier finite-residual theorem for slice-LND images
entries.scope: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, B=k[x,s], D=partial_s, and I=qJ, where q is monic of positive s-degree and J=B or B/J has finite length, with no reducedness assumption. Then D(I) is a Mathieu--Zhao subspace. If q has two distinct roots over the algebraic closure of k(x), primitive evaluation and the one-variable moment lemma force every pure-power seed to be zero. If q has one root, q=(s-alpha(x))^d; translation reduces to t^d, and primary decomposition of J shows that off-carrier components force vertical-line vanishing while on-carrier components acquire linearly growing local order. Hence every fixed mixed multiplier enters D(I) eventually. Together with LND-ZDF and LND-NDD, this leaves only more complicated nonmonic leading-coefficient divisors, local-slice plinth saturation, and nonslice LNDs open in this program. The checker replays two nonreduced length-two residual charts for q=s^2 through order twelve; the all-order proof is written.

entries.title: Arbitrary zero-dimensional theorem for slice-LND ideal images
entries.scope: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, B=k[x,s], D=partial_s, and J any zero-dimensional ideal. Then D(J) is a Mathieu--Zhao subspace. For a primary component Q at P, either Q contains a polynomial slice s-phi(x), so D(Q)=B, or every Q-element has zero s-derivative at P and pure membership forces f(P)=0; local order then proves eventual mixed membership. Components on distinct x-fibers are patched by Hermite interpolation. If one x-fiber contains several support points, reduction to the radical interval-moment theorem forces x-a to divide f, and powers enter every primary component on that fiber. This removes all carrier-free finite residual schemes, including nonreduced ones, from the counterexample search. The checker replays both primary branches through order twelve; the all-order proof is written.

entries.title: Normalized repeated nonmonic degree-drop theorem
entries.scope: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, B=k[x,s], D=partial_s, p=xs-1, and I=x^c p^d J for c>=0 and d>=1, where J=B or B/J has finite length supported at (0,0). Then D(I) is a Mathieu--Zhao subspace. The canonical primitive at the rational root s=1/x defines the support weight w(f)=min_j(v_x(f_j)-j). Polynomiality of every pure-power quotient and the one-variable moment lemma force w(f)>=1, while root multiplicity forces p^(d-1) to divide f. For every fixed g, both the p-order and x-support weight of g*f^m then grow linearly; the fixed x-content loss does not affect eventual entry into J. The exact bounded compiler tests (c,d)=(0,1),(0,2),(1,1), three primary residual schemes, 256 sparse seeds, and six multipliers; it finds 58 pure-prefix survivors and no bounded mixed-tail obstruction. The search is a regression/candidate audit, not the all-order proof.

entries.title: Bounded plinth-divisor ideal-image search
entries.scope: For the linear locally nilpotent derivation D=x*partial_y+y*partial_z of Q[x,y,z], the local slice y/x has plinth element x and 2*x*z-y^2 is invariant. Exact rational linear algebra constructs D(I_n) degree by degree for five homogeneous ideals crossing x=0. Among 45 monomial/binomial homogeneous seeds, pure powers through six leave 13 survivors; every noncontrol survivor is visibly divisible by x, and none gives a mixed-tail obstruction through exponents four to six for g in {1,x,y,z}. This is a bounded negative search and support-cone diagnostic, not an all-order theorem or a proof of the LNED conjecture for this derivation. It redirects the counterexample search to nonhomogeneous triangular LNDs or reducible plinth divisors.

entries.title: Exact bounded linear and nonlinear reducible-plinth ideal-image search
entries.scope: For D_r=x*(x-1)*partial_y+y^r*partial_z on Q[x,y,z], r=1,2, assign weights wt(x)=0, wt(y)=1 and wt(z)=r+1. Each D_r lowers weight exactly by one, so membership in D_r(I) at fixed weight is an exact finite module calculation over Q[x]. Five coupled ideals leave respectively fourteen and seventeen six-power survivors, all divisible by x*(x-1), with no bounded mixed-tail obstruction. The grading-breaking perturbation D=x*(x-1)*partial_y+(y^2+x)*partial_z is handled by normalizing primitives modulo the kernel k[x,3*x*(x-1)*z-y^3-3*x*y], lifting a bounded primitive over Q[x], and testing its class in the finite kernel image modulo I. Across eight ideals, including three non-weight-homogeneous jet charts, and 350 mixed-weight seeds, it leaves 48 chartwise survivors representing seven distinct forms; all are divisible by x*(x-1), and none has a bounded mixed-tail obstruction for g in {1,x,x-1,y,z}. Individual membership decisions are exact, but the exponent ranges are bounded, so this is not an all-order theorem or counterexample. It redirects the search to the crossing plinth uv=0 for D=uv*partial_y+(y^2+u)*partial_z on four variables.

entries.title: Exact bounded crossing-plinth ideal-image search
entries.scope: For D=u*v*partial_y+(y^2+u)*partial_z on Q[u,v,y,z], the plinth equation u*v has intersecting components and W=3*u*v*z-y^3-3*u*y is invariant. Leading-weight normalization modulo Q[u,v,W], a Singular module lift over Q[u,v], and a finite quotient/kernel-image calculation decide every tested membership exactly. Five zero-dimensional crossing ideals and 956 sparse seeds, including quadratic base coefficients, invariant combinations, and images of ideal generators, leave 177 chartwise six-power survivors representing 36 distinct forms. Every survivor is divisible by u*v, no bounded mixed-tail obstruction occurs for g in {1,u,v,y,z}, and every tested seed not divisible by u*v fails by its square. The exponent ranges are bounded, so this is neither an all-order theorem nor a counterexample. It redirects the search to a genuinely nonprincipal plinth ideal, beginning with D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y.

entries.title: Exact bounded nonprincipal-plinth ideal-image search
entries.scope: For D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y on Q[u,v,x,y], the kernel is Q[u,v,w] with w=u*y-v*x and the plinth ideal is nonprincipal. Exact homogeneous module lifts over Q[u,v] and finite quotient closure under u,v,w decide each tested membership. Five zero-dimensional ideals meeting (u,v), 1,055 sparse seeds, and pure powers through six leave 494 chartwise survivors representing 100 distinct forms. Every survivor lies in the base-support cone (u,v)A, no bounded mixed-tail obstruction occurs for g in {1,u,v,x,y,w}, and every tested seed outside (u,v)A fails its first power. The exponent windows are bounded, so this is not an all-order theorem or counterexample. All five displayed ideals contain (u,v)^3, so LND-NPF independently proves them safe at every order. These bounded experiments are retained regressions; a remaining nonprincipal counterexample must lie outside plinth-power saturation.

entries.title: Nonprincipal plinth-power saturation LNED theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y] over a characteristic-zero field, D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, and p=(u,v). The grading by total (u,v)-degree gives Im(D) intersect p^N=D(p^(N-1)) for every N>=1: low-degree components of any primitive are kernel elements and can be subtracted. The published rank-at-most-two four-variable linear-derivation theorem makes Im(D) Mathieu-Zhao. If p^q is contained in an ideal I and powers of f eventually lie in D(I), then primality of p forces f into p; hence g*f^m lies in Im(D) intersect p^m eventually and therefore in D(p^(m-1)), which is contained in D(I) for m>=q+1. Thus D(I) is Mathieu-Zhao for every I with p contained in radical(I). This includes I=(u,v,ell(x,y)) for every nonzero linear form ell and all nilpotent plinth-supported thickenings. It does not treat ideals such as (x), whose invariant image modulo I has positive module rank.

entries.title: Exact bounded positive-dimensional nonprincipal-plinth search
entries.scope: For D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, five ideals retain a free y-direction: (u,v,x) and four nilpotent or tilted plinth jets. The images of u,v,w=u*y-v*x are nilpotent in each quotient, so the kernel-image span and each membership decision are exact without truncating y-degree. Among 1,055 seeds, pure powers through six leave 289 chartwise survivors representing 75 distinct forms. Every survivor lies in (u,v)A, every tested seed outside that cone fails its first power, and no bounded mixed-tail obstruction occurs for g in {1,u,v,x,y,w}. The checker verifies the free-line coefficient-functional identity through total degree eight and the plinth-filtration identity through total degree seven. The exponent windows are bounded regressions, while LND-NPF independently proves all five ideals safe to every order.

entries.title: Exact bounded principal-conductor valuation-face search
entries.scope: For A=Q[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, and I=(x), the invariant ring Q[u,v,w] with w=u*y-v*x maps modulo I to Q[u,v,u*y]. Hence a primitive residue lies in the invariant image exactly when every monomial u^a*v^b*y^c satisfies a>=c. This gives an exact, untruncated membership test. Among 1,055 seeds, pure powers through six leave 48 survivors, all divisible by u; no bounded mixed-tail obstruction occurs for g in {1,u,v,x,y,w}, and every failed seed has pure-prefix length at most one. Of the survivors, 43 are y-free, thirteen are invariant, and four touch the slope-zero face. Every survivor lies in u*ker(D)[x], and LND-PCG proves all 48 safe to all orders. The checker also verifies over Q(sqrt(-15)) an exact failure of the proposed square gate: the homogenized face p(t)=2*t-1+(sqrt(-15)/3)*(6*t^2-6*t+1) gives f,f^2 in D((x)) but f^3 not in D((x)). Thus it is a finite-prefix obstruction, not an LNED counterexample. It verifies the local-slice identity T(D(x*y*a))=(u*y)*a used by the exact two-branch criterion and the aligned/crossed identities D(u*x*a)=u*D(x*a), D(u*y*a)=u*D(y*a). For q_1=u*x+w, normalization of A/(q_1) gives the exact support criterion a>=2*c; seventeen seeds survive powers four through six, all in u*ker(D)[q_1], with no bounded mixed-tail obstruction. For q_(1,1)=u*v*x+w, the exact cone is a>=2*c and b>=c; eight seeds survive powers four through six, all in u*v*ker(D)[q_(1,1)], with no bounded mixed-tail obstruction. The exponent windows remain bounded; the independent all-order conclusions are LND-PMI, LND-MLT, LND-GTR, LND-LIC, LND-RRL, and LND-TPR. LND-CPM subsequently closes every nonzero principal ideal for this model. The unproved model frontier is genuinely nonprincipal ideals outside the plinth-power theorem, not another principal-conductor search.

entries.title: Principal-conductor strict and local-slice polynomial cone theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, I=(x), and B=ker(D)=k[u,v,w] with w=u*y-v*x. Define omega(f) as the minimum of a-c over support monomials u^a*v^b*x^d*y^c. For every fixed g, g*f^m lies in D(I) for all sufficiently large m if ord_u(f)>deg_y(f), or if ord_v(f)>deg_x(f) and omega(f)>0. These cases follow from finite Neumann-series inversions using zero-constant x- or y-integration. More generally, the conclusion holds for every f=u^r*F with r>=1 and F in B[x]. In the local slice s=x/u, write g=sum b_j*s^j over B_u and F^m=sum c_(m,k)*u^k*s^k. Termwise integration has summands b_j*c_(m,k)*u^(r*m-j-1)*x^(j+k+1)/(j+k+1), which are polynomial and divisible by x for large m. This larger normal form subsumes the strict cones and proves all 48 survivors of LND-PCD safe to all orders. LND-PMI proves that the eventual pure-power hypothesis always forces this normal form.

entries.title: Moving-linear principal-ideal LNED theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y] over a characteristic-zero field and D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y. Then D((ell(x,y))) is Mathieu-Zhao for every nonzero linear form ell. More strongly, eventual membership f^m in D((ell)) implies eventual mixed membership g*f^m in D((ell)) for every fixed g. After reducing to ell=x and embedding A in B_u[x], B=k[u,v,w] with w=u*y-v*x, exact membership is T(h) in u*A for T(h)=x^(-1)*integral_0^x h dt. If the lowest u-order of f is r=-q<=0, its leading face F is divisible by z^q for z=w+v*x, while membership of the powers forces T(F^m) to be divisible by z^(q*m+1). In the z-coordinate this is the vanishing of integral_0^w Phi(t)^m dt for every sufficiently large m. Applying the one-variable polynomial moment lemma to Phi^M for one sufficiently large M forces Phi=0, a contradiction. Thus r>=1, so f lies in u*B[x], and LND-PCG supplies the mixed tail. A simultaneous GL_2 change gives every nonzero ell. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.
dependencies: external: one-variable polynomial moment lemma (Sun-Wang 2024, Lemma 2.2)

entries.title: Moving-linear thickening LNED theorem
entries.scope: For A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, every nonzero linear form ell(x,y), and every d>=1, D((ell^d)) is Mathieu-Zhao. After reducing to ell=x, D(x^d*A) is contained in x^(d-1)*A, so eventual pure-power membership forces x to divide f. LND-PMI gives a primitive P_m in x*A for each eventual mixed target g*f^m, while x|f makes that target divisible by x^m. If P_m=x^r*a and D(P_m) is divisible by x^r, reduction of D(P_m)=r*u*x^(r-1)*a+x^r*D(a) modulo x^r forces x|a. Iterating from r=1 through d puts P_m in x^d*A. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.

entries.title: Generic two-root principal-carrier theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, B=ker(D)=k[u,v,w] with w=u*y-v*x, and L=Frac(B). If a nonzero carrier q in A, viewed in the local-slice polynomial ring L[x], has at least two distinct roots over the algebraic closure of L, then the eventual-power radical of D(q*A) is zero. Indeed, a primitive q*a_m of f^m vanishes at two distinct roots alpha,beta, so integral_alpha^beta f(t)^m dt=0 for every sufficiently large m. Applying the one-variable polynomial moment lemma to f^M for one sufficiently large M forces f=0. Consequently D((x*y)) and D((x*(x-1))) are Mathieu-Zhao. For q=x*y the exact criterion is T(h)/(u*y) in A, and the checker verifies T(D(x*y*a))=(u*y)*a in the local slice. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.
supersedes_notes: the reducible carriers (x*y) and (x*(x-1)) as live counterexample charts

entries.title: Linear invariant-content principal-carrier theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, and B=ker(D)=k[u,v,u*y-v*x]. For every a in {u,v} and ell in {x,y}, D((a*ell)) is Mathieu-Zhao. It suffices by simultaneous exchange to treat (u*x) and (u*y). Since u is invariant, D(u*x*A)=u*D(x*A) and D(u*y*A)=u*D(y*A). In the aligned case, eventual pure membership and LND-PMI force f=u*F with F in B[x]; the local-slice proof of LND-PCG accepts the fixed multiplier g/u because f^m clears its one extra u-denominator. In the crossed case, pure membership gives u|f and the y-version of LND-PMI gives f=v*F with F in B[y]. Injectivity of B[y]/(u)=k[v,w,y] into A/(u)=k[v,x,y] under w->-v*x yields F=u*H, hence f=u*v*H. In the slice t=y/v, the factors u^(m-1)*v^m clear all fixed coefficient and substitution denominators in the primitive of g*f^m/u, which is polynomial and divisible by y for large m. Multiplication by u completes both cases. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.
supersedes_notes: the aligned and crossed invariant-content carriers (u*x) and (u*y) as live counterexample charts

entries.title: Rational-root monomial-ladder principal-carrier theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y] over a characteristic-zero field, D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, w=u*y-v*x, and q_n=u^n*x+w for n>=1. Then D(q_n*A) is Mathieu-Zhao. In B_u[q_n], B=k[u,v,w], one has x=(q_n-w)/u^n, y=(v*(q_n-w)+u^n*w)/u^(n+1), and D=u^(n+1)*partial_(q_n). If the lowest u-order of f is r<=0, the actual lowest associated-graded face of the zero-constant primitive of f^m is divisible by q_n-w. Evaluation at q_n=w produces all sufficiently large moments integral_0^w F(s)^m ds=0, and the one-variable polynomial moment lemma gives a contradiction. Thus r>=1 and f lies in u*B[q_n]; its growing u^m content clears every fixed denominator in the mixed primitive. Exactly, normalization of A/(q_n) by x=u*t and y=-(u^n-v)*t sends w to -u^(n+1)*t, so a primitive residue is invariant-correctable iff every monomial u^a*v^b*t^c satisfies a>=(n+1)c. For n=1, the exact bounded search retains seventeen of 1,055 seeds on powers four through six; all seventeen lie in u*B[q_1], and no bounded mixed-tail obstruction occurs. The census is bounded; the ladder conclusion is an independent internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.
supersedes_notes: the monomial rational-root carriers u^n*x+(u*y-v*x) as live counterexample charts

entries.title: Two-prime monomial rational-root principal-carrier theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y] over a characteristic-zero field, D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, w=u*y-v*x, and q_(r,s)=u^r*v^s*x+w for r,s>=1. Then D(q_(r,s)*A) is Mathieu-Zhao. Normalization of A/(q_(r,s)) by x=u*t and y=-(u^r*v^s-v)*t sends w to -u^(r+1)*v^s*t, giving the exact primitive-residue support cone a>=(r+1)c and b>=s*c. In B_(uv)[q_(r,s)], independent lowest-face arguments at u and v show that eventual pure-power membership forces positive order at both primes: f lies in u*v*B[q_(r,s)]. The factor (u*v)^m then clears the fixed u- and v-denominators of every mixed primitive. For q_(1,1)=u*v*x+w, the exact bounded search retains eight of 1,055 seeds on powers four through six; all eight lie in u*v*B[q_(1,1)], and no bounded mixed-tail obstruction occurs. The checker verifies normalization identities for 1<=r,s<=3. The census is bounded; the two-prime grid conclusion is an independent internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.
supersedes_notes: the tied monomial rational-root carriers u^r*v^s*x+(u*y-v*x) as live counterexample charts

entries.title: Monomial invariant slope with arbitrary invariant intercept theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y] over a characteristic-zero field, D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, B=ker(D)=k[u,v,u*y-v*x], and q=u^r*v^s*x+b with r>=1, s>=0, and arbitrary b in B. Then D(q*A) is Mathieu-Zhao. For b nonzero, writing delta=q-b in B_(uv)[q], the lowest-u face moment argument forces f to have positive u-order; when s>=1, the independent lowest-v face forces positive v-order. Thus eventual pure-power membership puts f in u*B[q] for s=0 and in u*v*B[q] for s>=1, which clears every fixed mixed-primitive denominator. For b=0, D(q*A)=u^r*v^s*D(x*A); divisibility supplies the required u and v content, while the moving-linear theorem supplies the B[x] normal form and accepts the fixed multiplier denominator. This is an internal proof, depends on the one-variable polynomial moment lemma, and has not been externally reviewed.
supersedes_notes: translated monomial-slope rational-root carriers as live counterexample charts

entries.title: Complete coprime invariant-slope theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, B=ker(D)=k[u,v,w], and q=a*x+b for arbitrary nonzero coprime a,b in B. Then D(q*A) is Mathieu-Zhao. For each irreducible factor pi of a other than u, the lowest pi-face of the zero-constant primitive is divisible by q-b; coprimality makes the endpoint b mod pi nonzero, and the one-variable moment lemma forces positive pi-order of every eventual-power seed. The u-face gives the same conclusion when u divides a. When u does not divide a, its face root is beta=(b mod u)-(a mod u)*w/v. If beta is nonzero, the moment lemma forces positive u-order. If beta is zero, the equality v*(b mod u)=(a mod u)*w is equivalent to q lying in u*A; then D(q*A) is contained in u*A, so eventual pure membership directly forces u to divide the seed. In every case the accumulated radical content clears u*a and every fixed mixed denominator. Only a nontrivial common invariant factor of a,b remains outside this theorem. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.
supersedes_notes: all coprime nonmonomial invariant slopes, including aligned conductor descent, as live counterexample charts

entries.title: Complete invariant-linear principal-carrier theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, B=ker(D)=k[u,v,w], and q=a*x+b for arbitrary a,b in B with a nonzero. Then D(q*A) is Mathieu-Zhao, without a coprimality assumption. The abstract scaling lemma says that if M is a Mathieu-Zhao subspace of a domain and c*M is contained in M, then c*M is Mathieu-Zhao: from eventual f^m in c*M, choose one large N and apply the Mathieu property of M to the fixed multiplier g*f^N/c. Writing c=gcd(a,b) and q=c*q_0, LND-GCS or the moving-linear theorem makes M=D(q_0*A) Mathieu-Zhao. Since c is invariant, D(q*A)=c*M and M is a B-module, so the scaling lemma applies. This closes every degree-one carrier already presented in the generic B[x] slice. LND-IAC supplies the intrinsic denominator descent and multiplicity step for all remaining one-root principal carriers. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.
supersedes_notes: common invariant content of a generic linear carrier as a remaining principal obstruction

entries.title: Invariant-affine carrier and thickening theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, and B=ker(D)=k[u,v,w]. If H is a noninvariant irreducible polynomial with D^2(H)=0, then D(H*A) is Mathieu-Zhao. Writing s=D(H)=b_1*u+b_2*v gives H=b_0+b_1*x+b_2*y and embeds A in B_s[H]. At each irreducible pi dividing s, one of u,v is a unit in B_(pi), and the corresponding inverse coordinate is unit*(H-beta_tilde)/s. Every negative pi-face is therefore divisible by H-beta. The endpoint beta cannot vanish, because the inverse identities would imply H in pi*A, contradicting irreducibility and noninvariance. Eventual pure powers and the one-variable polynomial moment lemma force positive pi-order at every denominator prime, which clears the primitive of every fixed mixed multiple. If h lies in ker(D^2) minus ker(D), then h=c*H with c in B and one such H; divisibility bootstrapping proves D(H^d*A) Mathieu-Zhao for every d>=1, and the Mathieu scaling lemma restores c^d. The checker replays the invariant-affine coordinate identities but not the all-order moment argument. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.

entries.title: Complete principal-ideal theorem for the rank-two linear model LND
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y] over a characteristic-zero field and D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y. Then D(q*A) is Mathieu-Zhao for every nonzero q in A. If q is invariant, this follows from the plinth-power theorem for D(A) and Mathieu scaling. Otherwise view q over Frac(ker(D)) in the generic orbit coordinate. Two or more distinct roots give zero eventual-power radical by LND-GTR. With one root, UFD factorization and A_u=B_u[x] show that q=c*H^d with c invariant and H the unique noninvariant irreducible factor of generic degree one; equivalently D^2(H)=0. LND-IAC handles H^d and scaling removes c. This closes all principal ideals only for this model derivation. Genuinely nonprincipal ideals outside the existing finite-residual and plinth-power theorems, and general locally nilpotent derivations not reducible to this two-slice normal form, remain open. The proof is internal, unformalized, and has not been externally reviewed.

entries.title: All-dimensional singular-gradient stratum and DVR-torsion law
entries.scope: Let grad(Psi):A^n->A^n have degree m>=2, let its top potential depend on r<n essential variables, and let C be an irreducible component of dimension s and degree d in the projective singular locus of the essential top hypersurface. The corresponding reduced infinity component is Join(P^(n-r-1),C), of dimension n-r+s, codimension r-s in P^n, and degree d. At its generic point let B_C be the transverse top Jacobian algebra of length mu_C. The active lower-layer gradient quotient is a finite module over R=K[[epsilon]] and therefore has a unique DVR profile R^rho direct-sum_j R/(epsilon^a_j), with rho plus the number of torsion summands equal to mu_C. After adjoining epsilon^m its exact active length is L_C=m*rho+sum_j min(m,a_j). Quotienting by the epsilon-divisible missing kernel gradients leaves a final transverse length lambda_C satisfying mu_C<=lambda_C<=L_C<=m*mu_C, and the component contributes d*lambda_C to sigma_(r-s). If rho=0 and every torsion order is one, or if a missing component is epsilon times a unit, the contribution is exactly d*mu_C. If the active module is flat, a missing initial form epsilon^q*s gives the sharper upper bound d*(m*mu_C-(m-q)*dim(B_C*s)). Without flatness, the torsion orders are essential. The repeated-root binary quintic h5=x^3*y^2 has mu_C=2, while h4=0, x*y^3, and y^4 give active profiles of truncated lengths 8, 3, and 2 for m=4, proving that singular-locus dimension, Hessian rank, and transverse top multiplicity do not determine the Segre contribution. HC4PPG9 applies the order-one active law to binary root partitions. The theorem does not compute the DVR profile for the remaining HC4 singular packets or determine later Segre components.

entries.title: Six-variable quartic HN Waring-rank rigidity through rank nine
entries.scope: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, no essential six-variable homogeneous quartic Hessian-nilpotent polynomial has Waring rank at most eight. At rank nine, every essential quartic HN polynomial has polynomially invertible gradient map z -> z-grad(P). Consequently every essential six-variable quartic HN counterexample has Waring rank at least ten. In rank ten, the HN trace identities exclude every projective Gale parallel class of multiplicity at least four and every pair of distinct triple classes. Thus every remaining rank-ten candidate has parallel-class multiplicity at most two except possibly one triple class. The finite codimension-two Gale, one-latitude rank-nine, complementary-minor, and rank-ten parallel-obstruction calculations are exact SymPy checks; the coordinate-free trace, matroid base-packing, Hesse, and Witt-index arguments are written proofs. QHNW1 does not prove the residual cyclic-complement matroid lemma or a rank-eleven lower bound, and it has not received external mathematical review.

entries.title: Rank-ten Gale-matroid survivors and the nonsimple trace obstruction
entries.scope: The cyclic-complement lemma formerly proposed in OP-QHNW10 is false: U_(4,6) direct-sum U_(0,4) is a literal characteristic-zero counterexample, and duplicating the first three columns of the displayed seven-point family K_simp(a,b), with realization scheme Spec Q[a,b,1/(ab(a-1)(b-1))], gives a loopless rational counterexample. The literal loop survivor cannot support a rank-six Gram matrix satisfying the first two HN traces because its four free Waring covectors would span a totally isotropic four-plane. Relative to the rank-four catalogues through nine simple points distributed by matroid-database 0.3, the complete loopless nonsimple slice has 37 coloured survivor types over 17 simplifications. Two normalized realization ideals are the unit ideal over Q and the remaining 35 types have rational points. Every one of those 35 types contains a six-element rank-two Gale flat. On its four-dimensional kernel the first trace forces the six Gram diagonal entries to vanish, the second trace forces the whole Gram block to vanish, and the six-dimensional Witt bound excludes every rank-six Gram matrix on the type. The checked-in script freezes and replays the returned catalogue records but does not regenerate the external catalogue. This result does not enumerate simple rank-four matroids on ten elements, construct a rank-ten HN counterexample, or raise the Waring lower bound to eleven, and it has not received external mathematical review.

entries.title: Rank-ten Gale-loop census and 103-type closure
entries.scope: Relative to the rank-four matroid catalogues through nine simple points distributed by matroid-database 0.3, the complete Gale-loop slice has 115 coloured abstract survivor types over 66 simplifications. Three normalized realization ideals are the unit ideal over Q, removing four coloured types; the other 63 simplifications have exact rational points, leaving 111 characteristic-zero types. If there are at least two Gale loops, Gale duality splits the Waring covectors into complementary spaces of dimensions at most four, so Hessian determinant factorization and the characteristic-zero Hesse theorem in at most four variables exclude all 66 such types. For a one-loop type, the first two HN traces require a nonzero self-square vector in the active Gale kernel. A realization-independent cyclic-support and Witt-index inequality excludes 16 of the 45 characteristic-zero one-loop types. At an exact rational realization of every one-loop type, ten coordinate-square maps have full rank and the other 35 projective self-square ideals are the unit ideal; projectivity therefore excludes the self-square incidence on a nonempty Zariski-open realization set in every type. Exact realization-open saturation in all five projective kernel charts closes 21 of the 29 special-locus types. Thus 103 of 111 characteristic-zero loop types are closed for every realization and all 45 one-loop types are generically closed, while eight special types remain. The checker freezes and replays the external catalogue records but does not regenerate the catalogue. This result does not close those eight types or the simple ten-point branch, construct a rank-ten HN counterexample, or raise the Waring lower bound to eleven, and it has not received external mathematical review.

entries.title: Complete closure of the rank-ten Gale-loop branch
entries.scope: Starting from the eight characteristic-zero one-loop types left by QHNW3, the active Gale matroid of catalogue type (7,70) with colour 1111113 is disconnected and splits the Waring polynomial into essential summands of dimensions 3, 2, and 1, so Hessian determinant factorization and low-dimensional Hesse exclude it. Exact Singular standard bases over Q give unit realization-plus-self-square saturations for types (7,3)/1111113, (8,581)/11121111, (9,188841)/111111111, and (9,188846)/111111111. Each of the final types (7,0)/1111113, (7,1)/1111113, and (7,2)/3111111 has a unique possible self-square support disjoint from its triple Gale class. On the triple-class slice, independence of four trace quadratics kills the three Gram diagonals and independence of seven trace quartics kills the three mutual Gram entries. The triple Waring vectors and the independent isotropic Gale-loop vector would then span a totally isotropic four-plane in a nondegenerate six-space, contradicting Witt index three. Consequently all 45 characteristic-zero one-loop types and all 111 characteristic-zero Gale-loop types are impossible. Together with QHNW2 this leaves only the simple ten-point branch of the rank-ten matroid search. This result does not enumerate that simple branch, construct a rank-ten HN counterexample, or raise the Waring lower bound to eleven, and it has not received external mathematical review.

entries.title: Complete simple rank-ten Gale census and Waring-rank-eleven lower bound
entries.scope: Relative to the complete rank-four nine-element catalogue distributed by matroid-database 0.3, exact modular-cut enumeration scans all 190,214 deletion types, including all 185,981 simple types. The cocircuit and cyclic-complement constraints leave 13 residual deletion types. Exact Z3 enumeration gives 23 catalogue-extension models and exact abstract isomorphism testing gives five simple rank-four ten-point matroids, distinguished by basis counts 114, 110, 108, 105, and 90. Their normalized realization ideals over Q are respectively (x3-x2), (0), (0), (0), and (0), with exact rational points on every realization open set. Thus the cyclic-complement lemma is false even under simplicity. Every survivor contains a six-point rank-two Gale flat. On its four-dimensional supported value space, six coordinate squares and fifteen off-diagonal square-pairs are independent throughout the realization open set, so the first two Hessian traces force the full Gram block on that flat to vanish. Gale duality makes the corresponding Waring span four- or five-dimensional, contradicting Witt index three in a nondegenerate six-space. Hence no rank-six Gram survivor exists and no essential six-variable quartic HN polynomial has Waring rank ten. Combined with QHNW1, QHNW2, QHNW3, and QHNW4, every essential six-variable quartic HN counterexample has Waring rank at least eleven. The catalogue regeneration remains relative to the external database; the checked-in verifier freezes and exactly replays the generated census. This result does not construct a counterexample, enumerate rank-eleven Gale matroids, or prove six-variable injectivity, and it has not received external mathematical review.

entries.title: Rank-ten simple-matroid gate
entries.scope: Resolved by QHNW5. Exact modular-cut enumeration gives five characteristic-zero realizable simple rank-four ten-point survivors, so the cyclic-complement lemma remains false even under simplicity. Every survivor has a six-point rank-two Gale flat whose first-two-trace Gram block vanishes throughout the realization open set; Gale duality and Witt index exclude all five rank-six Gram branches. No nonradial collision test is reached. Combined with QHNW1, QHNW2, QHNW3, and QHNW4, this closes every rank-ten branch and raises the Waring-rank floor for an essential six-variable quartic HN counterexample to eleven.

entries.title: Binary root-partition Segre sieve
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h5 be a collision-normalized degree-five HC4 candidate whose top quintic has essential Hessian rank two and is a singular binary form. At a root p of multiplicity e>=2, the two top partial derivatives have transverse orders e-1 and e, so the transverse Jacobian algebra is K[x]/(x^(e-1)) and has length e-1. Assume at every repeated root that, after eliminating the leading transverse active equation, one redundant active gradient component has initial form epsilon times a unit. Then the active DVR profile consists of e-1 order-one torsion summands, and PGS3 gives component contribution e-1. If the binary quintic has q distinct roots, sigma2=sum_p(e_p-1)=5-q. Essential rank two excludes the pure fifth power, leaving partitions 2+1+1+1 with sigma2=1, 3+1+1 and 2+2+1 with sigma2=2, and 4+1 and 3+2 with sigma2=3. Their affine-degree-two/three atlas intersections contain respectively 51/50, 44/43, and 37/36 rows. Thus the generic double-root packet shrinks from 260/249 codimension-two rows to 51/50 on this open lower-layer stratum. The theorem excludes no row unconditionally: failure of the active-unit condition is a proper higher-X0-torsion stratum, and its constant-Hessian determinant faces remain open.

entries.title: All-degree squarefree top-Hessian obstruction for direct HC4
entries.scope: Let Psi be a characteristic-zero four-variable polynomial of degree D>2 with constant nonzero Hessian determinant, and suppose the top homogeneous Hessian has generic rank three. Gordan--Noether gives a constant top-kernel direction and a ternary top form f. The first two scaled determinant faces force the transverse diagonal to vanish at first order and then impose q*det(Hess(f))=grad(a)^T*adj(Hess(f))*grad(a). If det(Hess(f)) is squarefree, the generic corank-one rank-one-adjugate argument makes adj(Hess(f))*grad(a) divisible by the full determinant. The resulting polynomial quotient is homogeneous of negative degree, so the assumed first nonzero off-diagonal motion must vanish; hence the entire off-diagonal block is zero, and the required t-adic determinant order is at most D-2 rather than 4(D-2), a contradiction. Hence every rank-three top cone of a hypothetical HC4 counterexample has nonsquarefree ternary Hessian determinant. This is the all-degree direct-filtration version of HC4PPG5; it does not treat top-Hessian rank at most two or classify the nonsquarefree locus. The checker replays only the first two block-determinant identities; the universal quantifier is discharged by the written squarefree-divisibility and degree proof. Its cleanup mode hash-checks the committed identity artifact without symbolic replay or rewriting it.

entries.title: Repeated-linear top-Hessian gates for direct HC4
entries.scope: Continue HC4DIR2 on a rank-three ternary top cone with det(Hess(f))=ell^e*R, where ell is linear, R is squarefree, and gcd(ell,R)=1. Exact multiplicities e=2 and e=3 admit no four-variable constant-Hessian completion in degree at least five. The exact-multiplicity-four lower-rank boundary and both generic-corank-one and lower-rank exact-multiplicity-five boundaries are empty. For e=6 every generic-corank-one motion order is empty, including the normal, delayed two-/three-root, and outer boundary-rank-two packets. On its lower-rank boundary, synchronization removes the x^2 jet and reduces the sole pure-power survivor to a degree-five order-one resonance with common top f=C*z*ell^4+h5(ell,y) and pure-cube pivot. Its order-two scalar-parent realization is HC4-safe by HC4RSD12. Thus the remaining rank-three inputs are that order-one resonance, a linear factor of multiplicity at least seven, a nonlinear repeated factor, or several distinct repeated factors; top-Hessian rank at most two remains separate. The checker verifies the all-degree determinant, valuation, normal-form, and terminal-channel identities, while the UFD/DVR divisibility and maximal-channel arguments are written proofs. No unrestricted HC4 conclusion is claimed.

entries.title: Exact-sextuple pure-cube scalar-parent closure
entries.scope: Continue HC4DIR27 on its sole lower-rank degree-five order-one exact-sextuple resonance. Every four-variable completion has scalar-parent form Psi=H+w*P+eta*w^2/2 with cubic pivot top P3=kappa*ell^3. The graph-coordinate factorization of HC4RSD12, one dimension lower, then reduces every collision fiber to HC2. Thus the exact-sextuple order-one scalar-parent resonance is collision-free. entries.title: Nonreduced Hessian--Schur module normalization gate
entries.scope: Continuing the nonsquarefree frontier of HC4DIR2, let C be a symmetric 3-by-3 matrix of ternary degree-r forms with nonzero determinant Delta, and let d have degree r-1 with Delta dividing d^T*adj(C)*d. The cokernel of C is self-dual with twist 2r, and the adjugate is its symmetric pairing. On every irreducible component Q where C has generic corank one, the local Smith form forces the kernel coordinate of d halfway into the nonreduced thickening. Let P be the componentwise-minimal denominator clearing C^(-1)*d, rho=deg(P), and e=P*C^(-1)*d. Then P^2 divides Delta and e has degree rho-1. On the normalization of every component Q dividing P, let K_Q be the saturated kernel line and B_Q the divisor where the induced rank-two form drops rank. One has K_Q^2=O(B_Q-2r), and the nonzero residue of e gives deg(B_Q)>=2*deg(Q)*(r+1-rho). For the ternary-quintic packet r=3, 1<=rho<=4. Hence either rho=4 and Delta=P^2*ell with ell linear, or rho<=3 and every essential denominator component carries the stated positive corank-two defect. On the rho=4 packet the Schur problem is equivalently det(C)=P^2*ell, C*e=P*d, and d^T*e=P*a for a linear form a; Hessian and gradient integrability are imposed afterward. This is a structural reduction, not an exclusion or construction of an HC4 counterexample. Generic corank-two and corank-three Smith strata, including the radial sextic calibration, remain separate.

entries.title: Exact septuple-linear Hessian--Schur exclusion
entries.scope: Continue HC4NHM1 and HC4DIR27 on the generic-corank-one ternary-quintic Schur stratum det(Hess(h5))=ell^7*R2, with R2 squarefree and coprime to ell. If ell is essential in the minimal denominator clearing C^(-1)*d, its pole order b is 1, 2, or 3. On the normalized line, the saturated kernel is O(-kappa), the corank-two defect has length 6-2*kappa, and the nonzero cleared residue forces 0<=kappa<=b-1. Hence exactly six (b,kappa,defect) rows occur: (1,0,6), (2,0,6), (2,1,4), (3,0,6), (3,1,4), and (3,2,2). On the extremal (3,2,2) row the primitive kernel is a basepoint-free triple of binary quadratics. If its image is a projective line, Hessian integrability either drops the boundary Hessian to rank at most one or forces ell to have determinant multiplicity exactly one. Thus every repeated-line survivor on this row has a nondegenerate conic kernel. In boundary jets h5=F5+ell*G4+ell^2*H3/2+ell^3*J2/6+..., writing the conic kernel as (a,b,c), one has det(Hess(F5))=lambda*a^2 and the first-normal coefficient forces a^2 to divide 2*a*(b*H_y+c*H_z)+(b,c)*Hess(G4)*(b,c)^T; when it does, J2 is unique. On repeated-root binary quintics, the square-Hessian condition leaves the partitions 4+1, 3+2, 3+1+1, and 2+2+1, together with one exceptional 2+1+1+1 orbit characterized by (t^2-t+1)^3/(t^2*(1-t)^2)=25/4. On the squarefree stratum, an exact saturated factorization elimination gives a reduced degree-twelve marked scheme; all points form one PGL2 orbit, represented by F=u^5+v^5, whose Hessian is 400*u^3*v^3. Solving the complete tangent-kernel spaces for every repeated-root type and for the Fermat orbit shows that all but the 4+1 case have a common quadratic kernel factor; the primitive 4+1 family is killed by its first-normal remainder. Hence the extremal (3,2,2) row is empty. The same moving-line-image argument applies to primitive degree-one kernels and makes both defect-four rows empty. The three remaining constant-kernel rows split into transverse and tangent directions. The transverse direction successively kills every normal jet and makes det(C)=0. In the tangent direction, exact determinant faces either make the x^7 coefficient vanish or force it to be a scalar multiple of a square linear form, contradicting the squarefree residual quadratic. Hence the complete exact-septuple generic-corank-one packet with squarefree coprime cofactor is empty. Multiplicity eight/nine are outside this theorem and are subsequently closed by HC4NHM3. The nonsquarefree residual-quadratic incidence is subsequently classified by HC4NHM4 and excluded from four-variable prolongation by HC4NHM5; lower-Smith boundaries remain open.

entries.title: Octuple/nonuple linear Hessian--Schur exclusion
entries.scope: Continue HC4NHM1--2 on the generic-corank-one ternary-quintic Schur strata det(Hess(h5))=x^8*ell, with ell a line coprime to x, and det(Hess(h5))=x^9. If x is essential in the minimal denominator, the pole order is at most four. The saturated kernel degree kappa satisfies 0<=kappa<=min(b-1,3), giving ten pole/kernel/defect rows for either multiplicity. The moving-line and conic gates of HC4NHM2 eliminate every row with kappa one or two. The only new row is (b,kappa,defect)=(4,3,0). Its primitive kernel has either line image, already excluded, or nondegenerate rational-cubic image. In the latter case the binary boundary quintic has perfect-square Hessian. The complete square-divisor classification leaves only root types 4+1 and 3+2. Solving their boundary kernel equations forces a common factor in all three kernel entries, contradicting primitivity. Thus every positive-degree kernel row is empty. A transverse constant kernel is already incompatible with x^7 divisibility. For a tangent constant kernel, the determinant coefficient ladder through x^7 makes the entire quintic independent of the kernel variable once x^8 divides the determinant, so the determinant is zero. Hence both exact-multiplicity-eight and exact-multiplicity-nine generic-corank-one packets are empty before the gradient and scalar cleared-Schur equations are imposed. Equivalently, this closes the one-component partition P=x^4 of the clean quartic-denominator packet det(C)=P^2*ell. The next historical partition was P=x^3*y, with determinant incidences x^7*y^2, x^6*y^3, and x^6*y^2*z; HC4NHM4--6 subsequently classify and close all three. HC4NHM7--8 close the 2+2 and 2+1+1 partitions, and HC4NHM9--12 close the squarefree partition. Thus every split-linear clean quartic denominator is closed; clean nonlinear components, positive-defect packets, and lower-Smith boundaries remain open.

entries.title: Two-line quartic-denominator Hessian--Schur classification
entries.scope: Continue the clean generic-corank-one quartic-denominator branch of HC4NHM1 with minimal denominator P=x^3*y and determinant incidence det(Hess(h5))=x^7*y^2. On the septuple component, the global cleared vector has degree three. HC4NHM2 excludes kernel degrees one and two, while the defect-free cubic-kernel calculation of HC4NHM3 excludes degree three; the kernel is therefore constant. The transverse constant kernel is impossible, and the tangent determinant ladder gives the complete boundary h5=A*x*y^4+x^4*(B*y+Gamma*z)/24+D*x^5/120, with A*Gamma nonzero and determinant -A*Gamma^2*x^7*y^2/3. For this family, Schur divisibility first forces the z-component of d=grad(s3) to vanish and then reduces the adjugate quadratic form to -Gamma^2*x^6*d_y^2/36. Gradient integrability gives the complete Schur space s3=a*x*y^2+b*x^3, with quotient d^T*adj(C)*d/det(C)=a^2*x/(3*A). For a nonzero, the primitive cleared vector e=x^3*y*C^(-1)*d has nonzero residues on both lines and no common factor, so the minimal denominator is exactly x^3*y; for a=0 it drops to x. Thus the first two-component clean packet is nonempty and completely classified. In the four-variable rank-three face, it forces partial_t^2(h3)=a^2*x/(3*A), hence the term a^2*x*t^2/(6*A). No lower determinant face, constant-Hessian completion, collision, or HC4 counterexample is claimed by this theorem; HC4NHM5 subsequently excludes every genuinely two-component prolongation at the next determinant face. The residual-line incidence types x^6*y^3 and x^6*y^2*z are outside this theorem and subsequently closed by HC4NHM6; other quartic partitions, positive-defect packets, and lower-Smith boundaries remain open.

entries.title: Two-line quartic-denominator first-prolongation obstruction
entries.scope: Continue the explicit clean P=x^3*y, det(Hess(h5))=x^7*y^2 packet of HC4NHM4 in four variables (x,y,z,t). Write h4=t*s3+r4 with arbitrary ternary quartic r4. The Schur face forces h3=a^2*x*t^2/(6*A)+t*Q2+r3, with arbitrary ternary quadratic Q2 and cubic r3, and let h2 be an arbitrary four-variable quadratic. For the scaled Hessian M(lambda)=lambda^3*Hess(h5)+lambda^2*Hess(h4)+lambda*Hess(h3)+Hess(h2), the lambda^10 coefficient vanishes exactly by the HC4NHM4 Schur identity. In the complete lambda^9 face, the coefficient of x^8*t is -Gamma^2*a^3/(54*A). It is independent of B,D,b and every coefficient of r4,Q2,r3,h2. The only lambda^9 contribution involving h2 is det(Hess(h5))*(h2)_(tt), proportional to x^7*y^2, so it cannot alter the witness. Since A*Gamma*a is nonzero precisely on the genuinely two-component channel, no such leading packet prolongs to a four-variable constant-Hessian potential. Collision equations are not used. This closes the x^7*y^2 incidence inside the clean P=x^3*y partition; HC4NHM6 subsequently closes the x^6*y^3 and x^6*y^2*z incidences at the ternary Hessian boundary. entries.title: Squarefree quartic-denominator synchronization frontend
entries.scope: Continue HC4NHM1 after the HC4NHM8 exclusion. On the clean generic-corank-one packet with squarefree quartic minimal denominator P=L1*L2*L3*L4, every component has pole order one, so the residue bound forces saturated kernel degree zero and hence a constant kernel direction vi. The identity Hess(h5)*vi=grad(D_vi(h5)) makes the constant-kernel condition equivalent to D_vi(h5) lying in (Li^2). If vi is tangent to Li, symmetry automatically gives Li^2 dividing det(Hess(h5)). If vi is transverse, a local normal form has h5=F5+x^3*J2+x^4*K1+c*x^5 and first determinant coefficient 6*J2*det(Hess(F5)); generic corank one therefore makes the double determinant factor equivalent to the sharper condition D_vi(h5) in (Li^3). entries.scope: In the published regular J4 moving-frame system, the adapted graph Hessian is B=[[-b,-a,0],[-a,0,0],[0,0,0]] and the selected projective differential has determinant pq. entries.title: HC4 degree-101 bound, proper-power endpoint and degree-48 marked-graph exclusion
entries.scope: Using HCTANG2 and only Moh plane JC through maximum component total degree100, every four-variable constant-Hessian potential of degree at most101 has an automorphic gradient. Degree102 is also covered when the highest homogeneous part is a nonzero scalar times a proper power: in cotangent coordinates that power is independent of the fibres, forcing both coefficient degrees at most100. These assertions descend to characteristic zero by uniqueness of the formal inverse. More generally, for S=Hess(f) with nonzero constant determinant, emptiness over the algebraic closure of the projective constant-covector scheme v^T*adj(S(X))*v=0 implies invertibility. A nonautomorphic gradient necessarily admits a nonzero constant rank-one quadratic determinant-preserving direction, because the cotangent inverse Hessian has zero base/base block. Nonemptiness alone gives no counterexample. For the explicit v2 Meng--Yang potential Psi=A^2+13*A+2*B, complete support degrees by r-power are14,10,6, giving deg(Psi after r=R)<=max(14,2*deg(R)+6). Every polynomial graph of degree at most48 containing both marked points is excluded from having a nonzero constant Hessian determinant: the degree48 endpoint has square top and the graph chain rule transfers the collision independently of all graph first derivatives. Also excluded are arbitrary polynomial pullbacks of degree at most7 mapping distinct parameter points to the marked points with matching pulled-back gradient covectors; an affine p-coordinate suffices for that jet condition. This degree argument alone does not address unmarked constant-determinant graphs, graph degree>=49 or higher-degree/rational Schur/coisotropic reductions. It does not resolve unrestricted HC4 or JC2. entries.title: All-degree polynomial-graph affine-plane obstruction and nonrational formal model
entries.scope: For the scaled Meng--Yang Psi=L*A^2+M*A+N*B with L*N nonzero and any polynomial graph r=R(x,y,p,q) in characteristic zero, f_R admits no two-dimensional constant vector plane along which it is jointly affine. This elementary result uses no Tang theorem or plane JC input. On x=0 the fixed slice is L*p^2+M*p+N*(4*y^2*p+y*q), so a direction (0,b,c,d) with zero second directional derivative forces b=c=0. The exact identity x^2*B+(2-3*x*y)*A=u*(u+1)*p+2*x*(2*u+1)*q then proves deg_q(f_R)=2*deg_q(A_R)>=2 over K(x,y,p): A_R,q=x*(3*u^2-x^2*R_q) is nonzero by reduction modulo x. This excludes the last q direction and hence every affine plane. A separate explicit formal graph satisfies Psi_R=F=L*p^2+M*p+4*N*y^2*p+N*y*q+kappa*x*p, with det Hess(F)=(N*kappa)^2. Its quadratic equation L*x^5*R^2+C_R*R+D_R=0 has unit implicit derivative2*N and discriminant linear in q, with coefficient -12*L*N*x^3*(x*y+2), so its unique formal solution is nonrational. For every j>=2 its first q^j coefficient occurs at x order3*j-5 and equals (N/L)*binomial(1/2,j)*(-6*L/N)^j, nonzero; this is an all-order nontermination proof, not an inference from a finite jet. HC4MYGJ2 identifies it with the unique constant-determinant formal branch for its trace. At v2,kappa1 the graph component contains both marked points but is ramified there; the graph equation has R derivative0 and q derivative3, forbidding a regular graph through either. Full symbolic identities and nine normal coefficients were checked, with an independent radical expansion on the y=p=0 regression slice. The elementary arguments apply in every characteristic-zero field. No polynomial graph with unit Hessian is excluded merely by this elementary part; its global invertibility consequence requires the separately registered structural theorem. Formal verification, external review and novelty priority are not claimed.

entries.title: Complete all-degree standard polynomial-graph collision exclusion
entries.scope: For every polynomial R(x,y,p,q) of arbitrary degree and every scaled Meng--Yang Psi=L*A^2+M*A+N*B with L*N nonzero in characteristic zero, if the standard graph pullback f_R=Psi(x,y,p,q,R) has nonzero constant Hessian determinant, its gradient is a polynomial automorphism. HC4MYGAP1 excludes every jointly affine constant vector two-plane, while the external Tang structural alternative reproduced in HCTANG2 would supply exactly such a plane for a nonautomorphic gradient. Uniqueness of the formal inverse descends the complex conclusion to every characteristic-zero field. In particular no polynomial graph in this chart can produce any gradient counterexample, and for v2=(L,M,N)=(1,13,2) no graph containing both marked points can have nonzero constant Hessian determinant: the common ambient gradient has zero r component, so its collision transfers independently of all graph first derivatives. This closes the complete standard polynomial-graph collision route inside OP-HC4-SCHUR and replaces the degree48 marked-graph frontier of HCTANG3, without any plane degree bound or assumption of JC2. It does not exclude every unmarked constant-determinant graph. The statement uses the standard coordinates x,y,p,q up to constant affine changes; arbitrary nonlinear reparameterizations, other eliminated-coordinate graph charts, non-graph embeddings, rational Schur pivots and general coisotropic reductions remain outside it. OP-HC4-SCHUR, JC2 and unrestricted HC4 remain unresolved. The conclusion depends on the external structural theorem; its no-plane prerequisite and formal nonrationality example are elementary independent results. No full formal verification, external review, explicit inverse for every member or novelty priority is asserted.

entries.title: All-degree affine-plane obstruction for triangular and base-independent Keller dual substitutions
entries.scope: Let Psi=L*A^2+M*A+N*B be the scaled Meng--Yang family in characteristic zero, with L*N nonzero. For arbitrary polynomial R(x,y,P,Q), the reparameterized four-variable potential has no jointly affine constant vector two-plane in any of three classes: p=a*P+G(x,y),q=b*Q+H(x,y,P); p=a*P+H(x,y,Q),q=b*Q+G(x,y); or p=p(P,Q),q=q(P,Q) with nonzero constant plane Jacobian. The first two allow every polynomial G,H and every nonzero constant a,b. The third includes arbitrary base-independent dual automorphisms and all their alternating words; only the polynomial inverse Jacobian matrix is used, not a polynomial inverse map. The elimination identity completes the potential to L*U^2+alpha*p+Gamma*q-K0^2/(4L), where Gamma is affine and alpha quadratic in y. Immutable mixed jets have x^2 residues6*b and6*a, while polynomial graph corrections enter at x^3; polynomial-degree additivity excludes every affine x-invisible direction that moves y in the triangular classes. The first order excludes all remaining pure-dual directions. In the opposite order, a possible affine direction forces H(0,y,Q)=h*Q+h0(y); a hypothetical plane then transports its coefficient from x=0 to C=N*b*(y-eta*x), while restriction to u=0 forces C=2*N*b/x, giving the impossible identity eta*x^2+3=0. An explicit opposite-order positive control has one affine direction, so the plane argument cannot be replaced by exclusion of every individual direction. For the base-independent Keller class, exact slice identities give delta_second(p)=0, delta_second(q)=-16*delta(p), then delta(p)=0 and delta(q)=-4*p; invertibility of the polynomial Jacobian matrix contradicts the resulting nonunit directional ideal. Pure-dual directions die by the same ideal and polynomial-degree argument. The Hessian chain rule retains its full second-derivative term; a determinant-one coordinate change need not preserve unit Hessian. Exact marked-gradient pullbacks are -grad(p)/2, so nonlinear parameterizations require an actual jet match. The elementary all-degree theorem uses neither Tang nor a plane JC bound. Its coefficient, degree and two-divisor exhaustion is written; universal identities and controls are checked exactly. Base-dependent alternating words, nonlinear base changes, other graph charts and general mixed/coisotropic operations are outside this theorem. No formal verification, external review or novelty priority is claimed.

entries.title: All-degree gradient invertibility after triangular or base-independent Keller dual substitution
entries.scope: For every potential in any of the three all-degree polynomial-dual-substitution classes of HC4MYGT1, a nonzero constant four-variable Hessian determinant implies that its gradient has a polynomial inverse. The elementary theorem excludes every constant affine fibre two-plane, while the external Tang structural alternative reproduced as HCTANG2 would supply one for a nonautomorphic gradient. The conclusion descends from C to every characteristic-zero coefficient field using the unique formal inverse. Thus neither one triangular dual change in either order with arbitrary base-dependent polynomial coefficients, nor any base-independent plane Keller substitution (including arbitrary polynomial dual automorphisms and constant-coefficient alternating words), can produce a gradient counterexample through r=R of any polynomial degree. This uses no plane degree bound and does not assume JC2 or invertibility of the dual Keller map. Marked ambient-point containment alone does not transfer its collision after a nonlinear change: in the first order G_x,G_y must match at the two base points; in the opposite order H_x,H_y,H_Q must match at the two parameter points; in the third class the two gradients of p(P,Q) must agree. With those jet and point conditions, nonzero constant Hessian determinant is impossible. This narrows OP-HC4-SCHUR beyond the standard graph theorem HC4MYGALL1. It does not exclude every unmarked unit-Hessian potential. Longer base-dependent alternating words, nonlinear base-coordinate changes, other eliminated-coordinate charts, rational Schur pivots and general coisotropic reductions remain outside the theorem. Neither unrestricted HC4 nor JC2 is resolved. Global invertibility relies on the reproduced external structural theorem; its no-plane input is an independent elementary result. No explicit inverse for every member, formal verification, external review or novelty priority is asserted.

entries.title: Complete oriented-generator orbit and polynomial stabilizer of the relative cotangent row
entries.scope: For the retained Meng--Yang residual row gamma=(-y*P(x*y),x*Q(x*y)), with P=18*v^5+81*v^4+120*v^3+60*v^2-1 and Q=(v+1)*(v+2), use HC5T1's existing degree-ten C0 in SL2(K[x,y]) satisfying gamma*C0=(y,2*x). The complete right SL2 orbit is exactly all ordered polynomial generators g of the maximal ideal (x,y) with J(g)(0)=-2. The converse is constructive: decompose g=ell*A for ell=(y,2*x), express det(A)-1=mu*g1+nu*g2, and set A_prime=A+(-2*x,y)^T*(nu,-mu), which preserves the row and has determinant one. Then C=C0*A_prime realizes g without assuming an inverse map. The complete stabilizer of any such g is I+h*(-g2,g1)^T*g for arbitrary polynomial h, by the coprime syzygy classification and rank-one determinant identity. Thus all corrections realizing one g differ by this one-polynomial gauge. In particular C_h=C0+h*(-gamma2,gamma1)^T*ell has degree deg(h)+12 for nonzero h, yet always gives the identical linear output ell; its descended cotangent gradient has an explicit polynomial inverse. This classifies coefficient redundancy in arbitrary degree, rather than inferring exclusions from a matrix-degree box. The normalizer is credited to the retained HC5T1 calculation; the full orbit and stabilizer arguments are written proofs supported by universal symbolic identities and a nontrivial constructive example. The orbit includes non-Keller rows, so no all-degree constant-Hessian or JC2 exclusion follows merely from its classification. No formal verification, external review or novelty priority is claimed.
