entries.title: Positive-genus target obstruction to three PSL2(11) subgroup reductions of actual A11 and S11 Keller maps
entries.scope: Over algebraically closed characteristic-zero constants, restrict the Galois closure of an actual independently curve-induced degree-eleven Keller map to an exceptional transitive J=PSL2(11) subgroup of its A11 or S11 generic group. For the higher-power radicand (p,d)=(3,5) A11 map, the quadratic beta (6,2) S11 map, and the (2,10) S11 map, exact fixed-curve field presentations have passports (5^2*1,3*1^8,11), (2^5*1,6*1^5,11), and (10*1,2*1^9,11). The subgroup-reduced target curves M^J have genera 5678,7331,9343, respectively; their source quotients by the A5 point stabilizer have genera 62493,80641,102813. The finite field base change has the requested degree eleven and geometric group J, but the positive-genus target field cannot be stably rational, so none of these field pairs admits any polynomial affine-space model after independent stabilization and arbitrary birational source and target changes. Complete class intersections in the 660-element group, all cyclic inertia powers, alternating split-class counts and Riemann-Hurwitz prove the exact genera. The conclusion applies to either exceptional action through its Gassmann cycle dictionary. This closes these three subgroup-reduction routes; it does not exclude the independent Klein Shabat input or either abstract PSL2(11) action.

entries.title: Exact generic-pencil genera for natural PSL2(11) subgroup reductions of the two actual A12 families
entries.scope: For the natural transitive J=PSL2(11) subgroup of the A12 generic group of the actual level-two cone and alternating-shear Keller maps, compute the subgroup-reduced generic curve fibers over the algebraic closure of the retained pencil parameter field. The cone pencil has six single-three-cycle generators and (11,1) at infinity, yielding target genus 527826 and source genus 6333906 with relative degree-twelve ramification degree ten. The shear pencil has six single-three-cycle generators and (9,3) at infinity, yielding target genus 524161 and source genus 6289921; the relative degree-twelve curve cover is unramified. The target coset degree is 362880 and the source stabilizer in J has order55. These are exact full class-intersection and cyclic-power calculations. Unlike KMFI17, the input field pairs are genuinely two-dimensional before independent stabilization: positive generic-pencil genus does not prove nonrationality of their total surface fields. KMFI19 subsequently proves both total target surfaces are not stably rational using global regular two-forms, closing these specific affine-space reductions; the genus calculation alone did not supply that obstruction. No abstract action-level exclusion or affine-space realization is claimed.

entries.title: Composite three-dimensional boundary trace forbids a unit four-variable Hessian
entries.scope: For a polynomial f(s,z1,z2,z3) in characteristic zero, if f(0,z)=H(a(z)) with degree H at least two, its Hessian determinant cannot be a nonzero constant. No coordinate, Keller or embedding assumption on a is needed. If a is nonconstant, over the algebraic closure take a point with H_prime(a)=0; the three-by-three tangent Hessian block has rank at most one, and adding one normal row and column raises rank by at most two, leaving a singular four-by-four Hessian. If a is constant the tangent block is zero. Equivalently the nonconstant-composite boundary determinant is divisible by H_prime(a), since the dual adjugate has that factor and the dual determinant has its square. This forbids unit Hessian in both base-eliminated Meng--Yang charts whenever the omitted base coordinate vanishes identically on the free-base-zero slice, even after arbitrary polynomial retained-dual substitutions. The condition concerns the whole slice, not one parameter point. The argument is a written rank/divisibility proof and uses no Tang, line theorem or bounded degree calculation. Exact controls verify the bordered identities, without formal verification or independent external review.

entries.title: Origin-avoiding base-only graphs give exactly all relative polynomial coordinates
entries.scope: The original Meng--Yang A,B coefficient rows have ordered minors y*(1+x*y)^3, x*(1+x*y)*(2+x*y), and 2*x^2*(3+2*x*y). Their ideal is exactly (x,y), with literal polynomial certificates. For any base curve (X(s),Y(s)) generating the unit ideal in K[s], a Bezout combination of those minors supplies a third row and a determinant-one polynomial frame (A,B,W). Replacing B by L*A^2+M*A+N*B is a relative polynomial shear/rescaling, so the restricted potential is a coordinate of K[s][p,q,r], with actual polynomial companions and inverse. For the genuine base-only coordinate graphs x=h(y) or y=h(x), the condition is exactly h(0) nonzero, and arbitrary relative polynomial retained-dual automorphisms produce precisely every relative coordinate of the three-dual polynomial ring. These graph parameterizations are closed embeddings with the free base recovered by projection. No embedding assertion is made for an arbitrary nonembedded base curve. If h(0)=0, HC4MYGU0 forbids unit Hessian after all such retained-dual changes. Degrees are unrestricted, certificates use no localization at x,y or 1+x*y, and a nonzero retained-dual Jacobian is not substituted for an actual inverse. No plane surjectivity or unrestricted HC4/JC2 theorem, formal verification or independent external review is claimed.

entries.title: Unit-Hessian relative coordinates are exactly the unit-ideal plane Keller endpoint
entries.scope: Over C, existence of a four-variable unit-Hessian polynomial that is a coordinate of C[s][z1,z2,z3] is equivalent to existence of a plane Keller pair F(s,U),G(s,U) generating the unit ideal. Every such relative coordinate has no zero of its three dual derivatives at any base value, so its full gradient omits zero and is nonautomorphic. The reproduced Tang alternative supplies a jointly affine constant two-plane. Rank-one projection to s has form D(U,Z)+s*A(U,Z)+V*C(U,Z), with Jac(A,C) unit; choose C=0 and solve uniquely for s,V to kill the other two dual derivatives, a contradiction. Thus rank zero gives D(s,U)+P*F(s,U)+Q*G(s,U) after constant affine changes preserving the free-base fibration. A common zero of F,G would permit P,Q killing D_U+P*F_U+Q*G_U, again a dual critical point, so (F,G)=(1). Conversely a polynomial Bezout certificate a*F+b*G=1 gives a relative automorphism (U,P,Q)->(U,D+P*F+Q*G,-b*P+a*Q), with explicit polynomial inverse. If F,G are Keller its Hessian determinant is Jac(F,G)^2 and its gradient misses zero. No inverse of the plane pair is assumed. Both projection ranks and the Nullstellensatz argument are written proofs; exact controls do not exhibit a unit-ideal Keller pair or formally verify Tang. No plane surjectivity, singleton-zero properness or unrestricted JC2 equivalence is proved.

entries.title: One fixed x=1 graph realizes the full omitted-point Keller endpoint
entries.scope: For every base-only Meng--Yang graph x=h(y) or y=h(x) with h(0) nonzero, existence of a nonzero-constant-Hessian pullback after arbitrary relative polynomial automorphisms of the three retained dual coordinates is equivalent over C to existence of a unit-ideal plane Keller pair. One fixed physical hyperplane graph x=1 realizes every pair F(s,U),G(s,U) with a polynomial Bezout certificate a*F+b*G=1 as the literal pullback D(s,U)+P*F+Q*G. The explicit constant-determinant frame (A,T,W), potential-coordinate inverse and two-by-two row completion give genuine retained-dual automorphisms and closed graph embeddings with polynomial parameter inverses; no plane-map inverse or merely Keller parameterization is used. The actual Hessian determinant is Jac(F,G)^2. A unit-ideal Keller row would make the gradient nonautomorphic by omission of zero. Absence of these rows is exactly surjectivity of every complex plane Keller map, by translating a missing target and Nullstellensatz; this precise assertion remains unresolved here and is not identified with full JC2. For h(0)=0, HC4MYGU0 forbids unit Hessian after all relative retained-dual changes. The new coefficient ideal (1) is distinct from the origin maximal ideal in the nonlinear p-chart singleton-zero problem. The fixed x=1 graph cannot contain both original v2 marked base points, so no automatic fixed-collision transfer is asserted. The unimodular control (s,s*U-1) has Hessian determinant s^2 and is explicitly non-Keller. No unit-ideal Keller pair, plane surjectivity theorem, singleton-zero properness theorem, formal verification, independent external review or unrestricted HC4/JC2 solution is claimed.

entries.title: Conditional all-degree exclusion of arithmetic-compatible cotangent and shear words for Long
entries.scope: Assuming Kanel-Belov-Fedorov arXiv2610.33919v1 Theorem4.2, Long's polynomial symplectic endomorphism is not a finite composition of cotangent lifts of polynomial Keller maps, positional gradient shears, Fourier changes and linear symplectic transformations. Degrees and word lengths are arbitrary. For a Keller base F, its commuting inverse-Jacobian derivations delta_i satisfy delta_i^ell=0 in every good prime characteristic; the crystalline powers of their polynomial first-order Weyl operators are exactly sum_j B_ji^ell D_j^ell. Positional gradient shears have exact Frobenius center maps by Bavula's p-power formula, and odd-characteristic linear symplectic maps have the same compatibility. Composition preserves the Frobenius-twisted classical center map after one common arithmetic localization, contradicting the cited preprint theorem for Long. This is a written conditional corollary, not an independent proof or external review of that preprint. It excludes no arbitrary bounded formal lift, no arbitrary polynomial symplectic coordinate change lacking a proved arithmetic-compatible lift, and no general DC2 counterexample. No finite search, checker replay, formal verification or novelty priority is claimed.
dependencies: external: Bavula 2009 prime-characteristic Weyl p-power formula

entries.title: All-degree finite conic gates and complete cubic WZT family
entries.scope: For cubic P=W*(a+bZ+cT+dZ^2+eZT+fT^2)+G(Z,T), deg G<=3, the nondegenerate e^2-4df!=0 locus has a nonzero pure moment among the first 888. When f=0,e!=0, 447 suffice. In Laurent conic coordinates the rank is at most six and t^5*Phi has coefficient degree<=6; in the WZT and retained trapped-component models t^2*Phi has degree<=3. Logarithmic connection reduction gives N/H with numerator and denominator degrees B<=L*(r+1), L=6 or3. Minimal-seed cofactors bound scalar coefficients by B*s*(s+1)/2, and the nonzero zeroth coefficient gives prefixes 888 and447 at r<=6. These are sufficient bounds, not optimality claims or moment expansions through the claimed prefixes. Thus the complete fifteen-coefficient family f=0 satisfies GMC, with 447 initial zero moments implying all-order pure vanishing: e!=0 is excluded and e=0 is the existing fourteen-coefficient family with gate320. For the full sixteen-coefficient W-linear cubic family this result reduces the then-remaining analysis to candidates with f!=0,e^2-4df=0, and a Gaussian null rotation reduces it to W*(a+bZ+cT+fT^2)+G. This rank-one family includes the GMC-safe pure-null polynomial W*T^2 and is not excluded by the theorem. entries.title: Global monic elimination gives an equivalent 38-variable quadratic presentation of the rooted degree-eight necessary core
entries.scope: For both irreducible degree-eight marked coefficient fields, retaining the complete four-parameter actual pole-three cusp root S and the monic perturbation R=h^8+sum(c_i*h^i,i=2..7), the full rooted degree-eight necessary system of PF2RULED26-28 has a globally equivalent presentation with 38 variables and 39 equations of degree at most two over K. Write r=S0_prime/h, L=R_prime/h and C=lambda^2*r*L_prime+(2h*(S2+v*lambda*r)-lambda^2*r_prime)*L. The equations are the twenty coefficients of C-2*S0_prime*B-M, the eighteen coefficients of 2*M*S0+2*h*L*N-kappa, and kappa*invkappa-1, with degree bounds B<=8,M<=5,N<=10. Nine triangular quotient pivots24 and six remainder pivots-1 recover B,M; the remaining five first-identity equations equal the original primary high-remainder inputs. Evaluation at the cusp recovers kappa=2*M(s)*S0(s); eleven triangular pivots16 recover N and the remaining equations give exactly the original divisibility condition. These27 auxiliaries are polynomially recoverable without any parameter denominator, so all coefficient-zero, rank-drop and critical-root collision cases and the nonzero condition are preserved. The assertion covers all sixteen complex embeddings, with the original actual-global-root and boundary-amplitude normalization hypotheses retained. The checker reconstructs actual Cox sections, compares the normal Jacobian and all five primary high equations, and retains every exact quadratic polynomial. Separately, native msolve saturation at prime1073741827 returned the unit basis for one marked residue in each sector; the full current primary input was matched coefficientwise and both native runs replayed. These are finite-field observations only, not characteristic-zero exclusions. One retained first-sector unsaturated unit result is discovery evidence only. Bounded unsuccessful expanded and quadratic attempts are preserved. No exact characteristic-zero unit certificate has been obtained, so the full nonzero-kappa core remains open. No actual global section lifts, whole marked candidate or quartic packet exclusion, source Keller pair, field degree-four realization, global surface finiteness or arbitrary-normalization compatible embedding is established. The general root-free determinant and rank-drop locus, later normal equations through u^9, contact cases, other height-nine pairs, higher heights and all-height pole-four remain unresolved. This is a written global ideal-equivalence proof supported by exact characteristic-zero arithmetic, without formal verification, independent whole-proof implementation, external review, new imported theorem or novelty priority. The full research goal remains active.

entries.title: Invariant trace poles exclude endpoint limits for a specified nonzero-target collision family
entries.scope: For the foundational three-variable Keller map, let a(k)=((1-k)/2,-2,-4(1+3k)/k^2), b(k)=((1+k)/2,-2,-4(1-3k)/k^2), k!=0. Their common target is (0,-2,(1-k^2)/(2k^2)). In the normalized map H_k=(JF(a)L)^-1(F(a+LX)-F(a)), L=[b-a,e_y,e_z], no meromorphic matrix P(k) fixing e1 can give a finite coefficientwise limit of P^-1 H_k(PX) at k=0 or infinity, including after finite local ramification. Both trace JH(2e1) and trace JH(H(2e1)) are polynomial functions of the bounded-degree map coefficients and invariant under these conjugations. The first equals864*k^2-2736*k+723 and has a pole at infinity. The second has leading Laurent term -49460507836416/k^3 at zero. Exact primary symbolic arithmetic and an independent standard-library rational Laurent calculation agree on its entire Laurent polynomial. The pair family has105 generic nonlinear occurrences in its natural frame; no support minimum for its finite parameters is asserted. Other pair families, simultaneous variation of further parameters and finite-parameter sparsity remain open. The normalized raw-degree-seven support interval stays [10,48]; this is a closed degeneration route, not a degree improvement or global optimum.

entries.scope: Over any one-variable algebraic function field in characteristic zero with a nonzero derivation, no scalar differential operators of exact orders2 and3 have commutator a nonzero differential constant. Arbitrary nonmonic algebraic leading coefficients normalize after a finite cover because b^2/a^3 is constant. The normalized scalar commutator defines its own algebraic time tau with delta(tau)=1 and yields a Painleve-I equation y''=6y^2+alpha*tau+beta with alpha nonzero. Finite-point Puiseux balances exclude every nonintegral exponent: pole indicial roots are-3 and4 and regular roots0 and1. Riemann-Hurwitz forces an algebraic solution to be rational, and infinity degree balance excludes rational solutions. This covers arbitrary coefficient degrees, pole divisors, curve genus and finite algebraic covers, without assuming the recent arithmetic nonlifting theorem. It extends the stated domain of its monic quadratic-cover Lemma4.8. Orders(2,1) and(2,4) have explicit canonical examples, so no all-order exclusion is asserted. The exact checker verifies the general Ore identities, indicial factors and sharpness examples; the all-curve theorem is a written proof. Infinite or nonalgebraic formal coefficient series, matrices, changed order profiles and possible full lifts lacking a scalar reduction remain outside scope. No formal verification, independent theorem replay, external review, novelty priority or DC2 solution is claimed.

entries.title: Holonomic formal graph model with generic failure of left finite generation
entries.scope: For A=K[t]<x,p>/([p,x]-t), q=1-t^2*x and S=A[q^-1], give M=S the regular left action and right action x->x/q, p->q^2*p-t^3*q. The assignment is exactly canonical, M is parameter-flat and cyclic coherent over A^e because phi(1+t^2*x)=q^-1, and its formal completion is free of left rank one with special fiber the diagonal graph. Nevertheless M is the strict union of A*q^-k, so it is not finitely generated from the left, even over K(t). A word-length growth bound O(m^2) and Bernstein's inequality show generic holonomicity as an A^e module. The pole divisor x=t^-2 is invisible in the formal parameter neighborhood. Formal conjugation by exp(t*(x^2*p+t*x)) identifies the completed graph with the regular bimodule, so a better left-free algebraization exists in this example; only the inference that an arbitrary coherent/holonomic algebraization inherits formal left finiteness is refuted. Adding regular spectator pairs gives the same failure in every Weyl rank with holonomic dimension2n. The checker verifies the canonical assignment, cyclic generator identity and formal conjugation identities; infinite-chain, coherence, completion and holonomicity claims use written proofs. entries.title: Relative critical-scheme Hessian determinant invariant under polynomial dual automorphisms
entries.scope: Let f(s,z1,z2,z3) be polynomial and Phi=(s,phi(s,Z)) a polynomial automorphism over K[s], with relative Jacobian field unit d. For g=f composed with Phi, the relative gradient ideals satisfy I_g=Phi_star(I_f). The Hessian chain-rule correction has entries in I_g, since the base coordinate is unchanged. Hence det Hess g equals d^2 times Phi_star(det Hess f) modulo the full relative gradient ideal, not merely after passing to its radical. The critical schemes are isomorphic and their determinant classes differ only by a nonzero constant. A nonconstant determinant on one critical component, a singular critical point, or different constant values on two components excludes unit Hessian after every such automorphism. Actual inverse hypotheses transport the whole locus; merely Keller substitutions are not substituted. Constant affine changes of the free base also preserve the conclusion up to a field scalar. No nonlinear Hessian invariance away from the relative critical locus is asserted; an exact unit-Hessian control changes its off-critical determinant to -323. The chain-rule and ideal arguments are written elementary proofs. No external classification, formal verification or independent external review is used.

entries.title: Exact relative critical curve and Hessian function for every y=R(x,p)
entries.scope: For the Meng--Yang family with L*N nonzero and arbitrary polynomial graph y=R(x,p), independent of q,r, every relative critical point with x nonzero is exactly on 2*x*R+3=0 and R_p nonzero, with T=A=(13*N/(2*x^2)-M)/(2*L), q=-3*T/(4*x)+1/(16*x^2*R_p), and r recovered from A. If R_p vanishes on that curve, the remaining p derivative is -N/(4*x^2), so it is not a critical point. The critical value is D=-N*p/(4*x^2)-(M-13*N/(2*x^2))^2/(4*L). The localized curve derivation delta=partial_x+(3/(2*x^2)-R_x)/R_p*partial_p preserves its defining ideal. The native critical Hessian determinant is exactly -32*L*N^2*x^6*R_p^2*delta^2(D), from the actual dual Hessian and a Schur complement. The rational coordinates (p,A,q) are used only for this local computation and are not claimed as a global polynomial parameterization. After any actual polynomial retained-dual automorphism, unit Hessian requires the same nonzero constant on every critical component, including any separate x=0 locus. This is an all-degree necessary condition, not sufficiency or an exclusion of general nonlinear R. An opposite-chart control has determinant4 on two computed critical components but1556 at an off-critical point. The proof and controls use no Tang or other classification and assert no formal verification or independent external review.

entries.title: All y=a(x)p+b(x) with nonzero polynomial a excluded after every retained-dual automorphism
entries.scope: Over every characteristic-zero field and for L*N nonzero, no graph y=a(x)*p+b(x), with a any nonzero polynomial and b arbitrary polynomial, has a nonzero constant four-variable Hessian determinant after any relative polynomial automorphism of the three retained duals over K[x]. Coefficient degrees and word lengths are unrestricted, and a may have zeros. The generic critical branch is p=(-3/(2*x)-b)/a and its value D=N*(3+2*x*b)/(8*a*x^3)-(M-13*N/(2*x^2))^2/(4*L), with denominator dividing a*x^4. HC4MYGK0/1 force D_second=K/(a^2*x^6), K nonzero, under hypothetical unit Hessian. If d=degree(a)>0, after subtracting its affine polynomial part D would have infinity order2*d+4, exceeding the denominator bound d+4. If a is constant, the unavoidable x^(-3) coefficient3*N/(8*a) makes D_second have x^(-5) coefficient9*N/(2*a), contradicting that equation. The proof works on the nonempty rational open x*a nonzero; it never assumes a global inverse for p->a*p+b. Actual retained-dual polynomial inverses are required and constant affine parameter changes are harmless. The identically zero a case is excluded from the hypothesis and retains the base-only unit-ideal Keller endpoint or zero-slice obstruction. General nonlinear y=R(x,p), graphs involving q,r in the omitted base, opposite-chart reparameterizations and free-base/dual mixing remain separate. This elementary all-degree exclusion uses no Tang, line theorem, plane surjectivity or JC2 assumption and claims no formal verification or independent external review.

entries.title: Exact sign descent transports both rooted degree-eight necessary presentations and unit rows to quartic coefficient fields
entries.scope: For each marked sector(2,7),(4,5), the even irreducible octic P8(y)=P4(y^2) defines K of degree8 with sign involution y->-y and fixed quartic field F=Q(y^2). entries.title: Global holomorphic two-forms obstruct both A12-to-PSL2(11) target surfaces
entries.scope: Over algebraically closed characteristic-zero constants, let M be the Galois closure of either actual A12 plane field pair, the level-two cone or alternating shear, and let J=PSL2(11) be its natural degree-twelve subgroup. Each fixed surface field M^J has a smooth projective model with a nonzero regular two-form and is therefore not stably rational. Write O for the 165-element J-orbit of four-subsets and B_A=product_(i in A,j notin A)(w_i-w_j). The cone form is sum_(A in O)(sum_(i in A)w_i)^10/B_A times dP wedge dQ; the shear form is Y^4*sum_(A in O)1/B_A times dP wedge dY. On weighted compactifications P(1,6,11) and P(1,2,9), they extend using projective factors s^4 and s^12 and the Euler contraction. Complete branch resultants give only ordinary nodes, four (2,5) cusps and the (2,3) origin cusp; the shear additionally has an apparent unramified three-root loss on Y=0 and a (3,28) weighted boundary cusp. Weighted local root-difference bounds prove extension across all exceptional divisors. Exact nonzero certificates are 473 over F991 and 173+114h over F179[h]/(h^2-2), with all specialized roots distinct and all cut denominators units. Finite quotient descent gives nonzero forms on resolutions of the J-targets. Consequently neither subgroup-reduced threefold pair, nor any further common independent stabilization and birational affine rechart, admits an ordinary affine-space polynomial model. Combined with KMFI17 all five audited subgroup-reduction routes are excluded. This does not exclude either abstract PSL2(11) action, independent Klein Shabat completion or a different higher-dimensional field pair; the full action spectrum remains open.

entries.title: Complete sixteen-coefficient W-linear cubic GMC theorem and sharp mixed cutoff
entries.scope: Every pure-null polynomial P=W*(a+bZ+cT+dZ^2+eZT+fT^2)+G(Z,T), deg G<=3, satisfies GMC. This is the complete sixteen-coefficient W-linear cubic family. Nondegenerate e^2-4df!=0 is excluded by the logarithmic conic theorem; f=0 is the completed fifteen-coefficient family; f!=0 on the degenerate discriminant is reduced by a Gaussian null rotation to G3WTRANKONE20261114. The sufficient initial pure-moment gates are888,447,425 respectively, so888 suffices for all-order pure vanishing in the whole family. Every pure-null member has E(QP^m)=0 for m>3*deg Q, sharply by the previously registered cubic Gaussian shear; the new rank-one products and the one-sided/quadratic branches need only m>deg Q. There is an exact coordinate-free frame criterion: for P=F3+F2+F1+F0, a Gaussian W-linear frame exists if and only if a nonzero vector v satisfies B(v,v)=0, grad F3(v)=0 and F2(v)=0, since D_v^2P(x)=2 grad F3(v) dot x+2F2(v). Thus any global cubic GMC failure must have that projective intersection empty. No proof establishes that all pure-null cubics meet the criterion. W^2,W^3,W^2Z,W^2T and the empty-intersection case remain outside the theorem. Internal written period proofs and exact algebra checks have no external review or formal verification. entries.title: Rank-one algebraic dual criterion and exact limits of formal scalar reduction
entries.scope: For a nonzero torsion-free rank-one left module M over a left noetherian two-sided Ore domain A, finite generation from the left is equivalent to Hom_A(M,A) being nonzero: a nonzero dual map embeds M into A, and finite generators admit a common right denominator. In the QGM1 localization M=A[(1-t^2*x)^-1], the algebraic left dual is zero by the intersection of q^k*A, while every parameter-jet dual and the completed dual are nonzero. The same boundary model is simple and holonomic generically, so those standard graph properties do not force a nonzero algebraic dual. Its Ext1 is the cokernel of (y_k)->(y_k-q*y_(k+1)) on the product of copies of A; the constant sequence1 has a nonzero class that disappears in the completed recurrence. Separately the exact degree-one quantum automorphism x->x+t^2*p, p->p has identity classical reduction but its graph constraint R_x-L_x acts as t*partial_p+t^2*p, is nilpotent modulo every t^N, and is not locally nilpotent generically. Exact shears Q->Q+t^2*P^N preserve the classical map and boundedness for fixed N while producing arbitrarily high generic differential orders. Thus bounded full lifting does not by itself supply the actual local nilpotence or raw order preservation needed for scalar reduction. These examples admit good algebraic normalizations, so no intrinsic impossibility or Long nonlifting conclusion follows. The exact checker covers the stated PBW identities and finite controls; the dual criterion, infinite intersection, Ext class and all-N statements use written proofs. Rank-one/torsion-free hypotheses and a free frame must be established separately; no bounded Long lift, DC2 proof, formal verification, external review, independent theorem replay or novelty priority is claimed.

entries.scope: Let f(s,z1,z2,z3) over C have nonzero constant Hessian determinant. Its relative critical scheme is smooth of pure dimension one when nonempty. entries.title: Projective formal-frame degeneration and compatible filtered-frame descent
entries.scope: For every Weyl rank n>=1 and integer m>=1, in the finite PBW algebra A_R with [p_i,x_j]=t*delta_ij over R=K[t] or K[[t]] in characteristic zero, the left ideal I_m=A_R*(1-t^m*x_1)^2+A_R*((1-t^m*x_1)*p_1-2*t^(m+1)) is rank-one projective and stably free with a two-generator, one-relation polynomial presentation and an explicit splitting. Its inclusion into A_R is an isomorphism modulo every t^N and after completion, and supplies a nonzero algebraic dual section, but its generic fiber is not free in any rank. Canonical generic coordinates give the strict symbol ideal (u^2,u*v), which is nonprincipal; in rank one its normalized Berest-Wilson charge is exactly one, while the special module is free. Thus finite projectivity, bounded presentation degrees and bounded generic charge do not make a formal free frame effective. Separately, a module with an exhaustive bounded-below compatible filtration, finite R-modules in each graded degree, R-flat associated graded and special associated graded freely generated over the polynomial symbol ring is free over A_R for R=K[[t]], by degreewise Nakayama and symbol induction. entries.title: Absolutely stably atomic imprimitive Keller maps with a unique block and nonregular generic deck involution
entries.scope: Every signed-alternating affine-four-space map in KMFI29 is absolutely and stably atomic under polynomial Keller composition despite its imprimitive geometric action. entries.scope: In Weyl rank two over every characteristic-zero field with nonzero scalar h, every finite polynomial endomorphism of the Ore centralizer C=K[x,y][b;h*theta], r=x*(1+x*y), theta=x^2*d_x-(1+2*x*y)*d_y, that fixes r is exactly x to x, y to y, b to b+F(x,y); it is automatically an automorphism. entries.scope: For every normalized characteristic-zero Keller map f in n variables, f_t=t^-1*f(t*x) and its inverse-Jacobian cotangent Weyl images define an exact finite polynomial family for independent parameters h,t with all full Weyl relations. entries.title: The plane polynomial P(F squared minus one)+QF has nonpositive generic fibre Euler
dependencies: external: Abhyankar--Moh closed-line degree theorem, Garcia Barroso--Ploski 1208.0913v1 Theorem6.9
entries.scope: For every nonconstant complex polynomial F(P,Q), let Z=P*F+Q and G=P*(F^2-1)+Q*F=F*Z-P. Only finitely many fibres G=lambda have an actual closed A1 component. On such a component parameterized by t, put a=F and b=Z; then P=a*b-lambda and Q=(1-a^2)*b+lambda*a. If both vary with positive degrees A,B, the embedding coordinate degrees A+B and2*A+B lie strictly between divisibility multiples, contradicting the explicitly imported Abhyankar--Moh degree theorem. Constant a gives a straight line; constant nonzero b gives the parabola Q=b-P*(P+lambda)/b; b=0 gives the vertical Z-zero line, except the collapsed lambda=0 point. Every parabola intersects every candidate straight line and parabolas over distinct values intersect. Infinitely many disjoint A1 components across distinct values would therefore be parallel lines. A fixed direction permits at most two constant-a values, since parallel normals give (a-b)*(a*b+1)=0; zero-b lines lie on Z=0. A fixed nonzero F-a or Z cannot contain infinitely many distinct lines. Thus generic smooth fibres have no A1 component and Euler at most zero, component by component. Generic irreducibility is neither assumed nor needed. Total degree and embedding degrees are unrestricted; the degree import reuses the retained primary v1 PDF at its additional Theorem6.9, with an explicit manifest. entries.scope: Consider a potential L*A^2+M*A+N*B with L*N nonzero and A,B linear in the three ambient duals. Fix a scalar free base and a nonzero constant linear dual row ell, and let the omitted base be any nonconstant polynomial R(w), w=ell dot(p,q,r). Suppose the ambient coefficient rows of A,B are independent at every omitted-base value z and K_ell(z)=ell dot(A_z cross B_z) is nonconstant. Restricting the rows to ker ell gives rank two away from the finite roots of K_ell(R(w)), and rank one at them; rank zero is impossible. Rank two gives one affine-line value fibre. At rank one, if A_z is not proportional to ell, a generic quadratic value equation gives two affine lines; if it is proportional, B remains nonconstant and gives one affine line. Explicit row inversion identifies the open whole stratum with (A1 minus m points) times A1. The generic value-fibre Hodge polynomial is t^2+k*t, where k counts distinct quadratic-type w values, with every multiplicity ignored and every linear-type root counted once. A single quadratic-type z root gives k>=1 by polynomial surjectivity, independently of deg R. HC4MYHC0 then forces gradient invertibility under actual unit Hessian and throughout every actual retained-dual automorphism orbit. Fixed-base linear completion of ell is not a global inverse over the polynomial base ring and no such inverse is assumed. All products are actual stratum isomorphisms, not arbitrary finite-cover multiplicativity.

entries.title: Every y base graph in one arbitrary affine dual direction is closed in all degrees
entries.scope: Work in the scaled Meng--Yang family Psi=L*A^2+M*A+N*B with L*N nonzero. For y=R(x,w), w=a(x)*p+b(x)*q+c(x)*r with a,b,c polynomial and not all zero and R polynomial of positive w degree, every actual retained-three-dual automorphism over K[x] with unit full Hessian has an invertible gradient over any characteristic-zero field. Affine offsets in w may be absorbed into R. No coefficient is required to be a field unit and the row need not be unimodular. At generic x=s nonzero, the native row cross product is (2*s^2*(2*s*z+3),-s*(1+s*z)*(2+s*z),z*(1+s*z)^3), never zero. The direction polynomial has degree one or two when c=0 and all roots are quadratic type. For c nonzero it is quartic with at most one linear-type value. Scaling its possible proportional-A row at tau gives derivative -6*(1+tau)^3 at that root, so another root is quadratic; at tau=-1 the exact polynomial -v*(v+1)^3 retains the quadratic root zero. Thus every direction has a quadratic-type root, including pure old-r, and HC4MYHD0 applies in every graph/coefficient degree and word length. This enlarges the old-r-dependent closure without any boundary condition; it does not claim all general nonlinear dual dependence is covered or that every unit-Hessian member is absent.

entries.title: Every opposite one-dual-direction graph except the pure old-r direction is closed
entries.scope: Work in the scaled Meng--Yang family Psi=L*A^2+M*A+N*B with L*N nonzero. For x=R(y,w), w=a(y)*p+b(y)*q+c(y)*r with (a,b) not identically (0,0) and R polynomial of positive w degree, every unit-Hessian actual retained-three-dual pullback over K[y] has a polynomial gradient inverse over any characteristic-zero field. Direction coefficients, graph degree and automorphism word length are unrestricted, with no unimodular-row assumption. At fixed y=s nonzero, the native independent row cross product is (2*z^2*(2*s*z+3),-z*(1+s*z)*(2+s*z),s*(1+s*z)^3). The weighted cubic K=2*alpha*v^2*(2*v+3)-beta*v*(v+1)*(v+2)+gamma*(v+1)^3 is nonconstant, since its three nonconstant coefficient map has determinant -6. A proportional-A direction has at most one linear-type finite value tau; its exact factor (v-tau)*Q_tau has a nonconstant remaining polynomial, with Q_tau(tau)=6*tau*(tau+1)^3. This gives a different quadratic-type root except the separately handled pure-p tau=0 case, whose root -3/2 works. The tau=-1 row is precisely pure old-r and is excluded. If alpha=0,beta nonzero there is no linear-type root at all. HC4MYHD0 gives positive Hodge coefficient. The pure-r exception has only linear-type roots and generic Hodge polynomial t^2, so no positive coefficient is invented for it.

entries.title: The remaining pure-r opposite family reduces to the existing unit-ideal or singleton-zero plane endpoints
entries.scope: Work in the scaled Meng--Yang family Psi=L*A^2+M*A+N*B with L*N nonzero. For x=R(s,r), y=s, followed by every actual retained-dual automorphism over K[s], there are no relative critical points at s nonzero. On 1+s*R nonzero, the exact T=A chart has q coefficient N*s, and on its zero stratum the native q derivative is -2*N*s. At s=0 put R0=R(0,r),g=r*R0. The whole critical set is s=0,T=-M/(2*L),gprime=0,q free. Its full native critical Hessian is -4*L*N^3*gsecond, including every nonlinear off-slice jet. R0=0 gives a forbidden critical two-plane. If deg R0=d>=2, unit Hessian requires gprime squarefree and gsecond to take the same nonzero value at all d roots; gsecond minus that value has degree below d and must vanish identically, contradicting d>=2. Thus unit Hessian forces a nonzero constant boundary, with empty entire critical scheme, or a nonconstant linear boundary, with one smooth closed critical A1 and Hessian -8*L*N^3 times its leading coefficient. For a hypothetical nonautomorphic member Tang rank one is impossible by emptiness or HC4MYGR0. Rank zero supplies a plane Keller pair, each origin preimage contributing one critical A1. Empty and singleton cases therefore give respectively the unit ideal and the maximal ideal of one reduced point. These are exactly the two existing complex plane endpoints as necessary problems. No converse realization inside this pure-r graph family, properness theorem or critical-Hessian sufficiency is supplied. Conditional cotangent models show why trace t^2 or t^2-t alone cannot close those endpoint signatures. Unit-ideal and singleton-zero remain distinct and unresolved.

entries.title: Complete binary cubic and N=2 three-factor moment schemes, with five and forty-five primary components
entries.scope: Over C in characteristic zero, the full homogeneous binary-cubic Gaussian pure-moment ideal in four coefficients P=xW^3+yZW^2+zZ^2W+wZ^3 is J=(xw+yz,xz^3+y^3w-3y^2z^2,y^3z^3). A balanced-monomial/reversal invariant ring C[s,t,u] proves all-order generation from the first three even moments, not finite extrapolation. J has an explicit verified five-component primary decomposition, radical (x,y) intersect (z,w), degree2, nilradical index6 and intrinsic origin torsion of length1 in degree8. Pulling back by x=def,y=aef+dbf+dec,z=abf+aec+dbc,w=abc gives the full coefficient ideal I for three centered linear factors in two Gaussian coordinates. Its radical is the squarefree triangular-prism cover ideal (bcdf,bcde,acef,acde,abef,abdf), with nine coordinate minimal primes. Generic zero-factor and isotropic-pair local lengths are8 and2, giving degree36 and reduced degree9. I has exactly45 associated primes over C:27 coordinate primes and18 noncoordinate primes (a,d,bf-lambda*ce) and factor permutations, where lambda ranges over the six distinct nonzero roots of D(t)=t^6+4t^5+14t^4+18t^3+14t^2+4t+1. On the normalized zero-factor chart, exact PID Smith forms give a free rank8 base module plus D-torsion with ranks1,2,1 in A-degrees4,5,6; intrinsic local torsion at each noncoordinate prime has length4. Its chosen root-fiber primary component has colength12, a distinct quantity. All45 primary components are constructed explicitly: nine isolated saturations,18 root-fiber saturations, and18 embedded coordinate primary ideals from positive-weight pure-power truncations. Their full intersection and irredundancy follow from the complete associated-prime list and a written graded-separation/minimal-associated-prime proof; no expanded45-way CAS replay is asserted. Embedded coordinate orbit representatives have free faces abc,ad,ab,a,empty, intrinsic local torsion lengths84,62,8,2,13 and top weights13,18,21,32,30, with explicit truncation powers in the certificate. The coefficient-origin torsion is 3t^28+6t^29+4t^30. Exhaustive reductions of all1540 generators of the ninth radical power and a nonzero eighth-power witness (acef)^8 prove exact nilradical index9. The full six-variable primdecGTZ call is a retained terminal50-second timeout, not the source of a claimed decomposition. Internal constructive written and exact symbolic/CAS proof; no independent replay, external review or formal verification. N=3,4 coefficient schemes, arbitrary further subfamilies, changed characteristic, affine factors and arbitrary cubic GMC remain separate.

entries.title: Ramification forces position avoidance and excludes low-order source polarizations
entries.scope: Long's actual generic fiber map is a finite cubic cover with a double-root boundary and a second branch over the same divisor where the position v varies. A general two-branch valuation lemma gives K(r)(S,T) intersect K(r)(v)=K(r) in every rational function degree. This field intersection persists for every exact-R formal quantum lift in completed quantum function fields, without a common spatial bound. For finite differential operators over K(r)((h))(v), QSO2 then excludes every Weyl pair in the entire completed fiber image having either order at most two; arbitrary polynomial source Weyl automorphisms and rational source substitutions producing finite differential operators are covered, with parameter poles allowed. Separately, any full formal Long lift whose first image U_h remains positional, even if deformed, meets the target position algebra exactly in the completed algebra generated by U_h. For bounded finite-PBW lifts the intersection is K((h))[U_h], so no polynomial source Weyl automorphism can make both position images positional in the original target chart. In the exact-R case the ambient ad-nilpotent elements of the fiber image are exactly K((h))[R]. The boundary lemma, valuation descent, image-intersection and all-degree exclusions use written proofs; exact controls verify cubic and discriminant identities, both branch parameterizations, first-order normal-form and local-nilpotence controls and retained input hashes. High-order pairs, target changes moving the position ring, nonpositional first images and arbitrary nonalgebraic operator coefficients remain open. No bounded full lift, all-representative nonlifting, DC2 solution, independent theorem replay, formal verification, external review or novelty priority is claimed.

entries.title: Natural high-rank affine canonical constructions cost at least N, and N+1 when the rank is invertible
entries.scope: For N>=5 over every field, an S_N-equivariant polynomial Keller map between d-dimensional affine representations with a fixed target and complete natural marked N-point fibre requires d>=N when the characteristic divides N, and d>=N+1 otherwise. If N is invertible the orbit barycentre supplies a source origin even when the characteristic divides N!, and UACANCOST1 applies. In divisible characteristic the actual affine orbit spans the sum-one permutation hyperplane or its scalar-line quotient, of dimensions N-1 and N-2. One two-block stabilizer S_r times S_(N-r), with both blocks at least two and r invertible, has nonempty fixed affine span of dimension one or zero. Its ambient fixed dimension is at most d-N+2; UAFIXGEOM1 requires at least two because the marked fixed fibre is empty. Thus d>=N without a modular representation catalogue. If the source already has a fixed origin, N+1 applies in every characteristic. The generic degree is unrestricted. The low-rank modular exceptions are real. This extends the linear bound to affine source bundles and bounds any uniform stabilization, but not arbitrary nonlinear actions or unmarked ktdim.

entries.title: Missing affine sheets bound inertia and force rank-one ramified boundaries for cyclic affine generic groups
entries.scope: For every polynomial Keller self-map of ordinary affine space over an algebraically closed field with geometric generic degree n, the complete geometric generic rank r_D above every affine target prime divisor is at least one, and its inertia embeds in S_(n-r_D). The characteristic-free divisor pullback argument retained in KMFI1 supplies every actual unramified sheet. Loss at most one gives trivial inertia; loss two can ramify only by a transposition, tame outside characteristic two; nontrivial wild inertia in characteristic p needs loss at least p. In characteristic zero a noninvertible map has some affine ramification and loses at least two sheets, or at least three if its group lies in A_n. A nonsquare geometric discriminant in odd characteristic forces an odd-inertia divisor and loss at least two. For geometric generic group F_q semidirect C_m in its natural affine action, m>1 dividing q-1, every ramified affine divisor has rank one and cyclic inertia in a label stabilizer C_m, and at least one exists by the nonconstant Kummer quotient, as in UAFINITE1. Actual rank may be smaller than the number of inertia-fixed labels: omitted unramified branches in the written translation normalization give a strict example. The same divisor argument gives power-injectivity b(F) in k(X)^*a implies b in k(Y)^*a for all a>=2, hence no nontrivial cyclic prime-to-characteristic generic Galois intermediate field. These are stable under polynomial left-right equivalence and identity stabilization. Wild affine fundamental groups are not treated as trivial.

entries.title: Full-degree canonical symmetric fibres force normal monodromy and usually automatic absolute stable atomicity
entries.scope: For a polynomial Keller self-map with arbitrary compatible polynomial S_N actions, geometric generic degree N>=2 and a complete natural marked N-point fibre at a fixed target, its geometric monodromy is transitive and normal in S_N. The N etale points exhaust the normalization degree, giving an invariant finite-etale chart at that target; pointed fibre-functor equivariance normalizes monodromy by the full symmetric label group. For N>=5 the possibilities are A_N or S_N. At rank three C3 or S3 is primitive; rank two C2 is primitive. At rank four only V4,A4,S4 occur, and UAINERTIACOST1 excludes regular V4 outside characteristic two by its quadratic Galois subfield. Hence UAALLATOM1 gives absolute stable atomicity except the possible case N=4, characteristic two, geometric group V4. The exception occurs for the decomposable canonical two-coordinate Lang map. In characteristic zero KMFI1 excludes nontrivial regular groups, leaving S3 in rank three, A_N or S_N for N>=4, and no rank-two realization. These assertions are independent of affine linearizability. A marked boundary fibre of rank N inside a higher-degree map is outside the theorem, and imprimitive monodromy alone is not declared decomposable. UAFIXDEFECT1 now excludes every characteristic-zero full-degree realization in every dimension, so that part is a valid but vacuous conditional. The modular normal-monodromy theorem remains applicable, while higher-degree boundary candidates need separate monodromy and atomicity proofs.

entries.title: Matrix Lang maps give canonical affine finite-field local systems and fixed universal atomic maps in every vector rank
entries.scope: For q=p^e, n>=1 and k containing F_q, Phi_(n,q)(X)=X-X^[q] is a degree-q^n finite-etale Jacobian-one canonical marked affine-bundle realization over B_AGL_n(F_q), with affine source action AX+b and linear target action A. It has regular translation monodromy and decomposes when en>1. The fixed matrix map L_(n,q)(U,X)=(U,X-U X^[q]) on A^(n*n+n) has Jacobian one, exact arithmetic and geometric AGL_n(F_q) monodromy and absolute stable atomicity. On det U nonzero a specified frame satisfies U B^[q]=B, det B nonzero and mu-U mu^[q]=V; matrix and additive Hilbert90 realize every framed torsor over every extension, including finite fields and disconnected torsors. The map is globally polynomial on the whole affine source. Shifting U=I+T gives affine source and linear target actions with common determinant character det A, so its marked canonical descent is effective and source origin absent. Over F_q, UAFINCOUNT1 forces fixed framed dimension at least n+1 whenever GL_n(F_q) is nontrivial; no general matching minimum is claimed. The canonical dimension is exactly n for q>2 over every such base by a faithful prime-to-p diagonal stabilizer, and for q=2 over F2 by point count; UA1CANCLASS1 gives n=2 exactly two over all characteristic-two bases. General q=2 minima over larger bases are not deduced. The basis-free receiver consists of an affine bundle with specified compatible Frobenius-periodicity isomorphisms, whose difference map is finite etale with derivative identity. Zhang2026 TheoremI supports arbitrary fibered bases and imperfect fields; without F_q constants the finite group scheme may be nonconstant. Periodicity as a property alone does not select its gluing data.

entries.title: A globally finite atomic four-coordinate map realizes every quartic algebra in characteristic two
entries.scope: Over every characteristic-two field, Q(s,t,x,y)=(s,t,x+(1+s*t)*x^2+s*y^2,y+t*x^2+y^2) is globally finite etale of rank four and Jacobian one, with arithmetic and geometric S4 monodromy and absolute stable atomicity. Every quartic etale algebra over every extension is a complete fibre. Every invertible two-by-two Frobenius matrix is equivalent without root extraction to [[1+s*t,s],[t,1]]: normalize determinant by diag(D^-1,1), then use the explicit nonzero-upper-right unipotent chart or zero-upper-right diagonal chart. UALANG1 supplies the affine cocycle construction, and the monic quotient basis 1,x,y,xy proves global finiteness. All16 F2 fibres have exact type distribution 1^4:1, 2+2:3, 2+1+1:4, 3+1:4, 4:4. UAFINCOUNT1 therefore leaves ktdim_F2(S4) in {3,4}; over arbitrary characteristic-two bases it lies between two and four. The general lower bound uses constant geometric V4 monodromy of any quartic univariate Keller polynomial. Separately S4=AGL2(F2) gives canonical marked affine-bundle dimension exactly two. Every such affine-plane realization factors through the V4 invariant map (x^2+x,y^2+y), hence decomposes, matching the exception in UACANATOM1. The canonical absolute-atomicity minimum is between three and six, with six from the full matrix construction; intermediate dimensions are not settled. The four-coordinate fieldwise normal form is not asserted to glue canonically. The finite S4 map realizes individual A4-induced quartic algebras but has no global A4 frame, illustrating the essential framing qualification of UAFINITE1.

entries.title: Complete integrability normal form and sharp pole bound for every z-dependent rational sweep multiplier
entries.scope: Over algebraically closed characteristic-zero constants, every polynomial nilpotent normalization lambda*[[-rho,1],[-rho^2,rho]] with nonzero polynomial lambda, rho in k(w)[z] depending on z, and the wave integrability equation has, up to translations/scaling, rho=(kappa*z+R(w))/w, top_z(lambda)=w^r z^s,r>=2,s>=0,C(r,s)=r(r-1)+2kappa(r-1)(s+1)+kappa^2(s+1)(s+2)=0. The Laurent polynomial R is arbitrary subject exactly to r+(s+2)m>=2 when its least exponent m is negative; polynomial R has no extra condition. Writing lambda=sum f_b(w)z^b,f_s=w^r, the wave equation is a finite triangular Euler recursion: f_b is the negative coefficientwise division by C(a,b) of Q_b=2(b+1)w^2(R f_(b+1)/w)_prime+2kappa(b+1)(b+2)R f_(b+1)+(b+1)(b+2)R^2 f_(b+2). All divisions on polynomial exponents are nonzero below the top by the unique integer-pair lemma. Lowest-weight bottom coefficients prove the pole bound necessary; it makes the recursion polynomial and the squared denominator divide lambda, proving sufficiency. Polynomial X is then reconstructed uniquely up to translation from closed derivative pairs, with det JS=gamma^2. This classifies the entire z-dependent rational wave chart, including all positive z degrees in lambda, not arbitrary rational two-variable charts or all Keller fields. Universal recursion and polynomial potential proofs plus exact controls; no formal verification or independent whole-proof review.

entries.title: Exact composite degree and complete affine normalization boundary of the full rational sweep chart
entries.scope: In the complete KMFI41 chart remove affine terms from R by the polynomial coordinate isomorphism. If nonzero terms remain, let j be the largest exponent. The exact sweep degree is N=(s+2)(r+(s+1)j), composite for every admissible positive or negative j. Set V=X2-wX1,W=X3-zX1. The z-resultant of V+wY1-Y2 and W+zY1-Y3 has exact w valuation(s+1)(r-1); after removing it the degree is N, leading coefficient is nonzero constant and constant term is (-1)^(s+2)b^(s+1)Y2^(s+2),b=(r+2kappa(s+1))/((s+1)(s+2)). A weighted wave ODE proves the leading lambda has simple roots and avoids its singular point, making the two leading resultant equations coprime. Its full generic inertia is e^g 1^(N-(s+1)),g=gcd(s+1,r-1),e=(s+1)/g, by the complete Newton-Hensel initial system. entries.scope: For every z-dependent rho in k(w)[z] with polynomial nilpotent normalization and integrability, use KMFI41 parameters r,s,R. entries.title: Coordinate-invariant pole spectrum classifies the simple regular-coordinate sector and forces a global norm/conductor gate
entries.scope: For every valuation v of C(x,y), trivial on complex constants, with v(x)=-q<0 and v(y)>=0, the regular source polynomial coordinates are exactly a*y+b with a nonzero, and the set of negative coordinate pole orders is q times the positive integers. A written induction over the full Jung-van der Kulk alternating normal form, with Bruhat factorization of affine factors, proves the statement for every polynomial source automorphism, not just bounded words. Thus the minimum coordinate pole mu=q is invariant under marked normalization isomorphisms. For any smooth affine surface N containing the actual plane U=A2 with sole omitted line R, volume divisor div(dx wedge dy)=R and one source coordinate having v_R(y)=1 after a boundary-value shift, the entire normalization is covered by U and the second plane W=N minus the retained closed line y=0. The induced W->A1_y has all reduced affine-line fibers; the explicitly imported Miyanishi TIFR60 ChapterI Theorem4.1.1 supplies its triviality. The exact transition is y=u,x=u*t+h(u), with h=sum_(j=1)^q c_j*u^(-j), q>=1 and c_q nonzero. The full marked ring is C[y,f=x*y^q-H(y),a=x*f,b=x^2*y^(q-1)*f], H(y)=y^q*h(y); three principal localization recoveries and the unit identity (f+H)-f-y*H_1=c_q prove affineness uniformly. Marked isomorphisms are exactly those with the same q and coefficient rescaling c_j_prime=b*alpha^j*c_j, with nonzero alpha,b; polynomial source shears extending over the boundary have zero constant. No classification after forgetting the source open is asserted. The volume is exact exactly when c_1=0; a uniform triangular negative-part inverse of determinant c_q^(q-1) constructs a global regular primitive for every zero-residue principal part. An actual finite Keller map in this sector therefore requires q>=2, and no coordinate change can lower it to one. This sharpens PF2RULED37's explicit controls: every q>=2 control genuinely has no alternative multiplicity-one source-coordinate ruling and no valuation-preserving marked Wright comparison. These surfaces are geometric controls, not finite Keller examples. Under an actual finite Keller map of any field degree d with the one index-two boundary, the retained lines y=beta are closed and have finite birational immersive A1-normalized images D_beta. The nonimmersed omitted image C is distinct from all D_beta. Pushing forward the divisors of the integral y-beta gives Norm(y)=H_C*H_0 and Norm(y-beta)=H_beta for beta nonzero, up to nonzero constants. The reduced latter norm forces K(y)=C(N) by the norm tower formula. Its monic minimal polynomial has degree d, reduced irreducible immersed A1-normalized nonzero-parameter members and one reduced two-component zero member. Gwozdziewicz1993 Theorem1.1, explicitly pinned and imported, forces a self-collision in every D_beta because injectivity on one source line would make the Keller map an automorphism. Therefore C[P,Q,y] is not normal; its normalization identifies distinct source points with the same target and y, and the support of its conductor has a component dominating the y-line. The norm family is not a linear pencil or a target polynomial fibration, and a primitive integral coordinate is not asserted to generate the normal ring. One hundred exact controls check primary and predecessor seals, Bruhat factorization, concrete Laurent valuation controls, all-parameter chart and coefficient identities, constructive primitives and toy norm algebra; no finite Keller realization is constructed. The all-word, all-q, geometric, norm and conductor proofs are written, not inferred from these finite controls. entries.title: One pure trace fixes every parallel Hodge profile of a nonautomorphic unit-Hessian polynomial
entries.scope: For a four-variable polynomial f over a characteristic-zero field in actual affine coordinates (s,z), suppose its full Hessian is a nonzero constant and one scalar trace generic value fibre has Hodge polynomial t^2+kappa*t, t=u*v. Under hypothetical nonautomorphy the base-adapted Tang plane must have projection rank zero: rank one has fixed smooth Keller curve C and E=t^2+(d_s-c)*t+G*(u+v)+(R-c), so a pure trace forces actual A1 components and a plane, hence full gradient, inverse. Rank zero makes every scalar trace E=t^2-m_s*t with m_s>=0, supported at finitely many s, and its whole relative critical scheme is a finite disjoint union of reduced vertical A1s; no trace has an isolated critical point. Thus one pure trace and any parallel trace outside this nonpositive pure family force gradient invertibility. Different genus or constant coefficients of two parallel traces also suffice. A pure trace alone does not establish properness or a unit ideal. Actual polynomial trace equivalences and retained-dual automorphisms preserve the whole fibres, without nonlinear Hessian invariance.

entries.title: Every genuinely two-variable coefficient in H(U)+V*a(U,W) excludes a nonpositive pure trace
entries.scope: For h=H(U)+V*a(U,W) over a characteristic-zero field with deg H>=2 and positive W degree a, the generic whole value-fibre Hodge polynomial cannot equal t^2-m*t for any m>=0. With C=V(a)_red and d the generic degree of H on its nonconstant components, actual product strata give E=t^2-E(C)+d*t. Normalization gives E(C)=c*t-G*(u+v)+c-R-e, e=sum(branches_x-1)>=0. A nonpositive pure signature would force every normalization A1, all singularities unibranch and all components disjoint. Positive W degree supplies a nonvertical component whose U polynomial on A1 is surjective, excluding every vertical component by intersection. Thus d=(deg H)*sum deg(U on normalized components)>=2c, contradicting d+m=c. No smoothness, squarefreeness, monicity, finite projection, genus or degree bound is imposed. Combined with HC4MYHE0, this trace and any parallel pure trace force a polynomial gradient inverse under actual unit Hessian.

entries.title: One constant slice closes arbitrary q-independent r boundaries of y graphs in all degrees

entries.scope: In characteristic zero, pairwise disjoint conjugate irreducible hypersurfaces whose coordinate rings have only constant units have equal total degree. For any UFD A with fraction field F, if h in A[D] has zero constant coefficient and gcd one among its nonconstant coefficients, then F[h] intersect A[D] equals A[h]. entries.title: Complete16-slot mixed-weight(2,-1,-3) degree-seven class is automorphic
entries.scope: Over every characteristic-zero field, every three-variable polynomial Keller map with source/output weights(2,-1,-3) and ordinary degree<=7 is a polynomial automorphism. No collision, support or coefficient nonvanishing assumption is made; invertible diagonal linear part is normalized by output scaling. The complete16-slot model admits the nonzero-a double covera=s^2,b=u/s,c=v/s^3, F=(s^2f,s^-1g,s^-3h), where f=1+mu*u^2+nu*u*v+P*u^4+T*v^2 is even and g,h odd. An independent Fraction audit reconstructs the original universal determinant and the half-coefficient quotient identity. A written smooth-quartic boundary argument givesP*T=0: sign involution exchanges both infinity points, oddg has equal pole orderm at each, and the invariant rho=h/g^3 has finite pole degree6m but zeros of rho-rho(infinity) totaling8m+2. Two replayed cleared identities, with69 multiplier monomials and maximum degree7, then give(4muT-nu^2)^4=0 onP0 andnu^6=0 onT0. Complete transverse boundary degree reductions and a written parity-univariate coefficient argument exclude every remaining nonlinear first quotient, including all coefficient-zero strata. The audit checks source parity/bounds, complete linear parameterizations, the completed quartic and coefficient identities; curve/divisibility reasoning is written mathematics, not formalized. The f=1 family is a plane Keller map overK(a) of degree<=5, covered by the explicit Nakai-Baba1977 Theorem3(1)-(2) import. Its unimodular linear matrix overK[a] makes the unique formal inverse haveK[a] coefficients, so the generic polynomial inverse is global. The imported theorem is not re-proved. The original unrestricted20-second coefficient query and30-second raw12 real UNKNOWN remain preserved; generic full-field extra factors and eight fixed unit controls are retained but not used as global proof. This closes the mixed class only through degree7. KCUB18 subsequently closes weight(1,-1,-3) through degree7; other weights/degrees/coordinates, global sparsity/degree and special-form dimensions remain open.

entries.title: The full scaled Meng--Yang potential is globally polynomially right-equivalent to a nondegenerate five-variable quadratic
entries.scope: Over a characteristic-zero field with L*N nonzero, the retained HC5T1 Bezout completion and determinant-one row normalizer C0 give a global base-preserving polynomial ambient automorphism Phi=(x,y,T,Z,W) with Jacobian one and Psi=-M^2/(4L)+L*T^2+N*y*Z+2*N*x*W. entries.title: Quadratic plus one polynomial square and a nondegenerate ternary quadratic trace are all-degree HC4 invertibility criteria
entries.scope: Over C, if a four-variable polynomial f=q+c*R^2 with deg q<=2 and c nonzero has unit actual Hessian, its gradient is a polynomial automorphism, with no degree bound on R and no nonsingularity assumption on q. Under hypothetical nonautomorphy Tang supplies a constant jointly affine two-plane W. Degree in W forces R=R0(z)+a(z) dot w with W degree at most one; the constant quadratic W block makes every a_i*a_j constant, hence a constant. Also, any unit-Hessian f with one actual affine-hyperplane trace a nondegenerate ternary quadratic polynomial has invertible gradient. If W lies in that hyperplane, its two-dimensional isotropy contradicts rank three; otherwise one W direction lies in it and its derivative is nonconstant affine-linear on the trace. Joint-affine transport along the other W direction extends it globally as an affine-linear Keller component, again triangular. These are elementary all-degree arguments after Tang, without an additional Hodge or embedding-classification import. Multiple complex polynomial squares are not asserted covered by the one-square proof.

entries.title: Every parameterized affine graph in every constant direction of an ambient nondegenerate quadric closes, including its genuine Meng--Yang pullbacks
entries.scope: Over C let Q be any nondegenerate quadratic polynomial on A5, a a constant point, B a constant 5-by-4 matrix and v a constant vector with (B,v) invertible. entries.title: Every quadratic ambient hypersurface embedding with three affine retained source projections closes in all degrees

entries.title: Galois intermediate fields of etale maps with constant units and torsion target Picard group come from actual etale covers
entries.scope: For a separated dominant generically finite etale morphism S->T of smooth connected varieties over an algebraically closed field, with source units constant and target Picard group torsion, the omitted target set has codimension at least two. entries.title: Seven Gaussian-phase critical points and exhaustive nodal escape profiles with nonzero actions
entries.scope: Over C in characteristic zero, for every ternary cubic with irreducible nodal leading curve, nonisotropic node v and F2(v)=0, affine normalization gives P=T*(uv+h)+a*u^3+d*v^3+b*u^2+c*v^2+e*u+f*v+k with a*d!=0, while retaining the full transformed nondegenerate Gaussian quadratic Q including metric cross terms and means and m=Q_TT!=0. entries.title: Formal fixed-R gauge classification, global admission and necessary momentum escape
entries.scope: In the h-adic rank-two polynomial Weyl algebra, every identity-mod-h formal R-preserving endomorphism whose two position images have uniformly finite momentum order is automatically an automorphism, preserves the position algebra, and is a formal cotangent change followed by a positional gradient shift.
