entries.title: Every locally finite constant Nambu direction of a complex Keller map is locally nilpotent; one nonzero such direction closes a plane pair
entries.scope: For a complex Keller map F in any dimension, let delta_i be the polynomial Nambu derivations defined by delta_i(F_j)=delta_ij, and D_c=sum c_i delta_i for a constant complex direction c. These derivations commute by uniqueness of derivation extension to the finite separable source function field. If D_c is locally finite on the polynomial source algebra, it is locally nilpotent. A hypothetical eigenvector with nonzero complex eigenvalue lambda has nonzero field norm r in C(F), satisfying D_c r=[C(x):C(F)] lambda r. In affine target coordinates D_c is one partial derivative; a rational function has logarithmic derivative vanishing at infinity, excluding a nonzero constant. Every finite invariant subspace therefore has only the zero eigenvalue and is nilpotent. The locally finite directions form a complex linear subspace because commuting locally nilpotent derivations have locally nilpotent linear combinations. In dimension two one nonzero such direction forces the whole Keller inverse: choose target coordinates U,V with D_c U=1,D_c V=0; HC4MYHX0 makes its constants field C(V), its polynomial kernel is C[V], and the directly proved locally nilpotent slice formula gives C[x1,x2]=C[V,U]. No Rentschler or cancellation classification is imported. The one-direction inverse assertion is plane-only. For the canonical failed-direction IS model the explicit relative derivation N(f-T)=1,N(V)=0 is locally nilpotent iff its carried pair is invertible: its slice would make the generic source quotient a domain, whereas IS1 gives the product of d polynomial rings. A polynomial slice alone is not a nilpotence certificate. No arbitrary Nambu direction is asserted locally finite or any endpoint resolved.

entries.title: The actual Legendre energy detects the intrinsic HC4 finite-direction plane; a third independent direction or one nonzero square forces an inverse
entries.scope: For any complex Keller potential h put H=Hess h, F=grad h and G=x dot grad h-h. Direct multiplication gives delta_i G=x_i and D_c^2 G=c^T H^(-1)c. The following are equivalent for each constant c: finite-dimensional complex span of all iterated D_c derivatives of G; local finiteness of D_c on the whole polynomial source ring; local nilpotence of D_c; and D_c^m G=0 for some m. A constant-coefficient recurrence for G propagates through the commuting delta_i to every source generator, proving the first implication without a bounded derivative search. Write Lambda_h for these directions. In four variables a polynomial gradient automorphism has Lambda_h=C^4. Under nonautomorphy the retained Tang reduction and unique affine plane W give h=D(z)+w^T K(z), eta=grad D+DK^T w, and D_(a,b)=a dot partial_eta+(DK^(-1)b) dot partial_z holding eta fixed. If b is nonzero and this derivation locally finite, IT0 would invert K and hence grad h. Therefore Lambda_h=W^perp has dimension exactly two; the only possible HC4 dimensions are two and four. A third independent finite-energy direction forces a gradient inverse for every actual HC4 potential in all degrees, with no ambient observable, class-group or graph-shape hypothesis. In Tang coordinates G=z dot eta-D, so every finite direction under nonautomorphy has D_c^2 G=0. Thus a single finite-energy direction with nonzero inverse-Hessian square, or two finite directions with nonzero mixed inverse-Hessian pairing, also forces the inverse. Affine source coordinate covariance is checked on the actual energy and derivations; no nonlinear source Hessian invariance is used. No extra finite direction, finite-prefix termination or unrestricted HC4/JC2 closure is assumed.

entries.title: A nonautomorphic HC4 inverse-Hessian zero cone must be a linear two-plane; pure traces and finite-energy directions share the same intrinsic certificate space
entries.scope: For a complex four-variable unit-Hessian potential define Z_h={constant c in C^4: c^T (Hess h)^(-1)c=0 as a polynomial source identity}. It is cut out by homogeneous quadrics in four direction coordinates using all source coefficient matrices of the polynomial inverse Hessian. Every c in Z_h gives D_c^2 x_i=delta_i(D_c^2 G)=0 for all source coordinates, hence an explicit polynomial quasi-translation x->x+t (Hess h)^(-1)c with parameter-sign inverse, translating the actual gradient by t c. Thus Z_h lies in Lambda_h unconditionally. Under hypothetical nonautomorphy IT1 gives the converse and Z_h=Lambda_h=W^perp, exactly one linear two-plane. Any other exact cone shape forces the polynomial gradient inverse, including the zero cone, a line, a nonlinear cone or a cone spanning at least three directions. Two zero-square directions whose sum has nonzero square are an exact nonlinearity certificate. A linear two-plane is not a converse: h=s^4+t^4+su+tv has that exact cone and an explicit gradient inverse; a transverse direction has nonzero square and energy termination exactly at order five. Consequently any mixture of exact pure-trace covectors, exact finite-energy directions and exact zero-square covectors whose combined span has dimension at least three forces the inverse, in every source and embedding degree. In particular two independent pure traces plus one transverse finite-energy direction suffice. entries.title: Integral projectivity and lattice rigidity of finite quantum graph carriers
entries.scope: Over R=K[[t]] in characteristic zero with quantum parameter a(t)=t^e*u(t), e>=1, every finite-left R-flat full Weyl bimodule whose identified special module is the rank-one graph S_psi is projective over A_R itself. Generic projectivity uses Kanel-Belov-Fedorov Lemma3.1; a self-contained central-fiber Ext argument glues it with special freeness: positive finite Ext groups are t-divisible and killed by a bounded central power, hence zero. Finite global dimension of the iterated Ore extension shortens a finite projective resolution. Thus a finite normalized corner certificate E^2=E, E0=e11, r_i=E*r_i*E, [r_i,r_j]=a(t)*J_ij*E, r_i0=psi_i*e11 is necessary and sufficient for existence of such a carrier, not merely sufficient. A three-factor elementary stabilization adds one zero coordinate to a projective presentation and normalizes E0 without inverting arbitrary lifted special-frame products. For any fixed full rational right Weyl action on D^r, there is at most one full finite left A-lattice inside that space. The intersection is full by Ore clearing; finite left torsion bimodule quotients vanish by Bernstein inequality for A_(2n). This is valid for every finite generic rank and all degrees. For a rank-one special graph, sub-quantum divided left/right differences are S-linear scalars. Finitely many polynomial left corrections automatically improve the graph congruence from modulo t to modulo a(t). For two parameter graph lattices with the same fixed rational action, the least central shift gives a nonzero special map f. Scalar corrections agree on both lattices. Quantum-order Hamiltonian connections give X_i(f) in f*S; the full symplectic frame forces f to be a nonzero constant. The cokernel is t-divisible and killed by a bounded central power, so the lattices differ only by a central t power at every ramification order. Their generic module is free exactly when the fixed rational full action becomes polynomial in some D-frame. No proper nonzero left ideal is preserved by a full polynomial Weyl tuple, in any degree. Written proofs cover all ranks, degrees and parameter orders; exact controls verify elementary normalization and six corner relations for independent h,t, ramified scalar corrections, full Hamiltonian frame inversion and failure of uniqueness with only one right coordinate. Fixed rational-action uniqueness does not compare arbitrary formal gauges. Rank-one scalar correction is not automatic for higher special rank or torsion. Integral projectivity is not freeness. No actual Long carrier, bounded scalar lift, all-representative nonlifting, DC2/JC2 solution, independent theorem replay, formal verification, external review or novelty priority is claimed.

entries.title: All odd dihedral degrees: formal splitting on the entire ramification curve and branch-avoiding cubic index
entries.scope: Let A=C[x,y], G nonconstant reduced irreducible, S=Spec A[z]/(z^2-G), tau(z)=-z. For ANY connected finite etale cyclic torsor T->S of odd degree n>=3 with an involution sigma over tau conjugating the cyclic action by inversion, its class chi satisfies tau*chi=-chi. The inclusion of the ENTIRE possibly singular ramification curve C=V_S(z) is fixed scheme-theoretically, so restriction is killed by both2 and n and is ZERO as a torsor class, not just as a line bundle on the normalization. Thus T|C is n globally labelled copies of C, with singular gluing retained. PF55 units and Kummer norm also give this for every odd Kummer class on S. This does NOT imply Pic(S)[n]=0. For EVERY m>=1, C->S_m=Spec(A/(G^m))[z]/(z^2-G) is nilpotent, and Stacks06NE/0ALI gives a unique compatible lift of the labelled splitting. On labels sigma is i->a-i; odd n gives one fixed label and (n-1)/2 swapped pairs. Invariants commute with reduction by averaging, giving the reflection quotient B/G^m B = A_m x (A_m[z]/(z^2-G))^((n-1)/2). Connected T makes B a normal integral rank-n finite locally free A-algebra. Distinct complex constants c0,...,c_h give formal generator (c0,c1+z,...,c_h+z), polynomial (W-c0)*product((W-ci)^2-G). The confluent Vandermonde determinant modulo G is a nonzero constant. Lift this element to B at any prescribed finite order: its nonzero power-basis index is a unit modulo G, so its index divisor is disjoint from C and it generates B on an open neighbourhood of the WHOLE branch. This is all odd cyclic/dihedral degrees and all branch degrees, without a rationality, immersion or A1-normalization assumption; arbitrary Sd and even-degree covers are not asserted. For the actual quartic cubic B=C3, choose formal trace-zero element (2,-1+z). Its polynomial is (W-2)((W+1)^2-G)=W^3-(3+G)W-2+2G, and its product-basis index is9-G. Normalize the global determinant to trace discriminant4G; in the connected G-adic completion its ratio to the formal determinant has square1, hence a constant sign; choose the positive orientation. For EVERY m a global trace-zero primitive t_m then has F_m=W^3-3a_m W-2b_m with a_m=1+G/3,b_m=1-G and normalized index I_m=1-G/9 modulo G^m, and the EXACT relation a_m^3-b_m^2=3G I_m^2. Thus I_m=1 on C and V(I_m) avoids C. PF56 makes EACH such I_m nonconstant throughout the actual quartic packet, for all source orders/rulings and target degrees. Different m may require different t_m; one element agreeing at every order would have the reducible formal polynomial globally, impossible for a primitive cubic field element. This does not force arbitrary primitive indices away from C. Oka's smooth Cstar branch has nonzero Pic3 but its Kummer function restricts to a cube on the branch, confirming that formal branch splitting does not imply global splitting or Picard vanishing. The A1 inner-A5 torus cubic has a triple-root fibre and only quasi-etale sign triple, so fails the necessary finite-etale hypothesis. The square index in the norm relation is retained; PF56 pure irreducible power difference cannot be applied by deleting it, and removing the index curve changes the affine source of its logarithmic argument. Any further exclusion must use a genuinely global invariant and the shared normal cubic/quartic conductor plus marked A2 source or Picard/linking, rather than larger finite branch jets or an assumed injective odd-Picard restriction. Written unbounded proofs plus exact symbolic/CRT controls; Stacks nilpotent invariance imported externally, no independent full reproof/formal verification/external review/novelty priority. No Pic3 vanishing, affine Keller realization, whole quartic or higher-degree Keller exclusion, or completed research goal.

entries.title: A closed affine base plane with constant quadratic trace restricts the helper rank to a reduced plane component
entries.scope: Let Q be a nondegenerate quadratic polynomial on A5 with critical point o and value lambda, and b1,b2 independent affine linear ambient functions vanishing at o. Suppose a genuine closed embedding j(z,w) retains b composed with j=w and Q composed with j(z,0)=mu is constant. Closed base change embeds the actual A2_z as a closed surface in the helper A3 at b=0. The restricted helper quadratic has rank r in {1,2,3}. With m=mu-lambda, the image equals one irreducible component of q_r=m by its prime height-one ideal and dimension. Rank three is impossible: at m=0 the irreducible cone is singular, and at m!=0 the smooth quadric XY+Z^2=m has exact class group Z^2/Z diagonal=Z by its factorial Laurent chart and two reduced removed lines. Rank two at m!=0 is impossible because XY=m has a nonconstant unit. At rank two and m=0 the image is one reduced plane component, whose other two helper coordinates are an actual polynomial coordinate pair of z. At rank one the image is a plane X=c with c^2=m, with its other two coordinates a source coordinate pair, including the reduced image at the double equation X^2=0. This classification requires the actual closed zero-section, not an arbitrary dominant surface map or generic immersion. All embedding and coefficient degrees are unrestricted, and no source Hessian assumption or general affine-surface rectification is needed.

entries.title: Retaining the intrinsic free projections at the ambient critical-value trace forces the Keller inverse without a fibre-affine embedding hypothesis
entries.scope: Let a genuine closed quadratic-ambient embedding retain the two intrinsic free variables through independent affine linear ambient projections centered at the unique ambient critical point. Suppose its actual potential is Q composed with j=lambda+w1 K1(z)+w2 K2(z), where lambda is the ambient critical value and K is plane Keller. Then K and the four-variable gradient are polynomial automorphisms, in all degrees and with arbitrary polynomial dependence of the other three embedding coordinates on all four source variables. The rank-three helper quadric is excluded by IU0. Constant ambient normal forms at rank two and one are XY+w1 Z+gamma w2^2, gamma!=0, and X^2+w1Y+w2Z respectively. In rank two the closed zero-section has X0=0,Y0=a,Z0=d with (a,d) a source coordinate pair. First free differentiation gives K=(d+a X_w1|0,a X_w2|0), so in actual (a,d) coordinates it restricts on a=0 to (d,0); retained Gwozdziewicz one-line injectivity gives its inverse. In rank one the same first jet is K=(a,d) directly. Higher free jets of every helper are unrestricted and no fibre-affine hypothesis is imposed. More generally the criterion covers ambient projections pulling back to A w+v(z), with constant A in GL2(C) and arbitrary polynomial v, when D-v^T A^(-T)K=lambda: the actual (z,b) potential is literally lambda+b^T A^(-T)K, whose Hessian is checked from that form. A base-dependent frame is not assumed to preserve its Keller pair. For a different constant trace mu!=lambda only the rank-one chart remains; its first jet is K=(a+2c X_w1|0,d+2c X_w2|0), c!=0,c^2=mu-lambda. This noncritical rank-one chart is not claimed solved. entries.title: A universal noncritical cotangent substitution has unit Hessian but its global immersion obligation already forces the plane Keller inverse
entries.scope: For any complex plane Keller pair K normalized to J(K)=1 and nonzero c, put A=(K(z)-z)/(2c), H=w dot A, and J_c,K(z,w)=(w1,w2,c+H,z1-H A1,z2-H A2). This polynomial substitution pulls X^2+w1Y+w2Z back exactly to c^2+w dot K, has actual unit Hessian, and has an embedded noncritical zero-section. If it is an immersion at every source point, then K is a polynomial automorphism; closed embedding is stronger. At a point write B=DA. If Bv=theta v, theta!=0, and A is not parallel to v, choose w with w dot v=0 and w dot A=1/theta. The full substitution then kills tangent (v,0). Global immersion excludes distinct eigenvalues on the dense nonzero-A locus, since det(I+2c B)=1 forbids a lone nonzero eigenvalue. Thus the discriminant vanishes identically, and tr B+2c det B=0 leaves only tr B=det B=0 or tr B=-2/c,det B=1/c^2. In the first case DA is nilpotent; in the second D(K+z) is nilpotent. The needed plane nilpotent-Jacobian inverse lemma is proved directly using the retained generative-polynomial input: algebraically dependent components factor through h, trace zero makes generic level components parallel lines, hence a fixed linear form triangularizes epsilon z+P for every epsilon!=0. No such lemma is asserted in higher dimensions. The implication is not a converse: K=(s+t^2,t+(s+t^2)^2/3), c=1 is an actual plane automorphism, but at z=(0,1),w=(3,-3) the substitution kills the nonzero source tangent (1,1,0,0), although the pullback Hessian is one. Therefore neither unit Hessian nor the embedded zero-section supplies a global immersion. The full noncritical rank-one embedding problem outside this exact family, both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open.

entries.title: Linear and quadratic multiplier factors are eigen-polynomials of the projective automorphism
entries.scope: For any rankr>=2, degreed>=1 andV=(u^d,u^d*v(x/u)) withv polynomial automorphic of degree<=d, let nonzero homogeneousF give normalizedH=F*V. Full rank is not required for this divisor lemma. Every irreducible factorq ofFbar=F(1,x) of degree1 or2 satisfiesq(v)=c*q with nonzero constantc. The determinant gate givesh=lambda*u^(d-1), and the exact projective characteristic-resolvent identity has no q-divisor pole for independentT because its denominator is monic inT. The separate factor residue therefore givesdq*W0 anddq*B*W0 moduloq forW=v-x,B=Dv. SinceW preserves(q), the identityW^2q=Hessq(W,W)+dq*(B-I)*W makes the Hessian term divisiblebyq. Finite quadratic Taylor expansion givesq dividesq(v), and automorphy preserves irreducibility, so the quotient is a constant unit. The linear case uses only the first residue. This is unbounded in totalF degree, factor multiplicity, rank and direction degree. It does not assert invariance for higher-degree factors or that discrete preservation suffices for normalization.

entries.scope: For normalized full-rankH=F*V in rank4, V homogeneous quadratic,V0=u^2, and nonaffine projectivev, F has no irreducible homogeneous quadratic factor in any total scalar degree. If its leading quadraticq2 has rank3, q2 vanishes on the dense quadratic image plane, impossible for a nondegenerate ternary quadratic form. entries.title: Composition duality and nonfinite boundaries of quantum graph carriers
entries.scope: For characteristic-zero finite-left parameter-flat full Weyl graph carriers over K[[t]] with common quantum parameter a(t)=t^e*u(t), e>=1, forward tensor composition is again a full finite graph carrier. The classical point map is chi composed with psi. Generic left and right division indices separately multiply, as do completed degrees delta. Thus the ratio N/delta multiplies and strict generic index excess cannot cancel under finite forward composition. No generic index symmetry is assumed. In every rank at least three, k-fold composition of the actual QNI1 identity family gives genuine polynomial full lifts with both generic indices3^k, completed degree1, forward degree at most12^k and arbitrary identity contact, for every k>=1. At contact order at least two they remain formally inner. This gives unbounded actual index loss, not a rank-two example or a forward bound independent of k. Every finite full graph carrier is also an integral projective generator: its trace ideal is all A_R because the quotient has zero special and generic fibers, is centrally bounded torsion and parameter-divisible. Its left algebraic dual is finite on the target right side, not automatically on the source left side. For C=M tensor_(B_R) Mdual, evaluation onto A_R is surjective. Its special fiber is the classical self-product T=S tensor_(S_B) S, and the evaluation kernel reduces exactly to its off-diagonal component Tprime. A characteristic-zero polynomial etale self-map of affine space has finite self-product projection exactly when it is an automorphism: its image omits no divisor; fpqc descent, purity across the codimension>=2 complement and constant affine-space covers prove the assertion. Therefore for every noninvertible symplectic classical map, C and its evaluation kernel are not finite as left A_R-modules. No generic nonfiniteness follows merely from this special-fiber argument. For Long, on the actual source chart S0=K[r,r^-1,v,v^-1,a,d], the cubic F(X) factors (X-a)*G(X) with G(a)=2v. The diagonal idempotent is G(b)/(2v). Since (w-A)*(w+A)=-8*r*v is a unit, admission of that second affine source point requires w inverse. Thus its actual off-diagonal ring is S0[w,w^-1]/(w^2-Q), finite etale over S0[Q^-1] but nonfinite over S0. The branch Q=0 is inside the source. entries.title: Rational recovery through any retained profile forces the exact native target-shear orbit
entries.scope: Characteristic zero, one UAM1 normalized block with retained identities u. Let H be ANY whole retained profile and T ANY whole polynomial native Keller map on the same source, without degree or affine-r restrictions. Rational output recovery T in k(u,H), an actual polynomial target factor T=E composed H, and the explicit formula T=(sigma,Bh+sigma^5*Ch^3*h(u,sigma,Ch),Ch) with unique polynomial h are equivalent. UAQFSAT1 makes rational recovery polynomial. The source x=0 plane forces E to retain u,a and fix c=0 pointwise. Its generic plane pair is Keller; the published HC4MYGL0 line theorem makes it an automorphism. UANATIVEORBIT1 then gives the exact global landing ideal (a^5*c^3). UANATIVE2GEN1 supplies native module membership, UAPROFILE1 whole profile landing and UAALLATOM1 inherited degree and absolute stable atomicity. Thus the conditional UACUBICDESC1 native branch with target factor degree greater than one is EMPTY, and vanishing cubic remainders characterize exactly the cubic target-shear orbit of degree3. Cout genuinely nonlinear in r excludes EVERY literal retained-profile first factor, not only the old cubic. Distinct retained profiles have incomparable literal output fields; this does not classify them after arbitrary source changes. A hypothetical finite polynomial integration of the UASELFFORMAL1 tangent would generically escape all these first factors; none is constructed. Mutually changing blocks, arbitrary intermediate maps, source changes moving the signal and full canonical stable atomicity remain outside.

entries.title: A positive polynomial section of a smooth affine four-quadric has the same infinite-order integral middle class as its positive zero-section plane

entries.scope: On V={x^2+w1 y1+w2 y2=c^2} over C with c!=0, the two complex planes P={w=0,x=c} and S={y=0,x=c} have the same integral Borel-Moore class alpha, of infinite order. After scaling c=1, P meets the compact real S4 given by x real,y=conjugate(w),x^2+|w|^2=1 transversely at one point, giving integral pairing +/-1. In coordinates a=(w+y)/2,b=(w-y)/(2i), rotation of the two b coordinates through pi preserves the quadric and exchanges both w-y pairs; its proper homotopy sends P to S with their complex orientations. entries.title: Finite matrix actions energy connection and primitive admission
entries.scope: In characteristic zero, restriction of differential operators along a finite free polynomial-coordinate map B/A gives a faithful matrix source Weyl action by chain rule, without etaleness. In an A-basis beta, a derivation h*delta acts as sum M_delta(F_alpha)*p_alpha+h*C_delta. More generally differential operator order does not increase under this finite free restriction, giving a map of Rees differential-operator algebras. For any monic univariate f of degree m, the companion pair Z, T=fprime(Z)*p+h*C with C_(j-1,j)=j satisfies [T,Z]=h*I. Its spatial degrees are at most1,2 independently of m. For f=z^m, Z^m=x*I and deg Z^k=ceil(k/m), so powers grow as required by QCI1. The actual branch term h*C breaks the classical factorization T0=Z0*(m*Z0^(m-2)*p); Z^-1*C has entry1/x. Thus classical factorization alone does not exclude a full quantum matrix action. For QIM1 varying smooth elliptic family, E(u)=u/(3b), E(v)=v/(2b), E(b)=1 lifts by E(w)=w/(6b). The matrix connection is C_E=diag(0,1/(6b),1/(3b)), with [E,delta]=delta/(6b). Its mixed curvature identity gives the full source surface differential action and all six physical rank-two Weyl relations through D_x=-(Y/b)*Z-3*X^2*P_B and D_y=(2X/(3b))*Z+2Y*P_B. Here [P_B,b]=h, so energy is noncentral, but x,y remain commuting positions. The physical-coordinate model is localized at b. It also has global logarithmic energy L_B=b*P_B with [L_B,b]=h*b, rather than a Weyl relation with b. Neither action has the identified rank-one Long graph. For any R-flat module over a DVR, an actual generic inverse of an endomorphism whose special map is injective preserves the integral lattice; hence an injective nonsurjective special map cannot become a generic unit. In a directly finite generic endomorphism algebra, the exact relation Y=X*W together with either [Y,X]=a*I or [T,X]=0,[T,Y]=a*I forces X to be a unit. Since det X0=-4b is nonzero and nonunit on the elliptic monic special module, no global finite extension with that special module can retain this exact primitive and either full relation pattern, for any quantum correction degrees or ramification order. Dropping explicit x inverse but retaining the primitive does not repair admission. Quantum relations which break Y=X*W are not excluded. The finite-free polynomial construction is the regular source differential division action of degree m over the target division ring. It is irreducible there and admits no rational rank-one compression when m>1. Its commutant has no nontrivial idempotents, so this same action cannot extend from A_n to Mat_k(A_n), k>1. Universal statements are written proofs; exact controls check symbolic monic degrees2,3,5, elliptic energy connection and both sets of six Weyl relations. entries.title: A plane Keller map is invertible if it is an isomorphism over the entire inverse image of one irreducible contractible target curve
dependencies: external: Lin-Zaidenberg classification including smooth AMS case, Palka arXiv1405.5391v2 Theorem A; newly imported without independent reproof
entries.scope: Let K be complex plane Keller and A a reduced irreducible closed target curve which is topologically contractible. If the entire reduced K inverse image C maps isomorphically onto A, then K is a polynomial automorphism. This requires the complete preimage, not one selected branch or an injective normalization. The new explicit external input is Lin-Zaidenberg in Palka1405.5391v2 Theorem A, including its smooth AMS case: a contractible plane curve is polynomially rectified to x^p=y^q with coprime positive exponents. Apply independent source and target rectifications. In the singular case the abstract cusp-ring isomorphism extends to normalizations t->a t and preserves the valuation semigroup, recovering the same unordered exponents. No arbitrary curve isomorphism is assumed ambient extendible. Complete prime support and HW0 square-free pullback give h(K)=c g with multiplicity one. Smooth coordinate-line pencils have genus zero and one puncture. Singular monomial pencils x^p-y^q=t have genus (p-1)(q-1)/2 and one puncture, by the degree-p Kummer cover with q finite simple total ramification points and one point at infinity. IY0 therefore forces degree one in every coprime cusp degree, and retained Keller denominator removal gives the actual inverse. The classification input is explicitly imported, not certified by finite symbolic samples.

entries.title: Primitive-unit rigidity for cofinite etale surface maps from the hyperbola complement
entries.scope: Over any characteristic-zero field K let U=Spec K[S,Y,(1-SY)^(-1)], r=1-SY. A dominant etale g:U->V to a smooth geometrically integral AFFINE surface, with at most finitely many missing target points and a unit v with v composed g=r, is an isomorphism. This sharpens the UAINTERSURF1 generic source-surface setting without a degree bound or presumed plane structure of V. On the generic unit fibre a surjective etale Gm map has smooth projective completion genus zero by classical Riemann-Hurwitz and a rational point. Its boundary has at most two rational points; the affine-line alternative has a Laurent-unit derivative and omits a value, so the target fibre is split Gm and the covering is c(r)*S^e. Its cyclic deck action extends to the ENTIRE U by (S,Y)->(zeta*S,zeta^(-1)*Y) and fixes the retained node. Differentiating g composed h=g at that node contradicts etaleness unless abs(e)=1. A birational etale open immersion with finite complement between normal affine surfaces is an isomorphism by Hartogs. The proof is geometric and descends. Primitive unit index, the retained node, affineness and cofinite image are actual hypotheses. The all-degree J_d self-maps have unit index d and are not counterexamples. Explicit invariant quotients UV=(1-r)^d display the singular retained node for d>1; no general quotient-classification theorem is imported. No assertion about arbitrary unit-free intermediate surfaces or whole canonical atomicity is made.

entries.title: All-degree Seifert base-genus quotient and companion permutation-tree obstruction; 32 further quartic tree representations excluded
entries.scope: General integral topology at ALL finite cover degrees and ALL cabling lengths: for a connected compact orientable 3-manifold assembled by gluing connected pieces along boundary tori and filling others by solid tori, select the Seifert pieces whose base surfaces are ORIENTABLE. Projection followed by capping all base boundaries induces H1(piece)->>Z^(2g), killing the ENTIRE H1 image of EVERY boundary torus. Standard handle loops lift and close along connected circle fibres, proving surjectivity. Arbitrary boundary gluing and meridian/fibre/other slope fillings therefore preserve these handle quotients. Mayer-Vietoris gives 0->C->H1(M)->H1(piece graph)->0, C the cokernel of edge maps after fillings; C surjects all capped-base H1 and the free graph quotient splits. Thus H1(M)->>Z^(b1(G)+2sum g_v), and b1(M)>=b1(G)+2sum g_v. No incompressibility, minimal JSJ decomposition, cyclic/regular cover, simple branching or special surgery slope is needed. Under PF61's actual SMOOTH affine extension containing A2 with ENTIRE DISJOINT A1 boundary, finite end H1 forces BOTH the whole orbit graph to be a tree and EVERY selected lifted base to be planar. Higher-degree smoothness is NOT automatic. For one connected piece orbit, regular-fibre permutation H is central; its cycles all have common length m. These fibre orbits F=Omega/<H>, NOT raw sheets, give base degree n=|Omega|/m. Induced cone/boundary monodromies give chi(Btilde)=n(2-2h-b-j)+sum cone cycle counts and boundary count=sum boundary cycle counts; derive exact genus at unrestricted degree. For torus companion H=a^p=b^q,M=a^u b^v,qu+pv1, induced cone counts equal counts(a),counts(b) since the powers are units, so 2g=n+2-cycles(a)-cycles(b)-cycles(M). Cable annulus/one-cone formula is analogous. In arbitrary degree with BOTH companion and adjacent cable actions transitive and companion image CENTRELESS, H1 and L=M^-pq, so PF62's tree condition makes M a full d-cycle; genus0 then forces cycles(a)+cycles(b)=d+1, equivalently the connected bipartite cycle graph of a^u,b^v with d sheet edges is a TREE. Applies in particular to an Sd companion for d>=3, but GLOBAL Sd does NOT imply a piece has Sd. Quartic application audits all596 periodic conjugacy classes in PF63's1152cells:112 already have graph cycles,484 tree;32 additional TREE classes have genus1 companion and b1end>=2, all S4/S4 with torus generator orders3 and4. They occupy8 residue cells,4classes each;452 tree classes have genus0 before other gates. NO whole formerly nonempty residue cell closes, and no other PF65-68 gate is counted into452. S4/S4 genus0 noncyclic survivors must have a transposition and a3cycle among torus generators; the whole S4/S4 sector is NOT excluded. Exact exponent12 shows genus is constant for every ACTUAL COPRIME exponent/winding lift, not by bounded interpolation. Full ordinary-word satellite controls p3q4r3 andp3q16r3 have H1Z2; p15q4r3 andp3q4r15 have Z2 plusZ5, confirming the quotient. Critical dropped-hypothesis control: cyclic4 T2,3 has nonidentity H=M2 and fibre degree2, base degree2/genus0; using all4raw sheets falsely gives genus1, while its r3 satellite genuinely has finite H1Z3. The p2q3r9 genus0 S4/S4 control still has H1Z24, nonzero R mark and quotientZ6, so this sector remains OPEN. entries.scope: Let K:A2->A2 be complex plane Keller, R=C[z], B=C[T] through K, and f nonconstant with B->R/(f) surjective. JA0 gives kernel (a), a(K)=f g and the unit ideal (f,g)=R. entries.title: All-degree peripheral cone torsion and individual-mark budget; quartic S4/S4 even first exponent forced to2
entries.scope: General ALL-DEGREE/ALL-CABLING-LENGTH integral obstruction: for connected pieces glued along boundary tori and filled by solid tori, select Seifert pieces with ORIENTABLE bases. Quotient each piece H1 by ALL boundary-torus classes and its regular fibre. With base genus g and cone orders alpha_i this is Z^(2g) plus T=(direct sum Z/alpha_i)/<(1,...,1)>, directly from the abelian Seifert presentation. Every edge map vanishes in these groups; Mayer-Vietoris and splitting of the free graph quotient give H1(end)->>H1(piece graph) plus direct sum of selected Q_v. This is a QUOTIENT, NOT an asserted subgroup/direct summand of H1. Every filling CORE maps to zero since a complementary boundary slope represents its core class. Consequently the quotient factors through all such marked cores, including every actual ramified omitted-prime end knot. In PF61's actual SMOOTH affine extension containing A2 with b ENTIRE DISJOINT omitted A1s, each individual knot K_i is the corresponding standard dual covector by its relative Thom class. For ANY subset I of s omitted knots actually identified as filling cores, H1(end)/<K_i:i in I> is generated by b-s elements. Thus at EVERY prime ell, b1(piece graph)+sum_v[2g_v+max(N_v(ell)-1,0)]<=b-s, where N_v counts lifted cone orders divisible byell. This individual-mark bound needs NO PRIMITIVITY of the canonical vector and works at arbitrary ramification indices; I contains all actual ramified omitted primes. All explicit smoothness, whole-line, orientable-base and actual-mark hypotheses are required, not automatic in arbitrary higher degree. entries.title: A nonlinear polynomial in a semisimple quadratic pencil forbids unit Hessian throughout every polynomial source orbit, in every dimension and outer degree
entries.scope: Over C let q_A=x^T A x be a nondegenerate homogeneous quadratic form in n>=1 variables and q_B=x^T B x nonzero, with T=A^(-1)B diagonalizable over C. For any H in C[t] of degree>=2, no polynomial source automorphism Phi makes h composed with Phi, h=q_A+H(q_B), have nonzero constant Hessian determinant. Both forms have a common center; arbitrary independent linear terms are not silently admitted. Simultaneous normalization is proved from A-self-adjointness and nondegenerate orthogonal eigenspaces. Retained HG0, also reproduced here, forces all native critical Hessian determinants to have one common nonzero value under a hypothetical unit-Hessian source reparameterization. Resonance 1+lambda Hprime(0)=0 already makes the origin degenerate. A repeated nonzero eigenvalue otherwise gives a positive-dimensional critical quadric. With all nonzero eigenvalues lambda_i simple, put p=Hprime, m=deg p>=1, b=p(0), P(s)=product(1+lambda_i s), C_i=product_{j!=i}(1-lambda_j/lambda_i). Roots r of p(r)=-1/lambda_i are nonzero and must be simple; their axis critical Hessians are 2^n times 2 lambda_i r pprime(r) C_i, whereas the origin gives 2^n P(b). Equality at every root forces p(t)=a t^m+b. The remaining equalities require P(b)=2m(s_i-b)Pprime(s_i) at all s_i=-1/lambda_i. Hence R(s)=2m(s-b)Pprime(s)-P(b)=2mk P(s), where k>=1 counts the nonzero eigenvalues. At s=b this says (2mk+1)P(b)=0, impossible. This is an all-degree proof, not bounded spectral, jet or source-degree checking, and uses neither Tang nor an unresolved Keller theorem. The diagonalizability hypothesis is essential: q_A=2xy+z^2+w^2, q_B=x^2 gives a nonzero square-zero T, and q_A+H(x^2) has Hessian determinant -16 and an explicit polynomial gradient inverse for every H. Nonsemisimple pencils, independently shifted quadratics and unrestricted HC4/JC2 are not classified. Current frontier update: HC4MYJE0 now inverse-closes every nonnilpotent common-center Jordan configuration under unit Hessian, and HC4MYJE1 reduces the entire admitted centered quadratic-composite graph family to the old singleton-zero endpoint. The earlier nonzero-Jordan open-frontier wording is historical, not an active remaining gate. The original semisimple nonexistence and nilpotent orbit theorems are retained; no unit-Hessian nonexistence theorem for all nonnilpotent pencils is asserted. Independent centers, arbitrary image geometry, the singleton-zero endpoint and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open.

entries.scope: Let Q(u,X)=q_A(u)+alpha X^2+beta X+gamma be a nondegenerate quadratic on A5, with u in A4, det A!=0 and alpha!=0. entries.scope: Characteristic zero, actual proper native/witness retained-signal intermediate of UAINTERSURF1, both whole factors noninvertible. UAUNITFACT1 supplies constant geometric units and a retained-field rational point. Every geometric AFFINE-type A1-ruling has base A1. The actual canonical volume makes its Hamiltonian derivation i_D omega=df regular and locally nilpotent: on the generic fibre the volume coefficient is a unit of K(f)[w], hence a scalar in K(f)*. Two inequivalent affine-type rulings have kernels with constant intersection, forcing trivial ML; UAMLFACTOR1 excludes this for a proper factor. Thus the affine-type ruling class is UNIQUE and necessarily Galois invariant. Choose a finite Galois definition field L, center f at the rational point and take h=sum sigma(c*(f-f(P))). Linear independence of field automorphisms supplies c for which h is nonzero, invariant and a scalar multiple of the original coordinate. Hence h lies in A and gives the actual ruling over K0. Its Hamiltonian derivation also descends and is nonzero locally nilpotent. No arithmetic UFD is transported to L. UAARITHRULING1 applies AFTER this proved descent, giving integral arithmetic fibres, reduced geometric fibres and a finite plane atlas; any such proper target would disprove JC(2). The standard surface additive-action quotient theorem identifies existence of a geometric affine-type ruling, a retained-field ruling, a geometric additive action and a retained-field additive action. CONDITIONAL on JC(2), proper native intermediates are therefore geometrically additively RIGID, ML=A, and all geometric rulings provided by UALOGVOL1 have complete base P1. A complete-type ruling cannot itself be Galois invariant in the actual arithmetic-UFD branch, since its descent would inject Pic(P1) into Pic(V)=0. UAGEOPIC1 makes the norm of a finite orbit of ruling line bundles trivial but this does not identify the rulings. Exact conjugate polynomial coordinates on A2, both centered at a rational point, have trace x+4*x^2*y with generic fibre Gm, disproving arbitrary averaging as a descent shortcut. Published rigid surfaces with inequivalent complete-type rulings prevent replacing affine-type uniqueness by general ruling uniqueness. Complete-type Galois-permuted ruling descent and absolute stable atomicity remain OPEN; no extra orbifold or degree condition is added.

entries.title: Degree dependence is necessary for pure tests and safe mixed cutoffs
entries.scope: For every fixed n,D a finite ordinary moment ideal prefix exists by Noetherianity, without an effective stopping certificate. No finite pure test works across all degrees in dimension2 or above: P_d=Z+W^d has E exp(sP_d)=exp(s^(d+1)) and first nonzero moment d+1. Even among homogeneous ternary degree-d forms, H_d=Z^d+W^(d-1)T has first nonzero moment2d-1 for even d and4d-2 for odd d, by exact balance and parity. For the already classified GMC-safe shears S_k=W+Z^kT-Z^(2k+1)/2, E(W exp(sS_k))=-s^(2k+1)/2; thus no C independent of deg P makes m>C deg Q sufficient, even for fixed Q=W. Written formulas hold for all indices;228 finite comparisons are auxiliary. No new fixed-cubic lower bound, unrestricted GMC theorem, or novelty claim. Internal written proof; finite exact transcription checks do not certify the universal argument. Independent replay, external review and formal verification remain false.

entries.title: All-degree support-universal Gaussian nullity and generic first moment
entries.scope: In any dimension with circular pairs and independent real spectators, for a finite nonempty monomial support A with independent coefficients c_a, every positive pure moment polynomial is identically zero iff zero lies outside the convex hull of the angular charges a_Z-a_W. Equivalently an integral strict separator exists. If the hull contains zero, doubling an integer balanced occupation resolves every real parity and gives a positive nonzero coefficient in a moment polynomial. The least balanced even-parity occupation length mu is the generic first nonzero moment; the exceptional coefficient hypersurface can cancel it. On separated support, eta.chi>=delta>0 gives E(QP^m)=0 for m>-L/delta, where L is the least eta-charge in Q, hence m>(max|eta_i|/delta)deg Q suffices. This classifies universal/generic coefficients, not every specialized null polynomial: balanced-support safe shears and failures both exist. The separation mechanism is retained prior work; this is an elementary synthesis without novelty claim. Internal written proof; finite exact transcription checks do not certify the universal argument. Independent replay, external review and formal verification remain false.

entries.title: Compatible simple affine-pencil determinant poles contribute complete critical groups and extend the zero reciprocal-Hessian obstruction beyond blocked poles
entries.scope: Over C in n>=1 variables use the affine-quadratic setup A=A^T invertible, B=B^T, T=A^(-1)B, h=q_A+H(q_B+2v^T A x+c), p=Hprime of degree m>=1, and P,x(s),R,F,W from JF0. Suppose F is not identically zero, W=O(s^(-2)) at infinity, and every root alpha of P is either blocked (its affine stationary equation is inconsistent and W is regular there), or simple stationary (Pprime(alpha)!=0 and that equation is consistent). If all native critical points are Morse, the complete critical set is finite and nonempty and sum_Crit(h) 1/det Hess h=0. Consequently no polynomial source automorphism makes h have nonzero constant Hessian determinant. At a compatible simple root put lambda=-1/alpha and R0=R(alpha), which is regular. The full stationary set has g=R0+lambda y^2 on its one-dimensional nondegenerate eigenline. Morse critical points force F(alpha)!=0 and every root r of p(r)=alpha to be simple and different from R0. The pole contributes exactly 2m critical points, two for each r, with original-coordinate determinant J=2^n det(A)*2(r-R0)pprime(r)Pprime(alpha). Partial fractions of 1/(p(z)-alpha) give the complete group identity sum_group 1/J=1/[2^n det(A)Pprime(alpha)F(alpha)], exactly the coefficient of W at that pole divided by 2^n det(A). Regular F roots have the retained JF0 weights, and blocked roots contribute neither finite source points nor poles. Complete partial fractions and the literal infinity decay prove the zero sum, while a unit-Hessian source orbit would make every native determinant one common nonzero C and give N/C!=0. No singular critical point is discarded, no pole is counted as just one source point, and no multivariate Euler-Jacobi theorem or properness is imported. Compatible multiple poles are not automatically covered: the exact centered Jordan control W=1/[s(1+s)^2] has residue -1 at s=-1 but no finite critical point there. The theorem is a sufficient complete boundary certificate, not a classification of every failed certificate.

entries.title: Nondegenerate proper Krylov spaces exclude noncyclic affine source orbits; every invertible simple-spectrum pencil is excluded for every affine offset and nonlinear outer degree
entries.scope: In the JF/JH affine-quadratic setup over C in n>=1 variables assume T invertible, K=span(v,Tv,...,T^(n-1)v) has nondegenerate restricted A-pairing (including K=0), and every inactive primary space is semisimple. Active means its eigenvalue occurs on K. Write l_lambda for multiplicity on K, k_lambda for multiplicity on the whole source, and m=deg Hprime>=1. If m(l_lambda+1)>=k_lambda at every active eigenvalue, no polynomial source automorphism makes q_A+H(g) have unit Hessian. K and K-perp are invariant actual constant orthogonal summands. The vector v is cyclic on K, so its primary top pairings give exact R pole order l_lambda+1 and singular stationarity is inconsistent already on K; the stated inequality makes W regular at all active roots. An inactive repeated semisimple primary gives a nonempty positive-dimensional critical quadric at a root of Hprime(r)=-1/lambda, directly forbidding unit Hessian without needing other active bounds. If all inactive primaries are simple, JH0 counts their entire finite critical groups. Invertibility makes R bounded at infinity and W=O(s^(-n-1)). Thus the argument covers proper noncyclic K and even v=0, and does not require the scalar A(v,v) to be nonzero. In particular for every invertible simple-spectrum T the hypotheses hold for every v,c and every deg H>=2: K is the orthogonal sum of marked nondegenerate eigenlines, active l=k=1, and inactive roots are simple. No generic-offset qualification remains. If all native critical points are Morse in this simple-spectrum case, their complete count is N=1+2mn. For semisimple T the pairing condition means every nonzero v_lambda has A(v_lambda,v_lambda)!=0, and the active bound is 2(deg H-1)>=k_lambda. In four variables every deg H>=3 meets the bound; every nonlinear H meets it when active multiplicities are at most two. For actual graphs X=P0(g) in nondegenerate Q=q_A+a0 X^2+b0 X+c0, a0!=0 and P0 nonconstant, H=a0 P0^2+b0 P0+c0 has degree 2 deg P0>=2 and every closed parameterization factors by a source automorphism. The simple-spectrum exclusion therefore covers every nonconstant graph/source degree and every affine offset, with certified quadratic-similitude and literal original Meng-Yang transfer. Degenerate Krylov spaces, inactive nonsemisimple primaries, uncovered active multiplicities and singular-pencil infinity cases are not silently admitted. The present JH nonexistence theorem and its exact sufficient conditions remain unchanged; its remaining-family wording is historical within this now inverse-closed semisimple branch. Singular pencils and nonsemisimple boundaries are not declared resolved, and JI does not assert that all its unit-Hessian source orbits are empty. entries.scope: On actual C[x,y,z,w],let q=xy+zw,k=yz-qw and D(y)=0,D(z)=-qy,D(w)=-y^2,D(x)=yz+qw. The commuting triangular root actions with coefficients y,q prove D locally nilpotent;its coefficient gcd is1 and all first jets vanish at the unique Morse point of q,whose Hessian determinant is1. The exact chart R_y=C[y,y^-1,q,k,w] and independence of q,k modulo y remove every possible y denominator,proving actual embedded ker D=C[y,q,k]. Slice identities D(-w)=y^2,D(-qx-z^2)=qk give V(pl D) inside two quotient lines. Both open lines y=k=0,q!=0 and y=q=0,k!=0 are missing from the quotient image,while local slices reach every point off the plinth. Hence sqrt(pl D)=(y,qk)=(y,k) intersect (y,q). The horizontal component is contained in q=0,so fixed finite cylindrical support fails. After inverting q,pl D=(y,k),using D(-z/q)=y. Every q!=0 fibre has a free action and the actual ideal fibre has length1;globally qk lies in the plinth but k does not,so its quotient has nonzero value torsion. B=C[y,k] is not a source coordinate plane:its y=0,k=lambda!=0 fibre is Gm times A1 with a nonconstant unit. Its differential has rank1 at the Morse point. Thus primitive Morse preservation plus polynomial kernel and even generic minimum length does not force a nonzero linear action,normal transversality or coordinate recovery. This actual control does not meet KF fixed-support hypotheses,does not disprove minimum length under them,and does not settle the universal quadratic endpoint;the native quadric itself already has an invertible gradient.

entries.title: Every C1 real seed on a connected positive smooth source has a uniformly positive interior pushforward lower bound
entries.scope: Let M be a connected smooth manifold without boundary of positive dimension,with continuous strictly positive volume density,and h:M->R nonconstant C1. entries.title: The full Keller normalization has a free boundary class group and an exact nonzero nontorsion canonical ramification vector
entries.scope: For every complex polynomial Keller map K:A^n to A^n,n>=1,let Z be the finite normalization of the target B in the FULL source field L. Integral elements lie in the normal source polynomial ring,and the canonical source lift is a birational Zariski-Main open immersion. For the omitted boundary prime divisors D_i,the retained KRP1 localization argument gives Cl(Z)=direct_sum Z[D_i]:factorial source makes all classes boundary-supported,and scalar source units make every putative boundary relation zero. This class-group statement is credited rather than claimed anew. The pulled-back target volume form has the tame codimension-one order e_D-1,proved by dt=e*a*u^(e-1)du+u^e da and separability of the tangential residue parameters. Thus [K_Z]=sum_i(e_i-1)[D_i],because K is etale on the actual source. Under nonautomorphy some coefficient is positive;otherwise retained purity and finite-etale affine simple connectedness give degree1 and the Keller inverse. Hence the canonical class is NONZERO and NONTORSION in its free boundary basis. The source open is not obtained by inverting one element or any finite list of elements of its normalization ring,as any such element would become a scalar source unit. The statement concerns the full source field or an intermediate field already supplied with an affine-space reconstruction open;it does NOT create such a model for an arbitrary intermediate field. It gives a necessary global obstruction,not a contradiction to the existence of a nontrivial canonical class.

entries.title: Every nontrivial embedded Keller intermediate field has a normalization with nontorsion Weil canonical class,without assuming any polynomial intermediate model
entries.scope: For a complex Keller map in ANY dimension and EVERY finite embedded intermediate field F=C(K) subset E subset L=C(z),let S_E normalize the target polynomial ring in E. Its effective ramification divisor R_E represents its Weil canonical class. If that class were torsion,m R_E=div(g) for some m>=1. Normal affine Hartogs makes g a regular integral element in S_E and hence a source polynomial. A source prime C dividing a nonconstant g maps to a ramified prime D over a target prime P,but the actual valuation tower has 1=e(C/P)=e(C/D)*e(D/P) with e(D/P)>1,impossible. Thus g is a scalar source unit,R_E=0,and retained purity plus complex affine simple connectedness force E=F. For E=L this gives the polynomial Keller inverse by retained denominator removal;for a proper E it excludes that intermediate field,not the entire L/F. This needs no monogenic presentation,no birational source lift to Z_E and no affine-space model for E. Factoriality is needed for KN0 free boundary coordinates,not for this torsion argument,which also works for a normal affine etale source with only scalar units. Finite Galois covers have torsion canonical ramification by uniform indices over each target prime,so this reproduces the already-retained KMFI1 Galois-intermediate exclusion;the new presentation target also includes nongalois covers with torsion canonical class. No root transitivity for every torsion-canonical external cover after Keller base change is asserted. Characteristic zero and the whole-source unit condition are essential.

entries.scope: For every complex Keller map,the following are equivalent:polynomial inverse;Tr_(L/F)(R) subset B;and a D_B-linear retraction R to B,where target Weyl partials act through the commuting polynomial Nambu derivations. Localizing any such retraction gives an F-linear functional on L,uniquely Tr(a*-) by separable trace duality. entries.title: Full factorial radial moments in the critical dimension force a positive-volume sphere diffeomorphism
entries.scope: Let M be a compact connected smooth d-manifold without boundary,with positive continuous volume density,and Z:M->C^q a C1 map,q>=2,satisfying the ENTIRE actual-conjugate moment law integral Z^alpha barZ^beta=delta_(alpha,beta)rho_|alpha| alpha!,rho0=1. Its compact pushforward is U(q)-invariant by the polarized moment kernel and polynomial approximation,and its support is exactly Z(M). For d<=2q-1,variable norm would force an open annulus in a lower-dimensional Lipschitz image,impossible. A nonzero tuple requires d>=2q-1. At critical d=2q-1,normR is constant,rho_m=R^(2m)/(q)_m,and Z pushes positive source volume to uniform sphere area. Any equal-dimensional C1 positive-volume-preserving map is a finite cover:at a rank-deficient point the image of an epsilon-ball has target mass o(epsilon^d),contradicting source mass>=c epsilon^d. Thus Z is a sphere covering,and since q>=2 it is one-sheeted and M is C1-diffeomorphic to S^(2q-1). No analogous conclusion in higher source dimension,for signed/holomorphic-only moments,or for q1 nontrivial circle covers. The theorem is an all-order geometric proof,not finite-sample inference.
